name: bluedog_AbleStretchUpgrade
title: Able stretch Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_Able_Engine
title: JA10-37-6 "Alpha" Liquid Engine
description: Primitive upper stage engine. Don't activate it in the atmosphere - the engine bell is optimized for vacuum performance. Neither the most powerful nor most efficient engine, but it's a start. Used on the Alpha upper stage for the Easton and Fenris rockets. Upgraded versions for use on early Daleth rockets/Alphastar are also available.

name: bluedog_AblestarUpgrade
title: Ablestar Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_ThorAble_Guidance
title: Alpha-AGU Guidance Unit
description: Guidance core for the Alpha upper stage as used on Fenris and Daleth rockets. Goes on top of the second stage tank.

name: bluedog_ThorAble_Tank
title: Alpha/Daleth 60-85 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: A slightly modified derivative of the Easton second stage, this lightweight 0.625m upper stage tank was borrowed for the Fenris-Alpha Rocket. The Fenris team promises they will return the tanks to the Easton team once they are done. In the meantime, this tank has integrated three-axis attitude control and a small monopropellant supply. A stretched version is unlockable for early Daleth upper stages.

name: bluedog_ThorDelta_Interstage
title: Alpha/Daleth-SIF 0.9375m Interstage Adapter
description: A 0.9375m to 0.625m interstage adapter/decoupler for the Fenris and Daleth rockets. Note that it decouples from the bottom, leaving a small section of the top part of the shroud attached to protect the engine.

name: bluedog_ATDA_Battery
title: Belle-BFB Battery Module
description: A large capacity battery unit for all your on orbit energy storage needs.

name: bluedog_ATDA_RCS
title: Belle-ADR Reaction Control System
description: This RCS system provides full 3 axis stabilization for spacecraft.

name: bluedog_ATDA_VHFAntenna
title: Belle-VAF VHF Antenna
description: This lightweight communications antenna provides omnidirectional coverage for relaying signals.

name: bluedog_Agena8096BUpgrade
title: Agena8096B Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_Agena8096CUpgrade
title: Agena8096C Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_AgenaBUpgrade
title: AgenaB Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_AgenaB_FairingBase_Ranger
title: Belle-RPF 0.9375m Fairing Base
description: This flared 0.9375m fairing base is custom made for the Burke probe series, but we're sure you'll be able to find other things to fit inside it.

name: bluedog_AgenaDUpgrade
title: AgenaD Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_AgenaD_FairingBase_LunarOrbiter
title: Belle-Codac 0.9375m Fairing Base
description: This flared 0.9375m fairing base is custom made for the Codac probe series, but we're sure you'll be able to find other things to fit inside it.

name: bluedog_AgenaHDAUpgrade
title: AgenaHDA Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_Agena_AInterstage
title: Belle-A 1.25m to 0.9375 Interstage
description: A 1.25m to 0.9375m adapter interstage for early Fenris/Belle launchers. Includes integrated solid retro motors in the aft skirt, for separating the previous stage.

name: bluedog_Agena_Avionics
title: Belle TRU Telemetry Response Unit
description: To ensure the standards of quality expected of Bluedog Design Bureau products, our engineers have developed this component for the Belle upper stage. A fully functioning autonomous command module, it allows an Belle stage to control itself for tasks such as disposal and spying on foreign powers. It has integrated batteries and a reaction wheel. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Add the Belle-IHSS Horizon Sensor Module to your craft to gain additional SAS modes.</color>

name: bluedog_Agena_Decoupler_LunarOrbiter
title: Belle-Codac 0.9375m Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A roughly 0.9375m payload separation mechanism specifically designed for the Codac probe series, providing room for the solar panels that fold under the main core platform.

name: bluedog_Agena_EngineMount
title: Belle 0.9375m Engine Mount
description: The engine mount for Belle upper stages. You can attach an equipment rack below for extra utility. Attach interstages to the bottom of the 0.9375m ring at the top of the part.

name: bluedog_Agena_EngineShroud
title: Belle-ESA Equipment Rack
description: Convert your Belle upper stage into a fully featured satellite bus with this equipment rack. It contains attitude control thrusters, monopropellant storage, and extra batteries. The sides of the truss section can also be fitted with solar panels, 'Nafuni' secondary engines, or even subsatellites, depending on the mission profile. Attach to the engine mount, and then place the engine inside.

name: bluedog_Agena_Engine_XLR81
title: Belle-RLX81 Liquid Fuel Engine Series
description: This flexible family of upper stage engines designed for the Belle upper stage / spacecraft family features a large number of unique features that differentiate it from other small vacuum engines. The use of a gas generator cycle over pressure fed means that the overall dry mass of the stage should be lighter, and the ISP grows significantly with each revision.

name: bluedog_Agena_EquipmentRack
title: Belle-ERD Equipment Rack
description: Convert your Belle upper stage into a fully featured satellite bus with this equipment rack. It contains attitude control thrusters, monopropellant storage, and extra batteries. The sides of the truss section can also be fitted with solar panels, 'Nafuni' secondary engines, or even subsatellites, depending on the mission profile. Attach to the engine mount, and then place the engine inside.

name: bluedog_Agena_HorizonSensor
title: Belle-IHSS Horizon Sensor Module
description: A small horizon scanner with a jettisonable fairing. Used as one unit on the Belle A and B upper stage tanks and used in pairs on the Belle D upper stage telemetry unit. On Belle D, each horizon sensor is 35 degrees apart from the center of the back face. Provides SAS modes.

name: bluedog_Agena_MultiPayloadAdapter
title: Belle-MPA Multiple Payload Adapter
description: Multiple payload adapter for the Belle upper stage. Build your first payload on the fairing base, and then attach this to the optional extra floating attach node on the fairing base. Decouple the bottom once the top payload is separated.

name: bluedog_Agena_RetroThrustModule
title: Belle-PSB Retro Thrust Module
description: This small vent valve can be used to vent your excess monopropellant to push an upper stage away from the payload.

name: bluedog_Agena_SLV3B_FairingBase
title: Bossart-PCR3B-FB 1.875m Adapter Fairing Base
description: 1.875m fairing base that integrates a 1.875m to 0.9375m structural adapter.

name: bluedog_Agena_SLV3B_Interstage
title: Bossart-PCR3B-SI 0.9375m Interstage
description: Half length 0.9375m interstage for the Bossart PCR-3B rocket.

name: bluedog_Agena_SOT_1p875m
title: Belle-SOT15 Strap On Tank
description: Lightweight strap-on tanks for the Belle upper stage. Attach using mini radial decouplers with crossfeed enabled in 8x symmetry and stage in pairs. These are designed to fit within a 1.875m fairing base.

name: bluedog_Agena_SOT_2p5m
title: Belle-SOT25 Strap On Tank
description: Lightweight strap-on tanks for the Belle upper stage. Attach using mini radial decouplers with crossfeed enabled in 6x symmetry and stage in pairs. These are designed to fit within a 2.5m fairing base.

name: bluedog_Agena_SOT_GuidanceArray
title: Belle-SOT-GA Guidance Array
description: This add-on guidance package for the Belle SOT provides additional communications and guidance support for the stage while on extended missions.

name: bluedog_Agena_SOT_SupportSkirt
title: Belle-SOT-SS Structural Support Skirt
description: This 1.875m fairing base ring mounts to the interstage node of a Belle engine mount, allowing 1.875m interstages to be used. An optional fairing base can also spawn from the bottom of the ring.

name: bluedog_Agena_StraightInterstage
title: Belle 0.9375 Interstage
description: A 0.9375m straight interstage for operational Fenris/Belle and Bossart/Belle launchers. Includes integrated solid retro motors in the aft skirt, for separating the previous stage.

name: bluedog_Agena_Subsat_Hitchhiker
title: Belle-P111 "Stowaway" Subsatellite
description: A small subsatellite designed to collect signals intelligence.

name: bluedog_Agena_Tank_Long
title: Belle-240BD Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Lightweight 0.9375m fuel tank for the Belle-B and D upper stage systems.

name: bluedog_Agena_Tank_Short
title: Belle-120A Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Lightweight 0.9375m fuel tank for the Belle-A upper stage system.

name: bluedog_Agena_UllageMotor
title: Belle-PSB Ullage Motor
description: This little solid motor is designed to be attached to the bottom of the Belle A and B equipment rack to provide ullage thrust. Attach one pair 180 degrees apart for each burn that is necessary for the flight profile

name: bluedog_Carrack_AgenaAdapter
title: Galleon/Belle 1.5m Adapter
description: Interstage adapter from 1.5m to 0.9375m. The bottom is slightly smaller than 1.5m, to allow placement inside fairings. Includes an optional long variant.

name: bluedog_Carrack_StraightAdapter
title: Galleon-L 1.5m Straight Adapter
description: 1.5m straight adapter for the Galleon rocket. Includes optional hardware for use as an interstage decoupler and/or a fairing base.

name: bluedog_Carrack_WideAdapter
title: Galleon-H 2.1m Wide Adapter
description: 2.1m flared adapter for the Galleon rocket. Includes optional hardware for use as an interstage decoupler and/or a fairing base.

name: bluedog_Corona_Heatshield
title: SG-RV3 Return Capsule Heatshield
description: A small heatshield to protect the Spyglass Return Capsule on reentry.

name: bluedog_Corona_Parachute
title: SG-RV2 Return Capsule Parachute
description: A small parachute for Spyglass Return Capsules. Makes you wonder if its possible to catch the capsule mid air... Includes a manually operated decoupler for separating the retro motor from the rest of the pod once the retro burn is accomplished.

name: bluedog_Corona_Pod
title: SG-RV1 Return Capsule Pod
description: Produced in direct competition with the crewed MOS space station, the Spyglass program takes the simpler approach of returning the film in these capsules for processing back on the ground instead of processing in an orbital laboratory. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: This pod has hibernation enabled by default in order to conserve power. Make sure to disable hibernation after separating from the mother craft in order to regain control.</color>

name: bluedog_Corona_Retro
title: SG-RV4 Return Capsule Retro Pack
description: A small retro pack to deorbit Spyglass Return Capsules.

name: bluedog_GATV_AcquisitionLight
title: Belle-TADL Acquisition Light
description: A small low profile flip out light, designed to assist in docking exercises.

name: bluedog_GATV_DockingPort
title: Belle-TAD Target Docking Port
description: This special docking port is designed to capture the Leo nose cone's docking mechanism. The simple mechanical connection won't even allow you to transfer resources, much less crew, but it will securely attach two vessels together, for berthing or travel.

name: bluedog_GATV_LBandAntenna
title: Belle-BA81 Command Antenna
description: This low bandwidth antenna extends to allow a Belle spacecraft to receive commands and transmit data.

name: bluedog_GATV_MMDetector
title: S-00M Micrometeroid Package
description: Our scientists think space might not be as empty as we once thought. This device contains three plates for measuring the impacts of 'micrometeoroids', the little pieces of debris and particles that travel through open vacuum at thousands of meters per second. Measuring the number of impacts gives us an idea of how dangerous an area of space may be for our ships. This variant is designed to be recovered and replaced by a Kerbal on EVA. Bringing home exposure packages would certainly help advance our materials science...

name: bluedog_GATV_MaterialsBay
title: Belle-LBTV SC-9375 Materials Bay
description: Cutting edge exposure laboratory containing several material packages. Cannot be transmitted, even for reduced science. Packages must be retrieved via Kerbal on EVA for return and analysis. Requires the S-00M Micrometeroid Package and N-00K Nuclear Emulsion Package parts to be on the vessel in order to produce science.

name: bluedog_GATV_NoseCone
title: Belle-RNRD Nose Cone
description: Nose cone halves for the Belle Target Vehicle.

name: bluedog_GATV_NuclearPackage
title: N-00K Nuclear Package
description: Our scientists want to study the radiation environment around Kerbin. Part of a suite of experiments designed to work together including the Belle-LBTV SC-9375 Materials Bay and S-00M Micrometeroid Package.

name: bluedog_GATV_RunningLight
title: Belle-RADL Running Light
description: Small running lights that can be used to help identify spacecraft in the inky darkness of space.

name: bluedog_GATV_SPS
title: Belle-ESPS-A "Nafuni" Secondary Propulsion System
description: Secondary engines for the Belle upper stage system. Attach to the node switch on the truss on the Belle-D for intended use. Unintended use is not covered under warranty, but is encouraged. Takes liquid fuel and oxidizer from the main tank, and contains a supplementary monopropellant supply for the posigrade thrusters.

name: bluedog_GATV_SPS_LFO
title: Belle-ESPS-B "Nafuni" Secondary Propulsion System
description: Alternate secondary engines for the Belle upper stage system, sacrificing the fine-tuning thruster for another pressure fed liquid engine. Attach to the node switch on the truss on the Belle-D for intended use. Unintended use is not covered under warranty, but is encouraged. Takes liquid fuel and oxidizer from the main tank, and contains a supplementary fuel supply.

name: bluedog_GATV_SPS_RCS
title: Belle-ESPS-C "Nafuni" Secondary Propulsion System
description: Alternate secondary engines for the Belle upper stage system, sacrificing the larger liquid engine for a second RCS thruster. Attach to the node switch on the truss on the Belle-D for intended use. Unintended use is not covered under warranty, but is encouraged. Contains a supplementary monopropellant supply for the posigrade thrusters.

name: bluedog_GATV_SpiralAntenna
title: Belle-LOA Spiral Antenna
description: This low bandwidth antenna extends to allow a Belle spacecraft to receive commands and transmit data.

name: bluedog_Keyhole_Camera_KH1
title: SG-1 "Bloodhound" Camera System
description: A rudimentary panoramic camera system for peaceful reconnaissance usage.

name: bluedog_Keyhole_Camera_KH4
title: SG-4 "Cerveza" Camera System
description: The SG-4 improves upon the SG-1 with a more advanced stereoscopic camera system.

name: bluedog_Keyhole_Camera_KH4B
title: SG-4B "Cerveza" Camera System
description: The SG-4B "Cerveza" camera system is similar in basic design to the SG-4 but is larger and achieves superior resolution.

name: bluedog_Keyhole_Camera_KH7
title: SG-7 "Gamble" Camera System
description: The SG-7 "Gamble" was a short-lived member of the Spyglass satellite series. It represents a significant improvement over the earlier "Bloodhound" in terms of resolution and reliability. Launched on the Muo-Belle launch vehicle.

name: bluedog_Keyhole_Camera_KH8
title: SG-8 "Gamble-3" Camera System
description: The SG-8 "Gamble-3" is the latest and greatest in Kerbin observation systems from Bluedog Design Bureau. Typically launched on the Prometheus 3B.

name: bluedog_Keyhole_DualAdapter
title: SG-DPA Dual Return Capsule Adapter
description: This dual adapter conveniently allows multiple Spyglass return capsules to be stacked on top of each other.

name: bluedog_Keyhole_OCV_KH7
title: SG-7 "Gamble" Orbital Control Vehicle
description: Control segment for the Spyglass-7 "Gamble" photographic reconnaissance satellite, featuring a batteries, fuel, attitude control thrusters and orbital manuevering thrusters for adjusting the satellite's orbit. The SG-7 series is unique among the Belle-based Spyglass satellites in that it separated from the upper stage after reaching orbit, thus requiring this control vehicle.

name: bluedog_Keyhole_RVAdapter
title: SG-RCA 0.9375m to 0.625m Adapter
description: A 0.9375m to 0.625m adapter typically used to attach a Spyglass Recovery Capsule to the larger 0.9375m diameter camera systems.

name: bluedog_Oscar1
title: HAMSAT 1 Radio Communications Package
description: A small, extremely rudimentary radio transmitter built by civilians designed to be launched on the aft equipment shroud of the Belle-B. Has a small internal power supply.

name: bluedog_Strawman_Bus
title: P770 "Scarecrow" Satellite Bus Fairing
description: The P770 "Scarecrow" Bus is intended to push Belle-based satellites' life and capabilities to their full potential. Not only does this bus expand the Belle's profile from 0.9375m to 1.25m, it also introduces redundant systems, intregated batteries, a built-in fairing, and a new state-of-the-art solid-state data recording system. This sytem is  While intended to be a platform for singals intelligence reconnaissance collection, this bus can be used for any number of applications with the Belle upper stage and beyond.

name: bluedog_Strawman_Harvester
title: P770 "Harvester" High-Band Antenna
description: The Harvester antenna serves as an optional upgrade/addition to the SIGINT data collection package of the later P770 "Scarecrow" satellites, but it can also function as a relay antenna in its own right. Once added to the Thresher/Reaper system, this part boosts the SIGINT data output. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: THE THRESHER AND REAPER PARTS ARE REQUIRED FOR THIS EXPERIMENT TO FUNCTION. </color>

name: bluedog_Strawman_Harvester_Standalone_Antenna
title: P770 "Harvester Lite" High-Band Antenna
description: A repurposed antenna from a P770 "Scarecrow" satellite. Originally meant for signals collection, this antenna has been stripped of all its SIGINT hardware and now only functions as a small, compact, deployable relay antenna.

name: bluedog_Strawman_Reaper
title: P770 "Reaper" Helical Antenna Array
description: A nest of several helical antennas designed to work in tandem for receiving signals. While it can function as a normal relay antenna, it is designed to be a part of the SIGINT data collection package in the P770 "Scarecrow" series of satellite.

name: bluedog_Strawman_Solar
title: P770 Belle Solar Panel
description: A folding solar panel designed to fit in the Belle-ERD equipment rack for the P770 "Scarecrow" series of satellites. Does not track the sun.

name: bluedog_Strawman_Starfish_Big_Antenna
title: P770 "Starfish" Relay Antenna
description: A compact-folding large antenna with relay capabilities. While it is designed to be used in the SIGINT data collection package for the P770 "Scarecrow" series of satellite, it can be repurposed as a general relay.

name: bluedog_Strawman_Starfish_Small_Antenna
title: P770 "Starfish Lite" Relay Antenna
description: The smaller twin of the P770 "Starfish" relay antenna. While it is designed to be used in the SIGINT data collection package for the P770 "Scarecrow" series of satellite, it can be repurposed as a general relay.

name: bluedog_Strawman_Thresher
title: P770 "Thresher" SIGINT Collection System
description: The core of the P770 "Scarecrow" satellite series' signals intelligence experiments, the Thresher system is able to pick out signals and determine their source with extreme accuracy. Designed to be used the other parts of the Scarecrow's SIGINT data collection package. Also includes two built-in spiral antennas. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: THE REAPER HELICAL ANTENNA ARRAY IS REQUIRED FOR THIS EXPERIMENT TO FUNCTION.</color>

name: bluedog_Strawman_Thresher_Antenna
title: P770 Telemetry Antenna
description: A small deployable telemetry antenna designed for the P770 "Scarecrow" satellite series.

name: bluedog_Titan3B_Interstage
title: Prometheus-IIIB 1.875m Adapter Interstage
description: Interstage Adapter designed to attach the Belle upper stage to the Prometheus III-B (23B and 24B variants)

name: bluedog_ALSEP_ALSD
title: BDSEP-SMSD Surface Drill
description: Crew operated, surface deployed drilling expermiment. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal, then run by a scientist.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_ActiveSeismic
title: BDSEP-STOKE Active Seismic Experiment
description: A small, crew-deployed mortar with explosive charges for triggering seismic events. Should not be used when personnel are nearby. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_CPLEE
title: BDSEP-C3PL Cosmic Ray Detector
description: Ground-deployed instrument package used for measuring the spectral data of charged particles striking the body's surface. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_FROST
title: BDSEP-FROST Farside Radio Observing Scanning Telescope
description: Similar to ultraviolet rays, cosmic radio rays are hampered by our atmosphere. By placing one (or an array of several, if you want to be accurate) on the far side of another body, our planet's radio transmissions would be shielded and cosmic radio sources made far easier to detect. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_Gnomon
title: BDSEP-GNOME Color Reference Gnomon
description: Small gnomon with color references, used for correcting and analyzing photos on return. Provides no functionality, but is a nice addition to our EVA photos. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_Gravimeter
title: BDSEP-AGD Advanced Gravioli Detector
description: Following demonstrations of the existence of gravioli particles, our scientists were desperate to obtain more data of this phenomena. The AGD contains a new and improved version of the original gravioli detector, intended for use as a long term, ground-deployed monitoring station. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_Hadley
title: BDSEP-JMK "Kadley" Observation Telescope
description: Compact telescope made with 3D printed parts. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal. Run the experiment and collect the data via the PAW post deployment. Does not require an Experiment Control Station.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_HeatFlow
title: BDSEP-THRMSTAT Heat Flow Experiment
description: This control station contains a pair of heat probes which must be inserted into the soil. Once emplaced, they allow gradient measurements to be taken, allowing scientists to inference the geothermal temperatures and activity. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_LRRR
title: BDSEP-LRA Laser Ranging Retro Reflector
description: This retro-reflector assembly allows the distance between Kerbin and the Mun to be measured down to the centimeter - very important for calculating mileage on kerbonaut's expense reports. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_LargeSolar
title: BDSEP-LSA Large Solar Array
description: Larger science stations require more power than RTGs can provide. For setups located in the lunar day, one or more of these panels can be erected to provide power for a BDSEP station. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_MEME
title: BDSEP-MEME Munar Ejecta and Meteorites Experiment
description: The cratered surface of Kerbin's closest moon is the result of thousands of asteroid and meteoroid impacts. While a large impact would likely destroy the experiment, smaller micro particles can be detected. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_Magnetometer
title: BDSEP-3MTM Tri-Axis Magnetometer
description: The loss of numerous tools, samples, and knick-knacks on previous missions made the inclusion of a magnetometer an essential piece of the BDSEP kit. Able to measure the magnetic field in all three dimensions, our days of raiding the supply closets will soon be gone! Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_PassiveSeismic
title: BDSEP-PSE Passive Seismic Experiment
description: A small, self contained seismic monitoring station meant to be deployed by crew. Includes its own solar panels, though they're only enough to power the station itself. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_Penetrometer
title: BDSEP-LSRP Penetrometer
description: Crew operated, surface deployed penetrometer, for testing mechanical properties of soil. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal, then run by a scientist.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_SBandAntenna
title: BDSEP-COM-16S S-Band Antenna
description: The advantage of setting up semi-permanent science stations on other bodies is the tremendous amount of data they can return. However, sending that data back to KSC requires large amounts of bandwidth. The solution is the COM-16S combination transmission dish and MP3 player, available in stylish gold. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_SEP
title: BDSEP-S3P Surface Electrical Properties Experiment
description: Ground-deployed instrument package used for electrical conduction properties of the body's surface. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal. AUTHOR'S NOTE: In real life, this was paired with the SEP experiment antenna on the rover.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_SWC
title: BDSEP-SWC Solar Wind Composition Experiment
description: This foil sheet is designed to capture solar wind particles. Once returned back to the lab, they can be analyzed to determine their composition and properties. Also useable as an emergency blanket if required. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal. Run the experiment and collect the sample via the PAW post deployment. Does not require an Experiment Control Station.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_SampleContainer
title: BDSEP-CH1S7 Sample Storage Container
description: A secure stowable container for storing core samples, shiny rocks, or detailed descriptions of your local surroudings. Deploy via a kerbal's inventory, store your science results, and pick it up again to stow back in a craft's inventory. Any science reports stored within will remain even when the part is stored.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_SolarWind
title: BDSEP-R2D4 Solar Wind Experiment
description: This peculiar little box contains instruments for measuring the solar wind emanating from Kerbol. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_TVCamera
title: BDSEP-TVO SSTV Camera
description: 10 frames per second of grayscale goodness, broadcast at an ear-shrieking rate to the excited people back home. Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_ALSEP_UVTelescope
title: BDSEP-UBT Ultra Violet Telescope
description: Kerbin's atmosphere, while protecting us from solar radiation, also blocks out many spectra that would be useful for astronomy. The ground stations we've been establishing on other bodies are a great opporunity to set up an ultra violet telescope outside the atmosphere.  Must be brought in cargo storage and deployed on the surface by a kerbal.

name: bluedog_Apollo_AARDV_Antenna
title: Kanaloa-AARDV-SBA Omni Antenna
description: A small omnidirectional antenna for sending and receiving commands from autonomous vehicles, such as the AARDV.

name: bluedog_Apollo_AARDV_Cargo_Block1
title: Kanaloa-AARDV-CRM Cargo Resupply Module
description: As the lifetime of stations increased from months to years, it became impossible to rely solely on supplies brought up using the limited space inside Kane-11 capsules. The previous first generation ships that had supplied MOS stations could not bring the large volumes of supplies that were needed for sustained operations. This is the cargo volume for the Kanaloa Block I automated resupply ship, the standardized second generation cargo vessel. Note that it only serves as an ore carrier by default, unless fascinating ideas such as 'life support' or 'advanced science systems' have been discovered...

name: bluedog_Apollo_AARDV_Cargo_Block2
title: Kanaloa-AARDV-CRM2 Cargo Resupply Module
description: As the lifetime of stations increased from months to years, it became impossible to rely solely on supplies brought up using the limited space inside Kane-11 capsules. The previous first generation ships that had supplied MOS stations could not bring the large volumes of supplies that were needed for sustained operations. This is the cargo volume for the Kanaloa Block I automated resupply ship, the standardized second generation cargo vessel. Note that it only serves as an ore carrier by default, unless fascinating ideas such as 'life support' or 'advanced science systems' have been discovered...

name: bluedog_Apollo_AARDV_Core
title: Kanaloa-AARDV-CACB Control Block
description: 2.5m inline control core for Kanaloa AARDV systems. Goes between the cargo module and service module, and provides control and guidance for resupply vehicles and tugs.

name: bluedog_Apollo_AARDV_Nose
title: Kanaloa-AARDV-FNA Nose Adapter
description: Small cone to adapt the Kanaloa-CRM's 0.9375m top node to the 0.625m Kane Docking Mechanism.

name: bluedog_Apollo_AARDV_Plate
title: Kanaloa-AARDV-FPA Adapter
description: A nearly flat 2.5m plate, for adapting the top of the AARDV cargo module to the docking nose.

name: bluedog_Apollo_AARDV_UnpressurizedCargo
title: Kanaloa-AARDV-UCS Unpressurized Cargo Segment
description: This 2.5m unpressurized bay is useful for bringing up things such as small station segments, satellites, supplies, and parts ready to be attached to the outside of something.

name: bluedog_Apollo_APAS75
title: Octans 75-A Androgynous Docking Port
manufacturer: Bluedog Design Bureau and Tantares Space Technologies
description: Adapters suck, this revelation led to a collaborative, international effort to develop a docking port that can dock with any other docking port of the same type. Male or female be damned. The guide plates will help alignment on approach, these can then be retracted to allow a hard docking. <#ef7b06>AUTHOR'S NOTE: THIS PORT CAN ALSO BE USED WITH THE TANTARES' OCTANS 75-S DOCKING PORT.</color>

name: bluedog_Apollo_ASTP_Antenna
title: Navalia-ASTP VHF-FM Antenna
description: A small, fixed VHF-FM whip antenna for the Navalia-ASTP "Diplomat" Docking Module.

name: bluedog_Apollo_ASTP_DockingAdapter
title: Navalia-ASTP "Diplomat" Docking Module
description: A specialized module designed to allow the docking of two separate spacecraft to either end of this module. In addition to mating spacecraft, it provides additional living/working space, as well as a platform for experiments. Can accommodate two crew at a time.

name: bluedog_Apollo_ASTP_UltravioletExperiment
title: Navalia-ASTP MA-059 UV Absorbtion Experiment
description: This experiment is a modified and slightly enhanced version of the Far Ultraviolet Spectrometer. This experiment can be used to study measure emissions from celestial bodies, zodiacal light, solar atmosphere emissions, stellar emissions, and galactic emissions.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block1_Nose
title: Kane Nose Cone
description: In early versions of the Kane capsule, the docking port was omitted because there were no plans to rendezvous and dock during a mission. This structural nose cone was placed on top instead. It is capable of interfacing with the Kane LES tower in the same way a docking port would.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block2_SM
title: Kane-11-MSM Service Module
description: A complete package of fuel, monoprop, batteries, fuel cells, and storage bays for your service module. The fuel cells are powered by monopropellant. Designed to circularize around the Mun with a lander in tow, and then return home to Kerbin. Engine, RCS quads, communications, docking light, and decoupler sold separately.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block2_SPS
title: Kane-11-SE60 Service Propulsion System
description: This massive service engine sacrifices much of its power to eliminate weight. The result is a very light, though not extremely efficient, propulsion system for large orbiters in the 2.5m size class and up.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block2_highGain
title: Kane-11-CDA High Gain Antenna
description: A collapsible relay antenna consisting of four high gain dishes, for transmitting the many exciting things you've discovered. Intended to be placed on the mounting bracket of the Kane-11 engine plate.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block3_MissionModule
title: Kane-11-8OMM Orbital Mission Module
description: The Kane-11's adaption to the Block III+ configuration resulted in an extremely cramped and uncomfortable capsule for the crew. While it was acceptable for short durations such as during takeoff and landing, any amount of time longer than an hour or so required a larger habitable volume. This mission module is essentially several more cubic meters of living space for the crew. Place it upside down in place of the lunar module, with docking ports on each end. Extract with the CSM after circularization.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block3_SM
title: Kane-11-3OSM Service Module
description: Similar to the Kane-11-MSM service module, the 13 variant includes a sufficient supply of fuel, monoprop, and large batteries storage for LKO missions. Complexity is reduced by simply packing batteries instead of fuel cells. Missions beyond LKO may void warranty. Engine, RCS quads, communication, lights and decoupler still not included. Allegations that a trash compactor is a key manufacturing component are entirely unfounded.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block3_highGain
title: Kane-11-CDA33 High Gain Antenna
description: A collapsible relay antenna consisting of a high gain dish, for transmitting the many exciting things you've discovered. Intended to be placed on the mounting bracket of the Kane-11 engine plate.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block4_MissionModule
title: Kane-11-12OMM Orbital Mission Module
description: Following the introduction of more capable lifters for crewed LKO missions, the venerable Kane Block III+ mission module was replaced with a larger can. Includes a larger attachment node on top for using larger androgynous docking ports. Place it upside down in place of the lunar module, with docking ports on each end. Extract with the CSM after circularization.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block5_SolarPanel
title: Kane-11-PPA Deployable Solar Panels
description: While previous Kane-11 ships had relied on fuel cells or batteries to provide power, the longer duration missions demanded of the Block V meant that bringing enough consumables was impractical. These solar panels are fixed to the bottom of the engine mount, providing lightweight sustainable power for as long as needed.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Block5_highGain
title: Kane-11-CDA55 High Gain Antenna
description: A collapsible relay antenna consisting of a high gain dish, for transmitting the many exciting things you've discovered. Intended to be placed on the mounting bracket of the Kane-11 service engine.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Boilerplate
title: Kane-SABP1 Command Pod Boilerplate
description: This "boilerplate" is designed to simulate the Kane-11-3 Command Pod in mass, shape, and more. This boilerplate capsule holds no crew and is intended for test flights to prove and certify the Kane's design before the capsule is used. Perfect for orbital flights, suborbital flights, and other types of test flights. Can be used with parachutes for drop testing. Includes probe control, minor SAS control, batteries, and a built-in direct antenna. However, this boilerplate does not include a real heatshield and as such is not intended to survive orbital reentry. Intended to be used with the Kane-SA-MSM Service Module Boilerplate.

name: bluedog_Apollo_CADS_active
title: CADS 1.25m Docking Port (Active)
description: Common Androgynous Docking Port. Developed to eliminate the limitations of the gendered Kane docking system, as well as provide a larger passageway for delivering cargo. Equipped with a deployable capture ring to dampen impact. Permanent station ports can use the passive version, which is simpler and lighter.

name: bluedog_Apollo_CADS_passive
title: CADS 1.25m Docking Port (Passive)
description: Common Androgynous Docking System, passive version intended to mate with active counterparts. Useful for permanent fixtures that won't have to form the active docking partner, such as berthing ports on station modules.

name: bluedog_Apollo_ConeDockingPort
title: Kane-11-DDM6 0.625m Passive Docking Mechanism
description: Advanced probe-and-drogue docking system. It possesses the smallest crew tube possible for Kerbals (their heads would get stuck if it were any smaller) to fit inside a 0.625m form factor. It would probably be better to have a larger passageway on cargo flights. This is the passive port, designed to catch the active port's probe.

name: bluedog_Apollo_CrewPod
title: Kane-11-3 Command Pod
description: Despite a... questionable track record during testing, this capsule is perhaps the pinnacle of our manned design program. While the Hermes and the Leo were essentially test vehicles, the Kane (pronounced 'khan-ay') is a real operational craft. Includes attitude control thrusters for reentry. Originally developed to be the orbiter segment of our Munar landing operations, a variety of upgrades and specialized components are being developed, and should become available in the near future.

name: bluedog_Apollo_CrewPod_5crew
title: Kane-11-5 Advanced Command Pod
description: By optimizing the internal volume and modifying the crew arrangement, we have managed to cram 5 Kerbals into the reentry vehicle for the Kane-11. They only will be comfortable in there for a short time, so be sure to bring some sort of extra habitable volume to dock with after you've achieved orbit.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Decoupler
title: Kane-11 2.5m Capsule Decoupler
description: This decoupler is designed to sit between a capsule's heatshield, and the service module. It includes an umbilical to connect the capsule to the service module's systems. The decoupler automatically maps to the abort action group in case of a failure of the launch stack.

name: bluedog_Apollo_DockingSpotlight
title: Kane-11-FBL Docking Floodlight
description: Essentially a pen light glued to a flap, this light (traditionally mounted to the decoupler ring on the Kane-11 CSM) swings out to provide illumination for docking/berthing operations.

name: bluedog_Apollo_DopplerAntenna
title: Kane-APA-18 VHF Doppler Tracking Experiment
description: This VHF antenna is specifically calibrated to use doppler tracking to detect and measure localized gravitational anomalies. Includes a conformal variant that is intended to conform to the exterior of the Kane service module as well as a flat variant. Can also be used as a basic relay antenna.

name: bluedog_Apollo_DrogueChute
title: Kane-11 Drogue Parachute
description: Drogue parachute for the Kane-11 Command Pod. Attach to the node in the nose section.

name: bluedog_Apollo_EVAFloodlight
title: Kane-11-LIB EVA Floodlight
description: Essentially a pen light on the end of a straw, this light (traditionally mounted to the decoupler ring on the Kane-11 CSM) swings out to provide illumination to aid kerbonauts on EVAs.

name: bluedog_Apollo_EngineMount
title: Kane-11-EMT 2.5m Engine Mount
description: Mounting plate for attaching a single engine to 2.5m tanks. Includes a node just below the top rim for attaching the Sarnus LAM as well as a mounting point for the high gain antenna system.

name: bluedog_Apollo_Feetshield
title: Kane-11-RFHS 2.5m Advanced Heat Shield
description: Advanced heatshield for the Kane-11 to enable safe land recovery of the capsule. Includes deployable impact attenuating legs, as well as retro solids for cutting speed during the terminal part of the descent. Parachutes still required (and sold separately).

name: bluedog_Apollo_Heatshield
title: Kane-11-MSHS 2.5m Heat Shield
description: Large 2.5m structural heatshield for Kane CSM. It is very thick in order to withstand the intense heat of munar reentries. Remove some of the ablator for Kerbin orbital missions, to save weight. The structure itself is lighter as well, at the cost of removing the jettison hardware. Make sure your parachutes can stop the weight of the capsule and the heatshield.

name: bluedog_Apollo_LES
title: Kane-11-LES PEBKAC Launch Escape System
description: The main thrust structure and escape engine for the PEBKAC Launch Escape System. Stage to jettison. For best results jettison high in (or out of) the atmosphere, usually around first stage cut off. After firing during an emergency abort, canards deploy to flip the capsule retrograde for parachutes. Automatically added to the abort action group. Autostrut to heaviest part to stop wobbling.

name: bluedog_Apollo_MainChute
title: Kane-11 Main Parachute
description: Main parachute for the Kane-11 Command Pod. Attach to the node in the nose section.

name: bluedog_Apollo_ParachuteCover
title: Kane-11-PMX3 1.25m Parachute Cover
description: Structural cover for Kane parachutes. Place on top of the capsule after adding the main and drogue parachutes. The Active Docking Mechanism goes on top. Includes a decoupler to clear the way for the parachutes.

name: bluedog_Apollo_ProbeDockingPort
title: Kane-11-DPM6 0.625m Active Docking Mechanism
description: Advanced probe-and-drogue docking system. It possesses the smallest crew tube possible for Kerbals (their heads would get stuck if it were any smaller) crammed inside a 0.625m form factor. It would probably be better to have a larger passageway on cargo flights. Once soft docking is achieved and the vessels properly aligned, retract the probe to hard dock and establish a solid connection.

name: bluedog_Apollo_RCML
title: RKPV-L Renovated Lab Module
description: Refurbished pressure vessel from a Kane pod, combined with much of the support systems from a Kane service module. Intended to be used as an orbital lab module.

name: bluedog_Apollo_RCS_1X
title: Kane-ACT-1X Single RCS Thruster
description: This attitude and translation thruster pack was developed for the Kane program. This model includes multiple variants of single-direction thrusters.

name: bluedog_Apollo_RCS_2X
title: Kane-ACT-2X Dual RCS Thruster
description: This attitude and translation thruster pack was developed for the Kane program. This model includes multiple variants of two-way thrusters.

name: bluedog_Apollo_RCS_3X
title: Kane-ACT-3X Triple RCS Thruster
description: This attitude and translation thruster pack was developed for the Kane program. This model includes multiple variants of three-way thrusters.

name: bluedog_Apollo_RCS_4X
title: Kane-ACT-4X Quad RCS Thruster
description: This attitude and translation thruster pack was developed for the Kane program. This model includes multiple variants of four-way thrusters.

name: bluedog_Apollo_RCS_Engine
title: Kane-ACT-E RCS Engine
description: A Kane ACT thruster with a larger nozzle and higher pressure. Useful as a spacecraft OAMS system when used in groups.

name: bluedog_Apollo_RCS_EngineQuad
title: Kane-ACT4-E RCS Engine Thruster Quad
description: Developed for the Leo-B1G service module, this attitude and translation thruster pack also includes powerful fore and aft thrusters linked to engine controls. Engine thrust direction toggles via action group Custom10 by default.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIM_ATM
title: Kane-OCX Payload Bay Solar Telescope
description: The predecessor of the Kane-OCO Telescope Mount used on the Hokulani space staton, the Kane-OCX Payload Bay Solar Telescope carries multiple solar observation experiments. Tracks the sun upon deployment. Defnitely not an orbital cannon.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_GRS
title: Kane K-SBG160 Gamma Ray Spectrometer
description: This instrument can measure the composition of even very low concentration ambient gasses in space near celestial bodies.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_IR_radiometer
title: Kane K-SBIRR171 Scanning Infrared Radiometer
description: The Scanning Infrared Radiometer measures thermal emission from the surface of celestial bodies in order to obtain a high-resolution surface temperature map.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_MasSpec
title: Kane K-SBM165 Mass Spectrometer
description: Kerbals have always wondered the eternal question: If I take off my helmet outside the ship, will I be able to breathe? The answer lies here.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_PanoramicCamera
title: Kane SBC-163 Panoramic Camera
description: Camera system designed for wide field panoramic imaging.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_UVspectrometer
title: Kane K-SBU169 Far Ultraviolet Spectrometer
description: The Far Ultraviolet Spectrometer is a versatile instrument which can among other things measure emissions from celestial bodies, zodiacal light, solar atmosphere emissions, stellar emissions, and galactic emissions.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_alphaXraySpectrometer
title: Kane KSBXA-161-162 X-ray and Alpha particle spectrometer
description: This combo experiment is designed to detect X-ray fluorescence and alpha particles both in deep space and in orbit around planetary bodies.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_mappingCamera
title: Kane SBC166-175 Mapping Camera and Laser Altimeter
description: This advanced imaging system combines a photogrammetric mapping camera with a laser altimeter for detailed surveys of planetary bodies. A side facing stellar camera is also built in for extra science!

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_radar
title: Kane KSB-CSAR209 Sounding Radar
description: This complex synthetic aperture radar system is capable of subsurface mapping, measuring galactic electromagnetic radiation around bodies, studying surface topography and even producing surface imaging.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_radarRecorder
title: Kane KSBRR-209 Radar Optical Recording Unit
description: This device was designed to record synthetic aperture radar data in an optical format on photographic film. We've adapted it to record other forms of scientific data as well.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_subSatellite
title: Kane-PFS "Sjogren" Subsatellite Core
description: This tiny satellite is meant to be carried in the service bay of a Kane-11 CSM, and ejected before return to Kerbin. Despite its small size it packs both a magnetometer boom (accompanied by two counterweight booms) and a charged particle detector. Use the K-MA1L Subsatellite Dispenser to store inside the Kane science bay.

name: bluedog_Apollo_SIMbay_subSatellite_dispenser
title: Kane K-MA1L Subsatellite Dispenser
description: Compact letterbox shaped dispenser to safely hold the K-MA1L subsatellite until its ready to deploy.

name: bluedog_Apollo_ScimitarAntenna
title: WPT Scimitar Antenna
description: This interesting device is known as a scimitar antenna. It is a curved antenna inside of an aerodynamic casing allowing it used while travelling though the atmosphere or as backup to a high gain antenna. And we think it looks cool. Place in 2x symmetry on the Kane Service Module.

name: bluedog_Apollo_VHFantenna
title: Kane-17-YG VHF Yagi Antenna
description: A folding Yagi antenna designed to enhance gathering of VHF radar sounding data. Can be used for communications in a pinch. Attach to the node on the Kane engine mount just under the science bay.

name: bluedog_Apollo_dipoleAntenna
title: Kane-17-DP HF Dipole Radar Antenna
description: An extending dipole antenna used to gather high frequency radar sounding data. Can be used as a communications antenna in a pinch. Attach in a pair to the nodes on the Kane engine plate.

name: bluedog_EarlyLunarShelter
title: Sina-EMSS-3 Surface Shelter Module
description: Longer surface stays require facilities and consumables beyond what can be carried in a single MLEM lander. This is a dedicated shelter module - while it sacrifices the ascent propulsion system, it can sustain three crew members for up to a month on the surface. Includes surface communications, deployable insulation, and an expandable airlock - make sure your front leg does not have the "porch". Use the "truck" variant of the descent tank assembly for autonomous landing.

name: bluedog_EarlyLunarShelter_Telescope
title: Sina-EMSS-TOP Observational Telescope
description: A small telescope designed for ground-based optical observations on non-atmospheric bodies

name: bluedog_LM_Antenna_EVA
title: Sina-MLEM-WCT Whip Antenna
description: A small whip antenna, originally meant to provide a communications link between Kerbonauts on EVA, and their Sina MLEM lander.

name: bluedog_LM_Antenna_VHF
title: Sina-MEM-SSC VHF Antenna
description: A small VHF antenna, originally meant to provide a communications link between a Sina MEM lander and the Kane CSM in orbit.

name: bluedog_LM_Ascent_Cockpit
title: Sina-MLEM-ASC Ascent Stage Cockpit
description: The Sina Ascent Stage Cockpit provides accommodations for two Kerbals to ride to the Mun's surface atop the Sina Decent Stage, then return to orbit. Includes integrated fuel tanks, RCS, communications system, extended life batteries, and two hammocks. Put the ascent engine on the bottom, and the passive docking port on the top. Remember to have all crew members on board before launching.

name: bluedog_LM_Ascent_Engine
title: Sina-MLEM-APS Ascent Propulsion System
description: Derived from experience from our Belle engines, this non-gimballing liquid fueled engine prioritizes one thing: Reliability. Failure of the ascent engine could leave brave explorers trapped on the Mun.

name: bluedog_LM_CosmicRayDetector
title: Sina-MLEM-CRD Cosmic Ray Detector
description: A small experiment for detecting cosmic ray impacts.

name: bluedog_LM_Descent_Engine
title: Sina-MLEM-DPS Descent Propulsion System
description: A lightweight gimbaling liquid fueled engine designed to bring the Sina lander safely to the Mun's surface.

name: bluedog_LM_Descent_Leg
title: Sina-MLEM-LSG Landing Leg
description: A sturdy retracting landing leg, perfect for landing on other bodies.

name: bluedog_LM_Descent_Separator
title: Sina-MLEM-ADS Lander Separator
description: A set of guillotines and explosive bolts for connecting, and then separating, the ascent and descent stages of the MLEM.

name: bluedog_LM_Descent_Tanks
title: Sina-MLEM-DST Descent Stage Assembly
description: The Sina Descent Stage Assembly contains fuel tanks and recessed engine mounting point for the Sina MLEM. Ascent Cockpit sold separately. Engine attach node located inside the hole in the bottom. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: The SINA MEM is attached to the payload structure of the Lunar Adapter Base via a hidden node within the descent stage, not the bottom of the engine.</color>

name: bluedog_LM_Descent_Tanks_Truck
title: Sina-MLEM-TRK Autonomous Descent Stage Assembly
description: The Sina Truck Autonomous Descent Stage Assembly contains fuel tanks and recessed engine mounting point for the Sina MLEM, as well as probe core funcionally to enable autonomous landing. Used to deliver Sina Surface Shelter modules, or large rovers using the Payload Deployment Platform, to the surface. Engine attach node located inside the hole in the bottom. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: The SINA MEM is attached to the payload structure of the Lunar Adapter Base via a hidden node within the descent stage, not the bottom of the engine.</color>

name: bluedog_LM_DrillExperiment
title: Sina-MLEM-MDCD Core Sample Drill
description: Wireline-type core drill designed to be mounted to the side of the Sina descent stage. A hollow drill bit digs down into the ground, leaving an intact cylinder of substrate inside the shaft. These core samples are broken off at set intervals and retrieved with a small grabbing mechanism which is lowered into the shaft. This allows the drill to stay in place while subsequent cutting sections are added to increase the drill depth.

name: bluedog_LM_Goo
title: Sina-MLEM-MGC Mystery Goo Experiment
description: A recent procurement mistake has left us with too many RTG plutonium storage casks. In an effort to save funds, BDB's engineers have converted several to mystery goo observation systems. We were worried the residual radiation from the cask might damage the experiment, but the goo seems... happy.

name: bluedog_LM_Lab
title: Sina-MLEM-CSL Laboratory Module
description: Efforts to extend the uses of the Sina MLEM hardware have resulted in this retrofitted orbital laboratory module. Useful as a free-flight sortie lab (with a CSM) or even a station expansion module. Contains life support for two to three crew for up to thirty days, as well as monopropellant and batteries. Experiments provided separately.

name: bluedog_LM_Lab_Battery
title: Sina-MLEM-BCT Rechargeable Battery Pack
description: Large capacity batteries for modified MLEM crafts. Attaches behind the landing legs, on the descent stage.

name: bluedog_LM_Lab_Magnetometer
title: Sina-MLEM-MGS Magnetometer Boom
description: Folding triaxial magnetometer boom with dual detectors.

name: bluedog_LM_Lab_MaterialsBay
title: Sina-MLEM-MEP Material Experiment Palette
description: Fixed, surface attached version of the MESA. The MEP contains several different experiments designed to test basic principles of manufacturing in the Munar vacuum and low gravity, and the hardiness of certain materials when exposed to the space radiation environment. As a bonus, it also serves as an excellent way of collecting extra surface samples in the form of statically charged dust! It also has a well-placed television camera for observing those tremendous first few steps onto the surface of another world.

name: bluedog_LM_Lab_Micrometeoroid
title: Sina-MLEM-MMID Micrometeoroid Collector Panels
description: Deployable micrometeoroid collector panels for the Sina MLEM-Lab.

name: bluedog_LM_LunarFlyingVehicle
title: Lono-MFV-HOP "Icarus" Munar Flying Vehicle
description: The Munar Flying Vehicle was designed to greatly extend the range from the MLEM that a Kerbal can explore. Includes storage for ALSEP components, for remote deployment. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Store inside the Sina Descent Stage Assembly's inventory (requires manually placing in a slot), and deploy by placing on the surface with an engineer. After boarding, select "Control From Here" in the PAW to align forward vector with the engines.</color>

name: bluedog_LM_MESA
title: Sina-MLEM-MESA Material Experiment Stowage Assembly
description: The Material Experiment Stowage Assembly is a complete, semi-automated material science laboratory designed to be stowed in the MLEM. MESA contains several different experiments designed to test basic principles of manufacturing in the Munar vacuum and low gravity, and the hardiness of certain materials when exposed to the space radiation environment. As a bonus, it also serves as an excellent way of collecting extra surface samples in the form of statically charged dust! It also has a well-placed television camera for observing those tremendous first few steps onto the surface of another world.

name: bluedog_LM_Q3_Storage
title: Sina-MLEM-Q3S Cargo Module
description: Additional cargo capacity for the Sina MLEM, useful for surface experiments and rover components. Attaches to Q3, on the back-right of the descent stage. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: To balance the thrust on the MLEM when the MRV is attached, fill with the in-situ rover parts and select the "Rover Counterweight" CoM option. The "LM CoT" option is to not impart torque on a rover-less MLEM.</color>

name: bluedog_LM_RTG_Folding
title: Sina-MLEM-RHU2 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator Mount
description: Folding dual mount version of the PB-PANS-9 RTG. Used for upgraded munar missions that need to have keep-alive power and heat during the dormancy period of a long sortie.

name: bluedog_LM_RTG_Rack
title: Sina-MLEM-RHU4 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator Rack
description: Radial quad-mount version of the PB-PANS-9 RTG. Used for upgraded munar missions that need to have keep-alive power and heat during the dormancy period of a long sortie.

name: bluedog_LM_Radiator
title: Sina-MLEM-STR Deployable Radiator Panel
description: Managing the thermal loads during a full munar day-night cycle is one of the chief concerns for extending the surface stay of the MLEM system. The one goes on the second quadrant of the descent stage, and is deployed once the craft has landed.

name: bluedog_LM_SheLab
title: Sina-MSL "Bungalow" Shelter/Laboratory
description: Inspired by the fishing shacks north of the KSC, this shelter is designed to provide living and working space for two Kerbonauts for up to three months. Packed with consumables, a sample processing lab, and more. Connect the MTV deployment ramp to the node on the side - otherwise the robotics won't work. Use the "truck" variant of the descent tank assembly for autonomous landing.

name: bluedog_LM_SheLab_Spotlight
title: Sina-FL4 Mounted Floodlight
description: Large mounted floodlight, for illuminating the area around your munar base. Attach to landers as needed.

name: bluedog_LM_Shelter
title: Sina-MLEM-SHL Surface Shelter Module
description: Longer surface stays require facilities and consumables beyond what can be carried in a single MLEM lander. This is a dedicated shelter module - while it sacrifices the ascent propulsion system, it can sustain two crew members for up to a month on the surface. Includes surface communications, deployable insulation, and an expandable airlock - make sure your front leg does not have the "porch". Use the "truck" variant of the descent tank assembly for autonomous landing .

name: bluedog_LM_Taxi
title: Sina-MLEM-CRZY Taxi Ascent Stage
description: The Sina Taxi Ascent Stage Cockpit provides accommodations for up to three Kerbals to ride to the Mun's surface atop the Sina Decent Stage, perform an extended surface stay, then return to orbit. During surface operations, the Taxi is shut down and put in a dormant state to save resources, while the crew operates out of a separately landed shelter. Includes integrated fuel tanks, RCS, communications system, extended life batteries, radiators, and deployable insulation for the dormancy period. Put the ascent engine on the bottom, and the passive docking port on the top. Remember to have all crew members on board before launching.

name: bluedog_LM_Truck_Platform
title: Sina-MLEM-PDP Payload Deployment Platform
description: This platform is intended to be mounted on top of a MLEM-TRK Descent Stage. Includes extending ramps for deploying a rover to the munar surface. Rover design or parts not included.

name: bluedog_LM_Truck_RCS
title: Sina-MLEM-TRK 3-4/45 RCS Thruster
description: Modified version of the standard Kane and Sina RCS cluster, designed to be mounted on the MLEM-Truck to provide independent attitude control for autonomous landing. Includes 3x variant for clearance when using the Payload Platform.

name: bluedog_LRV_Base
title: Lono-MRV-HPB Central Chassis
description: Main building base of the MRV. Attach the front and aft chassis segments, along with two seats. The bottom side contains a node for attaching to the deployment mechanism. Make sure to deploy the low-gain antenna once the rover is safely on the surface.

name: bluedog_LRV_Base_Combined
title: Lono-MRV-HPB Full Chassis
description: Alternate version of the MRV chassis. Welding the front/aft frame sections prevents it from being stored on the MLEM, but means you won't have robotics-related bugs when driving around, switching crafts, etc. Use this if the "real" MRV is giving you problems, and cheat it to the surface (or send it down on a separate lander if you want).

name: bluedog_LRV_Gravimeter
title: Lono-MRV-LTG Traverse Gravimeter
description: Deployable surface gravimeter for the MRV. Place on the starboard side of the aft pallet. Must be detached and placed on the ground by a scientist to be activated.

name: bluedog_LRV_Hinge
title: Lono-MRV-HDM Deployment Hinge
description: Robotic hinge for deploying the MRV from stowage on board a lander.

name: bluedog_LRV_HingePlate_Aft
title: Lono-MRV-HPA Aft Chassis
description: Aft section of the MRV chassis. Attach wheels to the nodes, before retracting into the folded position. Once deployed, attach the aft pallet to the center node. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Don't lock this servo while the MRV is stowed.</color>

name: bluedog_LRV_HingePlate_Fore
title: Lono-MRV-HPF Forward Chassis
description: Front section of the MRV chassis. Attach wheels to the nodes, before retracting into the folded position. Once deployed, attach the front pallet to the center node. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Don't lock this servo while the MRV is stowed.</color>

name: bluedog_LRV_LawnChair
title: Lono-MRV-PSD Foldable Chair
description: Deck chair modified for use on the munar surface. Contains a small stowage bag under the seat. Unfold the seats after the rover has been deployed from the lander.

name: bluedog_LRV_Pallet_Aft
title: Lono-MRV-ASP Aft Pallet
description: Rear pallet for the MRV, attached once it has been unfolded and deployed on the surface. Primarily used as a structural component, contains mounting points for the tool carrier, traverse gravimeter, and SEP experiment antenna.

name: bluedog_LRV_Pallet_Front
title: Lono-MRV-FCEP Front Pallet
description: Front pallet for the MRV, attached once it has been unfolded and deployed on the surface. Contains the main batteries, protected solar panels, and the main communications computer. Mounting points for the high gain antenna and main camera are also provided.

name: bluedog_LRV_SEP_Antenna
title: Lono-MRV-SEA SEP Experiment Antenna
description: Science experiment designed to analyze the electrical properties of the local surface. Attaches to the node on top of the aft pallet.

name: bluedog_LRV_Slider
title: Lono-MRV-SDM Deployment Hinge
description: Robotic slider for deploying the MRV from stowage on board a lander.

name: bluedog_LRV_ToolCarrier
title: Lono-MRV-HTC Tool Carrier
description: Hand tool carrier meant to be attached to the MRV. Attach to the port node on the aft pallet. Unlocking the carrier will swing it outwards, so the tools on the back side can be accessed. Once it's unlocked, it can be placed on the ground. This accomplishes nothing, but it feels good.

name: bluedog_LRV_Wheel
title: Lono-MRV-WHL Rover Wheel
description: Wheel for the MRV. Attach to the four nodes on the front and aft chassis, without symmetry, and then retract for stowage. Contains individual variants for each wheel fender. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: It's recommended to remove this from the Gear action group to prevent premature deployment. Override and boost spring power for use at 1G.</color>

name: bluedog_LRV_highGain
title: Lono-MRV-HGA Communications Dish
description: Primary antenna for transmitting video, voice, and data from the MRV. Attaches to the port node on the front pallet.

name: bluedog_LRV_mainCamera
title: Lono-MRV-MTC Television Camera
description: Primary television camera of the MRV, for showing the folks at home all the cool rocks you've found. Attaches to the starboard node on the front pallet.

name: bluedog_LTV
title: Lono-MTV "Mun Mite" Chassis
description: Lightweight, single crew scout rover designed to be deployed with the Sina-MSL "Bungalow" shelter. Includes storage for experiments, solar panels for recharging, and a core sample drill for performing short to medium range geological expeditions.

name: bluedog_LTV_Ramp
title: Lono-MTV-DHM Deployment Ramp
description: Robotic hinge for deploying the MTV from the Sina-MSL "Bungalow" shelter. Once the ramp has been lowered, the railing on the shelter can be raised. Failure to do so will result in an investigation by the relevant workplace safety organizations.

name: bluedog_LittleJoe2_Algol
title: Little Jeb 2 "Persei-T" Solid Rocket Motor
description: Primary booster / sustainer motor for the Little Jeb 2. Used both as a first stage, as well as a sustainer stage when fired in series. Has straight (center) and canted (outboard) variants. Make sure they're properly angled.

name: bluedog_LittleJoe2_Body
title: Little Jeb 2 Body
description: Main structural module for the Little Jeb 2 test vehicle. Mount the specially prepared "Persei-T" and "Newby" motors in the 7 slots on the bottom. Includes cold-gas attitude thrusters, which must be augmented with fins (sold separately).

name: bluedog_LittleJoe2_Fin
title: Little Jeb 2 Fin
description: Large aerodynamic fin with a control surface for the Little Jeb 2.

name: bluedog_LittleJoe2_Recruit
title: Little Jeb 2 "Newby" Solid Motor
description: Small solid motors for augmenting the liftoff thrust of the Little Jeb 2 test vehicle. They only fire for a second or two, but provide a much needed boost off the ground. Available in single and triple mounts. Make sure the canted nozzles are properly pointing outwards.

name: bluedog_Atlas_1p25m_fairingBase
title: Bossart LVO1 1.25m Fairing Base
description: 1.25m fairing base with a flat top for mounting wider payloads, such as the LVO1-23 Multi Probe Decoupler.

name: bluedog_Atlas_1p25m_structuralAdapter
title: Bossart-F-MCA 1.25m Structural Adapter
description: 1.25m structural adapter built for Bossart rockets. Includes optional decoupler hardware to turn it into an interstage.

name: bluedog_Atlas_1p875m_conicalAdapter
title: Bossart-F-MCA 1.875m to 1.25m Structural Adapter
description: 1.875m to 1.25m conical structural adapter built for Bossart rockets. Includes optional decoupler hardware to turn it into an interstage.

name: bluedog_Atlas_CELV_extensionTank
title: Bossart-ADLV-7100 Extension Balloon Fuel Tank
description: Cylindrical extension fuel tank for the Bossart-ADLV launcher. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can. Available in multiple convenient lengths.

name: bluedog_Atlas_J1U_1p875m_Mount
title: Bossart-J18E 1.875 Engine Mount
description: A 1.875m engine mount with multiple mounting and shroud length options.

name: bluedog_Atlas_LR101inline
title: Bossart-IE-101I "Finch" Inline Engine
description: These small vernier engines were meant to be mounted to the bottom of an engine's fairing or boattail, and add roll control to a stage with only a single engine. This version can be used as a rudimentary upper stage engine, or for a sounding rocket.

name: bluedog_Atlas_OV1_decoupler
title: LVO1-23 Multi Probe Decoupler
description: Standard low-profile 1.5m decoupler for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_Atlas_SCORE
title: SC-58Z1 "Chatterbox" Relay Antenna
description: Engineers at the Research Center tell us if we shoved a tape recorder and a relay transmitter receiver into this nose cone, attached it to a Bossart B rocket and launched the whole thing into space, it would count as a communications "satellite".

name: bluedog_Atlas_SLV3X_2p5mBoosterSkirt
title: Bossart-PBE14 Advanced Booster Skirt
description: 2.5m booster skirt that can mount 4 engines for larger Bossart vehicles.

name: bluedog_Atlas_SLV3X_5engineAftTank
title: Bossart-BTX5-680 Sustainer Adapter Balloon Fuel Tank
description: Lower adapter fuel tank for 2.5m Bossart rockets. Has a mounting point for a single sustainer and allows the use of a 2.5m jettisonable booster skirt supporting 4 engines. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can.

name: bluedog_Atlas_SLV3X_aftAdapter
title: Bossart-BTX3-900 Aft Adapter Balloon Fuel Tank
description: Lower adapter fuel tank for the Bossart-1X launcher. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can. While extremely resilient, it cannot have other components radially attached to it, as doing so would compromise the structural integrity.

name: bluedog_Atlas_SLV3X_conicalAdapterTank
title: Bossart-BTX3-700 Conical Adapter Balloon Fuel Tank
description: Conical adapter fuel tank for the 2.5m Bossart-1X launcher. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can. This adapter tank is available with 1.875m and 0.9375m top node variants.

name: bluedog_Atlas_SLV3X_coreTank
title: Bossart-BTX3-2900 Core Fuel Tank
description: Main fuel tank for the 2.5m Bossart-1X launcher. You'll need to attach the adapter tank on to the bottom before mounting the aft sections. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can. The distinctive side pod contains probe core avionics for an all in one launch solution.

name: bluedog_Atlas_SLV3X_extensionTank
title: Bossart-BTX3-2600 Balloon Fuel Tank
description: Extension fuel tank for the Bossart-1X 2.5m launcher. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can. Used as the upper half of the core Bossart-1X tankage, and is available in multiple convenient lengths.

name: bluedog_Atlas_tricoupler
title: Bossart-STC3-Tri-coupler
description: A structural tri-coupler that enables three 1.875m lower stages to be connected to a single 1.875m upper stage. Can optionally be used as a decoupler.

name: bluedog_CELV_ConicalAdapterTank
title: Bossart-ADLV-3800 Balloon Fuel Tank
description: Conical adapter fuel tank for the Bossart-ADLV launcher. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can. Available in multiple top node sizes and lengths.

name: bluedog_CELV_MainTank
title: Bossart-ADLV-9000 Balloon Fuel Tank
description: Main fuel tank for the Bossart-ADLV launcher. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can. The distinctive side pods contain probe core avionics for an all in one launch solution.

name: bluedog_atlas_ARS_sidePod
title: LVO1 "Jamal" Sidemount Carrier Pod
description: A larger evolution of the "Remora" series of sidemount pods, the "Jamal" can carry an entire "Limpet" class probe and its motor.

name: bluedog_atlas_A_noseCone
title: NC-57A Bossart Rocket Development Nose Cone
description: An all in one instrumentation package to aid in the development of new rockets, this aerodynamic nose cone features a barometer experiment, pressure and acceleration sensors, and optional lead ballast storage to use as a mass simulator.

name: bluedog_atlas_F_antenna
title: Bosssart-F Command Antenna
description: This lightweight communications antenna provides omnidirectional coverage for relaying signals.

name: bluedog_atlas_LR101
title: Bossart-IE-101 "Crow" Radial Engine
description: These small radial vernier engines mount to the bottom of the Bossart rocket's main fuel tank. They help control the rocket during ascent, as well as providing roll control after the booster engines have been jettisoned.

name: bluedog_atlas_LR105engine
title: Bossart-IE-105 "Vulture" Liquid Engine
description: This lifter engine is optimized for vacuum flight instead of the low atmosphere. It offers tremendous efficiency to the core stage once its been lifted above the densest part of the atmosphere.

name: bluedog_atlas_LR89engine
title: Bossart-IE-89 "Buzzard" Liquid Engine
description: Simple, reliable 1.25m lifter engine. Designed for use on the jettisonable Bossart-DBSF Booster Skirt for half staging Bossart rockets.

name: bluedog_atlas_SPP
title: BSP "Remora" Sidemount Carrier Pod
description: A sidemount pod for storing experiments and ocassionally a sandwich.

name: bluedog_atlas_aftTank
title: Bossart-BT5-500 Adapter Fuel Tank
description: Fuel tank that incorporates special nodes for stage-and-a-half designs. Attach the booster fairing to the node in the middle of this tank, and the sustainer to the bottom.

name: bluedog_atlas_boosterSkirt
title: Bossart-PBF Booster Skirt
description: Fairing for covering the booster engines on Bossart rockets. Attach the booster engines to the two side nodes, and stage them away once you no longer need the thrust.

name: bluedog_atlas_castor4a_decoupler
title: Bossart-Dioscuri-ESMR Radial Decoupler
description: Small radial decoupler originally designed for use on Bossart IIAS rockets with the Dioscuri 4A SRBs. Attach to the booster skirt not the core tank.

name: bluedog_atlas_conicalTanks
title: Bossart-BT1-700 Conical Adapter Balloon Fuel Tank
description: Conical adapter fuel tank for the Bossart 1.875m launcher. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can. This adapter tank is available in multiple lengths and top diameters.

name: bluedog_atlas_coreTank
title: Bossart-BT4-3400 Core Fuel Tank
description: Long fuel tank for the Bossart-1 launcher. You'll need to attach the adapter tank on to the bottom before mounting the booster engine skirt. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can. There is a specially reinforced ring at the bottom for attaching vernier thrusters. The distinctive side pods contain probe core avionics for an all in one launch solution.

name: bluedog_atlas_extensionTanks
title: Bossart-BT3-1200 Extension Balloon Fuel Tank
description: Extension fuel tank for the Bossart 1.875m launcher. Used as the upper half of the core tankage for extanded variants of Bossart, and is available in multiple lengths to suit multiple builds. The extremely thin walls of this tank are kept in tension by the pressure of the fuel (and pressurant gas as the fuel is used), providing a rigidity similar to a soda can.

name: bluedog_atlas_retroMotor
title: Bossart-Inon "Banana" Retro Motor
description: A small retro motor to aid with separation from larger upper stages. Attach 8 to 12 to the bottom of the Bossart core stage, just above the booster skirt and stage when separating an Inon upper stage or similar. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Optionally, you can enable sequential fire in the editor to have them fire one after another even when staged all at once.</color>

name: bluedog_Atlas3_1p875m_mount
title: Muo-G18E 1.875 Engine Mount
description: 1.875m engine mount made from left over bits from a DR180 "Czar" engine. Can be used to mount 1 or 2 engines.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_2p5m_EngineMount
title: Muo-G25E 2.5m Engine Mount
description: 2.5m engine mount made from left over bits from a DR180 "Czar" engine. Can be used to mount 1,2 or 4 engines.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_5xx_conicalAdapter
title: Muo-V-5XX 1.875m-2.5m Internal Conical Adapter
description: It might look like a typical 2.5 interstage adapter but this conical adapter is slightly narrower and designed to sit **inside** of the Muo-V-5XX 3.5m Fairing Base Adapter to hold a 1.875m Inon stage.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_AJ60motor
title: Muo-JA206-S1080 Solid Rocket Booster
description: Advanced radially attached solid rocket.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_CCB_lower
title: Muo-5A2-5300 Fuel Tank
description: A big engine needs a big orange tank. We don't know why these ones in particular need to be orange, but we do know they don't include retro SRBs to aid in stage separation.  The distinctive side pod contains guidance avionics for an all in one launch solution.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_CCB_upper
title: Muo-5A1-7700 Fuel Tank
description: Sometimes, your regular long orange tank just isn't enough. For those times, you bring in the big kahuna: the Muo-7700.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_FairingBase5xx
title: Muo-V-5XX 3.5m Fairing Base Adapter
description: A 2.5m > 3.5m adapter skirt with a fairing ring on top and an internal mounting ring for an interstage or upper stage. Decoupler not included.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_GEM63
title: Muo-CGR63-S1080 "Diamond" Solid Rocket Booster
description: Advanced radially attached solid rocket.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_HLVdecoupler
title: Muo-5GHV Heavy-duty Radial Decoupler
description: Radial decoupler originally meant for 2.5 core liquid boosters. \n\nSurface attaches (with 2x symmetry) to the core. Attach the radial boosters to the decoupler via either surface attachment, or the optional toggleable attach node on the Muo-5A1-7700 upper tank.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_HLVnoseCone
title: Muo 5HV 2.5m Nose Cone
description: 2.5m nose cone with built in separation motors.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_RD180engine
title: Muo-V-DR180 "Czar" Liquid Engine
description: Imported directly from Krussia, the "Czar" employs two thrusters instead of one, giving it more power and control. When smaller rockets see it, they do a 180 and walk away.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_SRMDecoupler
title: Muo-5GADC Radial Decoupler
description: Radial decoupler originally designed for use on the Muo rocket. Attach nodes can optionally help with precise placement on Muo, otherwise can still be used via surface attachement.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_Star5F
title: Muo-V-SF5 "Bronu" Separation Motor
description: This strangely shaped separation solid is designed to go on the inside of the Muo-V intertank. Place in 8x symmetry and line up the end of the nozzles with the points on the exterior of the first stage.

name: bluedog_AtlasV_centaurFLR
title: Muo-5FLR Inon Forward Load Reactor
description: A load bearing deployable structural piece of dubious utility. Attach to the top of Inon III fuel tank, between the fuel tank and avionics, and set the auto deploy altitude for after the payload fairing has deployed.

name: bluedog_CentaurD_Avionics
title: Inon-ACS Avionics and Control System
description: 1.875m avionics segment for the Inon upper stage, includes a control core, reaction wheels, and batteries. It also serves as the structural adapter for the payload.

name: bluedog_CentaurD_EngineMount
title: Inon Engine Mounting Plate
description: Mounting plate for attaching single or dual upper stage engines to 1.875m tanks. Includes a node just below the top rim for attaching the interstage fairing. Used primarily on the Inon upper stage.

name: bluedog_CentaurD_FuelTank
title: Inon-D-1 1800 Fuel Tank
description: A somewhat longer 1.875m LHO tank for the Inon-D-1(A/T) upper stage. The Bossart-SLV-3D, Bossart-I, and Prometheus-IIIE use this design.

name: bluedog_CentaurD_RL10
title: Inon-R-10A "Isor" Cryogenic Engine
description: By using cryogenic hydrogen and oxygen as propellants, engines are capable of reaching efficiency levels unheard of using traditional propellants.
