The R-10A "Isor" upper stage engine is the first such engine to use these fuels. Use one or two as the engines for the Inon upper stage family, and six in the Sarnus SIV upper stage. Be sure to check that any tanks connected to it are filled with the correct propellants, and remember its fuel will boil off over time. Has switcheable upgrades.

name: bluedog_CentaurIII_FuelTank
title: Inon-II 2240 Fuel Tank
description: An even longer 1.875m LHO tank for the Inon-II upper stage. Used on Bossart-II and Bossart-IIIA. Can also be extended to be used as the Inon-III upper stage, which is used on Bossart-IIIB and Muo-V.

name: bluedog_CentaurT_Avionics
title: Inon-TG-ACS Avionics and Control System
description: 2.5m avionics segment for the Inon G/G'/T upper stages, includes a control core, reaction wheels, batteries, and a small amount of fuel. It also serves as the structural adapter for the payload.

name: bluedog_CentaurT_TankA
title: Inon-TG-280 Cryogenic Fuel Tank (1.875m)
description: Short 1.875m tank for the Inon G' and T upper stages.

name: bluedog_CentaurT_TankB
title: Inon-TG-700 Cryogenic Adapter Tank
description: 1.875m to 2.5m adapter tank for the Inon G, G', and T upper stages.

name: bluedog_CentaurT_TankC
title: Inon-TG-680 Cryogenic Fuel Tank (2.5m)
description: Short 2.5m tank for the Inon G, G', and T upper stages.

name: bluedog_CentaurT_TankD
title: Inon-TG-1120 Cryogenic Fuel Tank (2.5m)
description: Short 2.5m tank for the Inon G, G', and T upper stages.

name: bluedog_Centaur_2p5m_Adapter
title: Muo-V-4XX 1.875m-2.5m Adapter Interstage
description: Bottom part of a Inon stage. Attach to the node at the bottom of the top rim on the Inon mounting plate. This one goes to 2.5m. Includes a decoupler.

name: bluedog_Centaur_ARCM
title: Bossart-IIA-ARCM Roll Control Module
description: Later versions of the Bossart rocket replaced the complicated and expensive vernier system with this self contained thruster block. A small spherical monoprop tank is connected to 4 RCS thrusters, capable of maintaining roll authority, and the entire assembly is encased in an aerodynamic housing. Traditionally a single unit is placed on the interstage for the Inon upper stage.

name: bluedog_Centaur_FairingBase4xx
title: Muo-V-4XX 2.5m Fairing Base Adapter
description: 2.5m fairing base used for 1.875m core stacks.

name: bluedog_Centaur_FairingBase4xx2
title: Muo-V-4XX 1.875m Fairing Base Adapter
description: 1.875m fairing base used for 1.875m core stacks.

name: bluedog_Centaur_Kickstage
title: Inon-DM 1500 Cryogenic Upper Stage
description: Our engineers found discarded blueprints for an interestingly shaped upper stage in the dumpster of a rival space agency. They adapted this design into a small, 1.875m Inon-based hydrolox upper stage/kick stage designed to be used in conjunction with the Inon-D-1(A/T) upper stage. While designed to be used on top of Bossart-Centaur or Sarnus IB-CE as a kick stage, this little upper stage that could can be used for a wide number of applications. Can be used with or without jettisonable insulation panels. Comes with integrated RCS thrusters.

name: bluedog_Centaur_MPF_FairingBase
title: Inon-MPF 2.08m Fairing Base
description: A slightly expanded fairing base for slightly larger payloads.

name: bluedog_RL10B2
title: RL10B2 Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_centaur1875mAdapterFairing
title: Inon 1.875m Interstage
description: Bottom part of a Inon stage. Attach to the node at the bottom of the top rim on the Inon mounting plate. This one is 1.875m. Includes a decoupler.

name: bluedog_AJ10_118F
title: JA10-118-F10 "Hebel" Liquid Engine
description: An evolved version of the JA10 engines, the "Hebel" engine uses a larger engine bell to achieve superior performance. Originally made for the Daleth F upper stage.

name: bluedog_DCSS_2p5mFairing
title: BD-AFB-2 2.5m Fairing Base
description: Standard low-profile 2.5m fairing base for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_DCSS_Interstage
title: Daleth-III-DHSS 2.5m Interstage
description: 2.5m Interstage decoupler for the Daleth Hydrogen Second Stage. Attach to the bottom of the DHSS's hydrogen tank.

name: bluedog_DCSS_PayloadAdapter_0p9375m
title: SXA 0.9375m Payload Adapter
description: This lightweight structural adapter goes on top of your upper stage to help mount payloads.

name: bluedog_DCSS_PayloadAdapter_1p875m
title: SGA 1.875m Payload Adapter
description: This lightweight structural adapter goes on top of your upper stage to help mount payloads. Include two different endcap diameters.

name: bluedog_DCSS_PayloadAdapter_2p5m
title: SPA 2.5m Payload Adapter
description: This lightweight structural adapter goes on top of your upper stage to help mount payloads. Include three different endcap diameters.

name: bluedog_DCSS_StructAdapter
title: Daleth-III-DHSS 3.125-2.5m Structural Adapter
description: A series of 3.125m to 2.5m adapters made from surplus DHSS interstages. We're sure you can find many uses for these.

name: bluedog_DCSS_Tank
title: Daleth-III-DHSS Cryogenic Upper Stage
description: Daleth Hydrogen Second Stage. A large cryogenic upper stage with avionics and attitude control thrusters, only missing an engine. Available in two sizes the original version for Daleth III and the stretched version for Daleth IV Medium.

name: bluedog_Delta118KUpgrade
title: Delta118K Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_Delta118XUpgrade
title: Delta118X Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_Delta2_dpaf_base
title: TSS-2B Dual Payload Adapter Base
description: Dual payload adapter system for the Daleth II rocket. Attach the first payload to the base and then attach the TSS-2B Dual Payload Adapter to the floating node.

name: bluedog_Delta2_dpaf_top
title: TSS-2B Dual Payload Adapter
description: Dual payload adapter system for the Daleth II rocket. Attach the first payload to the TSS-2B base and then attach this adapter to the floating node. The adapter is available in 2 sizes.

name: bluedog_Delta4_dpaf_base
title: TSS-5B Dual Payload Adapter Base
description: Base for a dual payload adapter system for the Daleth IV and Muo rockets. Attach the first payload to the base and then attach the TSS-5F Dual Payload Adapter to the floating node.

name: bluedog_Delta4_dpaf_top
title: TSS-5F Dual Payload Adapter
description: Dual payload adapter system for the Daleth IV and Muo rockets. Attach the first payload to the TSS-5B Dual Payload Adapter Base and then attach this adapter to the floating node.

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_3p125interstage
title: Daleth IV 3.125m Interstage
description: A thin 3.125m interstage adapter for the Daleth IV rocket

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_DCSS_3p125_payloadAdapter
title: SPA 3.125m Payload Adapter
description: Standalone version of the payload adapter truss from the 3.125m DHSS fairing base.

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_DCSS_5m
title: Daleth-IV-DHSS Cryogenic Upper Stage
description: Enlarged Daleth Hydrogen Second Stage for Daleth IV Medium Plus and Heavy variants. A large cryogenic upper stage with avionics and attitude control thrusters, only missing an engine. Its a tight squeeze but a dual engine mount is available.

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_DCSS_fairingBase
title: Daleth IV DHSS 3.125m Fairing Base
description: 3.125m fairing base with integrated payload attach fitting truss.

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_RS68
title: Daleth SSR-68 "Bruno"
description: Said to have been developed for less than the cost of a new safety razor design, the SSR-68 is an incredibly powerful cryogenic booster engine originally meant for the Daleth IV launch vehicle. The rushed design process means it's not the most efficient design but it makes up for it in sheer thrust.

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_heavyDecoupler
title: Daleth IV Heavy 3.125m Radial Decoupler
description: Large radial decoupler for separating 3.125m boosters and core from each other. Includes separation motors at the bottom. The side with double ended struts should be attached to the radial boosters.

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_noseCone
title: Daleth IV Heavy 3.125m Nose Cone
description: Large 3.125m nose cone with built in separation motors.

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_s1_lowerTank
title: Daleth IV Unified Booster Core 20790 Lower Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Large 3.125m cryogenic fuel tank designed to be the lower half of the Daleth IV rocket's first stage. Includes a special structural extension at the bottom to attach to attach to the SSR-68 "Bruno" engine boattail as well as a more generic option.

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_s1_upperTank
title: Daleth IV Unified Booster Core 6210 Upper Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Large 3.125m cryogenic fuel tank designed to be the upper half of the Daleth IV rocket's first stage. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Includes optional side attach nodes for precise attachment to the heavy configuration booster decoupler. We recommend attaching the decoupler in symmetry and building the booster cores individually out of symmetry so the raceway and pipes all face the same way.</color>

name: bluedog_DeltaIV_smallInterstage
title: Daleth IV 3.125m to 1.5m Interstage
description: We dont know why you want to do this but this interstage enables the use of 1.5m upper stages with a 3.125m core. Also has an additional option for 1.875m stages.

name: bluedog_DeltaKUpgrade
title: DeltaK Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_DeltaK_Stage
title: Daleth-P/K-180-240 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Lightweight 0.9375m(ish) upper stage tank for Daleth upper stages. The Daleth-P is the base version and is upgradable to the larger Daleth-K variant via part upgrade. Hang below the "skirt" fairing base to make a Daleth-P/K upper stage. Includes built in attitude control thrusters.

name: bluedog_Delta_Avionics
title: Daleth-P/K Avionics Core
description: An advanced avionics core made from a pressurized fuel tank for the Daleth-II rocket. Place below your payload.

name: bluedog_Delta_GEM40
title: Daleth-CGR-40 "Ruby" Solid Rocket Booster
description: An evolution of the Dioscuri booster design, the Ruby utilizes new production methods, making it one of the most advanced SRBs ever built. Despite this, it remains a cost effective way to add thrust to rockets. Switcheable between ground lit and air lit versions.

name: bluedog_Delta_GEM40_Inline
title: Daleth-CGR-40I "Garnet" Solid Rocket Booster
description: An evolution of the Dioscuri booster design, the Ruby utilizes new production methods, making it one of the most advanced SRBs ever built. Despite this, it remains a cost effective way to add thrust to rockets. This version is meant for inline mounting and can vector the nozzle.

name: bluedog_Delta_GEM46
title: Daleth-CGR-46 "Emerald" Solid Rocket Booster
description: This CGR series rocket is slightly bigger than the Ruby, and includes a vectoring nozzle to help keep the rocket pointing straight. Typically used on Daleth III and Daleth II Heavy vehicles where 6 SRBs are ignited on the ground and 3 altitude optimized versions are ignited after they burn out. Switcheable between ground lit and air lit versions.

name: bluedog_Delta_GEM60
title: Daleth-CGR-60 "Sapphire" Solid Rocket Booster
description: Advanced booster in the CGR line. It features an extended 0.9375m case as well as a vectoring nozzle, and an extended variant.

name: bluedog_Delta_Miniskirt_1p5m
title: Daleth-P/K 1.5m Fairing Adapter
description: This 1.5m fairing base ring allows you to "hang" a 0.9375m rocket stage within a large interstage, so it doesn't have to sustain the full launch loads. Designed for the Daleth P and K stages you could also just reuse leftover Alphastar tankage and Sina lander engines...

name: bluedog_Delta_Miniskirt_1p875m
title: Daleth-P/K 1.875m Fairing Adapter
description: This 1.875m fairing base ring allows you to "hang" a 0.9375m rocket stage within a large interstage, so it doesn't have to sustain the full launch loads. Designed for the Daleth P and K stages you could also just reuse leftover Alphastar tankage and Sina lander engines...

name: bluedog_TR_201
title: RW-ATR2201 "Lysenko" Liquid Engine
description: A derivative of the Sina MEM Descent Propulsion System, this handy upper stage engine was adapted for use on the Daleth P upper stage used on Daleth 1000, 2000 and 3000.

name: bluedog_E1_engine
title: Prometheus RB-1E471 "Cordele" Rocket Engine
description: Occupying a middle ground between the "Navi" and the "Regor" booster engines, the "Cordele" is a bit of a curious use case. Originally developed for the Prometheus-I first stage (where it would be accompanied by a pair of IE-101 verniers), it was later proposed in a 4-engine cluster for the Sarnus I first stage.

name: bluedog_G1
title: FG1 "Drury" Liquid Fuel Engine
description: This compact and innocuous looking upper stage engine is in fact powered by incredibly volatile and toxic propellants. Despite being a simple pressure fed engine, it achieves exceptional efficiency. Use with extreme caution.

name: bluedog_M1
title: MBC-1 "Megalodon" Cryogenic Engine
description: An almost unbelievably huge cryogenic engine, the Megalodon offers incredible thrust in the same class as the LEF1 Regor combined with the efficiency of liquid hydrogen fuel. Intended for mega rockets such as improved Sarnus vehicles. Originally designed for vacuum or high altitude operations, a sea level version is also available for booster applications.

name: bluedog_MB60
title: BX-60 "Kodama" Cryogenic Engine
description: An extrememe performance evolution of the basic expander bleed cycle, this engine uses upstream boost pumps to achieve high turbo-pump and chamber pressures and produces double the thrust of a typical closed expander cycle engine. By injecting the bleed exhaust back into the nozzle for film cooling, some of the Isp loss from using the bleed cycle is also recovered. The end result is a no compromise upper stage engine.

name: bluedog_NERVA_FF
title: LVN-1 "Banyan" Nuclear Engine
description: Using the same reactor as the NERV XE, this refined design uses a full flow cycle for improved performance and reliability. A curious aerospike nozzle variant is also available to shorten the considerable length of the engine although the size constraints result in a 20s loss of vacuum Isp.

name: bluedog_NERVA_II
title: LVN-2 "Redwood" Nuclear Engine
description: Built around an incredibly powerful reactor, this nuclear engine emphasises thrust to enable demanding crewed interplanetary missions.

name: bluedog_NERVA_XE
title: LVN-XE "Baobab" Nuclear Engine
description: An experimental nuclear engine running a hot bleed cycle just to see if whether using nuclear reactors for propulsion is a good idea or not... Features built in roll control utilising the bleed exhaust.

name: bluedog_RL20
title: PL20-X3 Cryogenic Engine
description: Bluedog Design Bureau's first attempt at a staged combustion cycle design, this high pressure engine delivers high thrust and Isp in a remarkably compact package. Includes variants optimized for either sea-level or vacuum operation. A deployable nozzle extension keeps the vacuum optimized version very compact even with a large expansion ratio.

name: bluedog_RS30
title: RXD-30 "Zhar-Ptitsa" Cryogenic Engine
description: This compact engine harnasses the capabilities of staged combustion to deliver astonishing performance. Although slightly less powerful than the latest Isor engines, the combination of high chamber pressure and a 1:400 expansion ratio results in an incredible 474s of vacuum Isp. Designed from the ground up for extended on orbit appplications such as space tugs.

name: bluedog_XLR129
title: PXR-129 "Hausenblase" Cryogenic Engine
description: Derived from BPL20, the PXR-129 has murky origins, having been allegedly designed for a classified rocket spyplane. Now available for civilian use, the Hausenblase engine provides improved thrust and greater flexibility compared to its predecessor. It is suitable for a variety of applications such as improved Sarnus rockets or even reusable spaceplanes. Of particular interest is its dual mode capability. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: The engine can be used with its two position nozzle either retracted for optimal sea level performance or deployed for optimal altitude or vacuum performance. This switch can be made in flight using the mode switch via the right click part action window or an action group.</color>

name: bluedog_smallNuclearEngine
title: SM01 "Aphid" Nuclear Engine
description: Using a left over small reactor design fromt the "NERV" development program, this tiny nuclear engine features an unusual sideways folding nozzle to maximise room inside limited spaceplane payload bays.

name: bluedog_BigG_Adapter
title: Leo-B1G-CCA "Raphael-A" Interstage Adapter
description: Interstage Adapter for the Leo-B1G capsule with "Raphael" cylindrical service module. Includes 1.875m, 2.5m, 3.125m, 3.75m, and 4.25m mounting options.

name: bluedog_BigG_Antenna
title: Leo-B1G-4200 Uplink Antenna
description: An extending antenna for keeping the B1G spacecraft in contact with ground stations.

name: bluedog_BigG_Cabin
title: Leo-B1G "Botticelli" Crew Module
description: As operations in space become more complex, more crew members are needed. This expanded crew module replaces the standard Leo service module, allowing four additional Kerbals to ride to space.

name: bluedog_BigG_ConicSM_CargoModule
title: Leo-B1G-CCC "Raphael-C" Cargo Module
description: Cargo module for the conical B1G service module. Place below the retro module. Includes cargo space(theoretically), as well as a supply of monopropellant and electricity. It also includes a built in decoupler for jettisoning from the retro module. Engines sold separately.

name: bluedog_BigG_ConicSM_RetroModule
title: Leo-B1G-CCR "Raphael-R" Retro Module
description: Hollow structural adapter for the conical B1G service module. Includes sump tanks for the OAMS system as well as mounting points for 8 retro solids. Hold the ALT key when placing them on the nodes.

name: bluedog_BigG_CylindricalSM_CargoModule
title: Leo-B1G-PCC "Raphael-C" Pressurized Cargo Module
description: Cargo module for the cylindrical B1G service module. Place below the equipment module. Includes cargo space, electricity, and fuel cell. It also includes an optional built in decoupler for jettisoning from the equipment module. Engines sold separately.

name: bluedog_BigG_CylindricalSM_EquipmentModule
title: Leo-B1G-CCR "Raphael-R" Equipment Module
description: Equipment module for the cylindrical B1G service module. Contains the main supply of monopropellant, mounting points for the RCS thrusters, and a crew access tube to connect the capsule to the Pressurized Cargo Module.

name: bluedog_BigG_Decoupler
title: Leo-M-3VS 2.5m Capsule Decoupler
description: Low profile decoupler for separating the Leo-B1G "Botticelli" capsule from the service module.

name: bluedog_BigG_DrogueChute
title: Leo-B1G-DPC Drogue Parachute
description: Drogue parachute for the B1G capsule. Attach to the node in the nose section.

name: bluedog_BigG_LES
title: Leo-B1G-LES Launch Escape System
description: A powerful Launch Escape System based on the Kane-11-LES, modified to fit the Leo-B1G capsule. Stage to jettison. For best results jettison high in (or out of) the atmosphere, usually around first stage cut off. After firing during an emergency abort, canards deploy to flip the capsule retrograde for parachutes. Automatically added to the abort action group. Autostrut to heaviest part to stop wobbling.

name: bluedog_BigG_MainParachute
title: Leo-B1G-MPC Landing Parachute System
description: Large, tri-canopy parachute for the B1G spacecraft. Remarkable for how much parachute is packed into such a small volume.

name: bluedog_BigG_Nose
title: Leo-B1G Nose Segment
description: Advanced nose segment for the Leo-B1G spacecraft. While it lacks hardware for docking, it still provides the most important task of any part: Aesthetics. And covering up the main chutes, we suppose. It also includes a spot for the drogue chutes, if crews have started complaining about G-loads during parachute deployment.

name: bluedog_GeminiB_AdapterModule
title: Leo-B-ATE "Angelo" Adapter Module
description: The lower half of the Leo-B adapter, includes two separation rockets, batteries, and a decoupler for separating from the retro section.

name: bluedog_GeminiB_RetroModule
title: Leo-B-6RST "Michel" Retro Module
description: This hollow structural adapter is designed to sit on top of the Leo-B adapter section and includes mounting points for six retro motors.

name: bluedog_Gemini_ArrowSM
title: Leo-C-MOTML "Pitseolak" Service Module
description: This service module was essentially created by welding together a Leo's Retro and Equipment modules. The interiors have been entirely rearranged, making way for a crew tunnel and a small pressurized volume in the aft section. While this prevents it from being as packed with fuel as the Meduci-M, it works better as a crew ferry vehicle with a rear-mounted docking port.

name: bluedog_Gemini_AugustusCapsule
title: Leo-M-ARP "Augustus" Automated Resupply Pod
description: As our program expands our manned stations in Kerbin orbit and elsewhere, it becomes increasingly important to bring supplies up and down in addition to crew. This modified "Vinci" command pod is capable of docking itself, and is loaded with room for cargo.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Capsule
title: Leo-M-63E "Vinci" Command Pod
description: It is clear that only so much can be accomplished by single kerbals in space. Though we'd eventually like to be launching even more in a single launch, this two-kerbal pod is an important step in developing the skillsets our program will need for more complex missions in the future.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Decoupler_1p5m
title: Leo-M-CSM 1.5m Decoupler
description: Low profile decoupler for separating the Leo capsule from the retro module.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Decoupler_1p875m
title: Leo-M-CSM 1.875m Decoupler
description: Low profile decoupler for separating the Leo capsule from the retro module.

name: bluedog_Gemini_DockingPort
title: Leo-M-6NDP Nose Docking Mechanism
description: One of the most crucial skills that the Leo program is meant to develop is the ability to rendevous and dock in space. This simple docking mechanism doesn't have the ability to transfer crew or resources, but it will allow you to connect two vessels in flight. This male active docking mechanism corresponds to the female Belle Docking Adapter. It includes an indexing key that slides into the V shape on the Belle Docking Adapter, to help line the two craft up properly.

name: bluedog_Gemini_DrogueChute
title: Leo-M-8DC Drogue Parachute
description: Drogue parachute for the Leo capsule. Attach to the node in the nose section.

name: bluedog_Gemini_EquipmentModule
title: Leo-A-O7NB "Meduci-E" Equipment Module
description: This orbital service module includes a supply of mono propellant for <s>extensive</s> orbital maneuvers, an optional fuel cell, and 8 rotational control thrusters. It also includes a built in decoupler for jettisoning from the Retro Module. Engines sold separately.

name: bluedog_Gemini_EquipmentModule_Empty
title: Leo-A-O7NBE "Meduci-S" Structural Equipment Module
description: This orbital service module includes 8 rotational control thrusters, but lacks a supply of monopropellant and electrical equipment. It also includes a built in decoupler for jettisoning from the Retro Module. Engines sold separately.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Heatshield_1p5m
title: Leo-M-SZR 1.5m Heatshield
description: It's like a frisbee! 1.5m heatshield for the Leo capsule.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Heatshield_1p875m
title: Leo-M-SZR 1.875m Heatshield
description: It's like a frisbee! 1.875m heatshield for the Leo capsule.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Heatshield_2p5m
title: Leo-M-SZR 2.5m Heatshield
description: It's like a frisbee! 2.5m heatshield for the Leo capsule.

name: bluedog_Gemini_HorizonScanners
title: Leo-M-2A2 Horizon Scanner Module
description: Horizon scanners module for the Leo CSM with a jettisonable fairing. Provides SAS modes.

name: bluedog_Gemini_LanderCan
title: Dona-LK217 Miniature Lander Can
description: This extremely small capsule is darn near the smallest capsule you can make to hold a single kerbal. Contains just enough supplies and features to enable a short romp down to the surface and back. Its pressurized cockpit makes it (slightly) safer than an external command seat, though there isn't room to take off one's helmet. Please peruse the other Dona parts in order to turn this capsule into a complete lander system.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Lander_Engine
title: Dona-LDAE8 Lander Engine
description: This remarkably simple and robust engine might not be the best in terms of thrust or efficiency, but its light weight and small size makes it ideal for small, lightweight landers. A single example is used as both the descent and ascent engine of the Dona lander, using the empty toroidal descent stage tank as a takeoff platform.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Lander_Frame
title: Dona-LTT60 Descent Stage Tank
description: Descent tank for the Dona Lander system. Attach to the bottom node of the engine. The descent stage can decouple using a built in decoupler. Meant to have 4x legs attached, but you can probably get away with less if you're brave. The ladder can be toggled in the VAB for uncrewed landers.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Lander_Leg
title: Dona-L3GG Landing Leg
description: While Professor Wernher was looking for his golf clubs, we were working on this landing leg for the Dona lander system. Attach in 4x symmetry to the descent stage. Swings downwards before locking into place - while this improves stability, it means there is no suspension system to absorb impacts.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Lander_LowProfilePort
title: Belle Low Profile Docking Port
description: This special docking port is designed to capture the Leo nose cone's docking mechanism. The simple mechanical connection won't even allow you to transfer resources, much less crew, but it will securely attach two vessels together, for berthing or travel. This low profile model needs to be deployed in order to dock. Be warned, it is not as forgiving as its larger sibling.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Lander_SaddleTank
title: Dona-LAT25 Ascent Stage Tank
description: Ascent tank for the Dona lander system. Place on either side of the lander can, make sure that any extra fuel in the descent tank is transferred before you tank off. Includes a whopping 8 integrated RCS thrusters.

name: bluedog_Gemini_LongFerrySM
title: Leo-L-MFBS "Bellini" Service Module
description: This stretched Leo equipment module includes batteries, a pressurized volume for cargo, larger fuel tanks. It has sets of RCS thrusters for lateral and retro translation, as well as attitude control. For use with the standard Leo retro module.

name: bluedog_Gemini_LunarReconSM
title: Leo-D-L8SM "Raphael" Service Module
description: This service module was essentially created by welding together a Leo's Retro and Equipment modules. Omitting the retro solids and packing in more fuel and batteries allows it to perform longer duration missions, perhaps on a lunar free return trajectory with a sufficiently powerful launch vehicle. Engines sold separately.

name: bluedog_Gemini_LunarRecon_Antenna
title: Leo-MRC-A Discone Antenna
description: A small extending antenna used for maintaining communications between the Leo spacecraft and the ground from distance beyond low orbit.

name: bluedog_Gemini_LunarRecon_Camera
title: Leo-XP-NRC Nose Camera
description: This adaptation of the Leo nose replaces the docking hardware with a set of cameras, for mapping terrain.

name: bluedog_Gemini_LunarRecon_Dish
title: Leo-MRC-D High Gain Dish
description: A small dish meant to fit in the aft compartment of a Leo spacecraft, for high bandwidth communications from distances beyond low orbit.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Magnetometer
title: Leo-XP-MFD Magnetometer Boom
description: A small extending magnetometer boom to be mounted in the trunk of the Leo spacecraft's adapter section.

name: bluedog_Gemini_MainParachute
title: Leo-M-7RC Landing Parachute System
description: Standard 0.625m inline parachute.

name: bluedog_Gemini_NoseFairing
title: Leo-M-1NAC Aerodynamic Nose Cover
description: Covers up the nose of the Leo Docking Mechanism to protect it during ascent. Jettison once out of the atmosphere.

name: bluedog_Gemini_OAMSThruster
title: Leo-EOMAS "Gus" Manuevering Thruster
description: This tiny thruster is nevertheless more than sufficient to manuever the Leo capsule around in low Kerbin orbit. Can function as both a primary engine and posigrade rcs thruster.

name: bluedog_Gemini_RadarEvaluationPod
title: Leo-XP-REP Training Subsatellite
description: A small subsat meant to fit in the trunk of the Leo spacecraft's adapter section. Used for practicing rendezvous and stationkeeping techniques. Includes batteries, antennas, and visual acquisition lights.

name: bluedog_Gemini_ReentryRCS
title: Leo-M-68V Reentry Reaction Thrusters
description: This RCS system provides full 3 axis stabilization for a pod. It is meant to be used during reentry, and is disabled by default. It can be manually enabled in flight.

name: bluedog_Gemini_RetroModule
title: Leo-A-O6NB "Meduci-R" Retro Module
description: This hollow structural adapter is designed to sit on top of the Leo equipment section and house a quad of retro motors for reentry. Houses six translational control thrusters. We're sure you can find other uses for this too.

name: bluedog_Gemini_RetroMotor
title: Leo-ET385 "Banger" Retro Solid
description: Leo retro solid derived from the Staara-13-A "Retras". Place in 4x symmetry in the gaps of the retro module cruciform. It features BDB's SafeSolid™ system, allowing the engine to be shut down in flight, allowing for more accurate orbital insertions and manuevers.

name: bluedog_Gemini_RumbleSeat
title: Leo-M-63F "Giotto" Crew Module
description: As operations in space become more complex, more crew members are needed. This expanded crew module replaces the standard Leo service module, allowing an additional Kerbal to ride to space.

name: bluedog_Gemini_Spectrometer
title: Leo-XP-SPE Spectrometer Instrument
description: A small ion spectrometer, meant to be mounted to the Leo spacecraft's adapter section. The data cannot be transmitted so remember to collect your data for returning to Kerbin.

name: bluedog_Gemini_UHFAntenna
title: Leo-MRC-U Uplink Antenna
description: A small extending antenna used for maintaining communications between the Leo spacecraft and the ground.

name: bluedog_Shuguang_EquipmentModule
title: Leo-S-714E "Zhengming-E" Equipment Module
description: This orbital service module includes a supply of mono propellant for extensive orbital maneuvers, batteries, and 8 rotational control thrusters. It also includes a built in decoupler for jettisoning from the Retro Module. Engines sold separately.

name: bluedog_Shuguang_Nose
title: Leo-S-714AC Aerodynamic Nose Cover
description: Covers up the nose of the Leo Docking Mechanism to protect it during ascent. This nose is meant to be kept on for rear-docking configurations, but nothing stops you from jettisoning after ascent.

name: bluedog_Shuguang_RetroModule
title: Leo-S-714R "Zhengming-R" Retro Module
description: This structural adapter is designed to sit on top of the Leo equipment section and house a quad of retro motors for reentry. Houses six translational control thrusters. We're sure you can find other uses for this too.

name: bluedog_Agena_StandardFairingBase
title: Belle-4900 Fairing Base
description: A 0.98m fairing base used as the standard shroud for the Belle upper stage. Used for payloads such as Aeolus. Later adapted as the standard fairing for the Daleth-E upper stage.

name: bluedog_Decoupler_0p625m
title: BD-SPD-0 0.625m Decoupler
description: Standard low-profile 0.625m decoupler for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_Decoupler_0p9375m
title: BD-SPD-05 0.9375m Decoupler
description: Standard low-profile 0.9375m decoupler for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_Decoupler_1p25m
title: BD-SPD-1 1.25m Decoupler
description: Standard low-profile 1.25m decoupler for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_Decoupler_1p5m
title: BD-SPD-12 1.5m Decoupler
description: Standard low-profile 1.5m decoupler for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_Decoupler_1p875m
title: BD-SPD-15 1.875m Decoupler
description: Standard low-profile 1.875m decoupler for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_Decoupler_3p125m
title: BD-SPD-25 3.125m Decoupler
description: Standard low-profile 3.125m decoupler for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_0p625m
title: BD-AFB-0 0.625m Fairing Base
description: Fairing base for 0.625m fairings. You can't fit too much inside one, but we're sure you'll find a use for it.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_0p9375m
title: BD-AFB-05 0.9375m Fairing Base
description: Standard low-profile 0.9375m fairing base for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau. Also features an optional floating node for a dual payload adapter.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_0p9375m_Static
title: Belle-RNRD 0.9375m Static Fairing Base
description: Low-profile 0.9375m fairing base for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau. Features side attach nodes for use with the Belle RNRD Nose Cone set. Also features an optional floating node for a dual payload adapter.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_1p25m
title: BD-AFB-1 1.25m Fairing Base
description: Standard low-profile 1.25m fairing base for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_1p5m
title: BD-AFB-12 1.5m Fairing Base
description: Standard low-profile 1.5m fairing base for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_1p875m
title: BD-AFB-15 1.875m Fairing Base
description: Standard low-profile 1.875m fairing base for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_3p125m
title: BD-AFB-315 3.125m Fairing Base
description: Standard low-profile 3.125m fairing base for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_3p75m
title: BD-AFB-375 3.75m Fairing Base
description: Standard low-profile 3.75m fairing base for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_4p25m
title: BD-AFB-425 4.25m Fairing Base
description: Standard low-profile 4.25m fairing base for rockets produced by Bluedog Design Bureau.

name: bluedog_FairingBase_6p25m
title: BD-AFB-625 6.25m Fairing Base
description: A gigantic fairing base for gigantic fairings to use on gigantic rockets.

name: bluedog_Fairingbase_2p5m_ring
title: BD-RFB-15 2.5m Ring Fairing Base
description: An ultra low profile ring fairing base

name: bluedog_Lateraltron
title: PDC-L "Lateraltron" Separation Motor
description: Small separation boosters in an aerodynamic housing. This model angles the thrust sideways, to push radial boosters away from the core stage. The rockets fire in the direction of the red arrows, so pay close attention and make sure they're thrusting the correct direction before you attempt to use them.

name: bluedog_PSM_0p3125m_HighProfile
title: P-SSM-3H 0.3125m Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A small, 0.3125m decoupler designed especially for deploying a satellite from the launch vehicle. Rather than using explosive bolts to separate the part above it, a spring loaded plate gently pushes the payload away. This one is taller than most, for payloads that need a large standoff from the upper stage below. Additional height (needed for solar panels or instruments hanging below the bottom plane of the payload, for example) can be gained by attaching structural payload adapters to the bottom.

name: bluedog_PSM_0p3125m_LowProfile
title: P-SSM-3L 0.3125m Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A small, 0.3125m decoupler designed especially for deploying a satellite from the launch vehicle. Rather than using explosive bolts to separate the part above it, a spring loaded plate gently pushes the payload away. This one is designed to be as low profile as possible, to minimize the length of the fairing. Additional height (needed for solar panels or instruments hanging below the bottom plane of the payload, for example) can be gained by attaching structural payload adapters to the bottom.

name: bluedog_PSM_0p3125m_MediumProfile
title: P-SSM-3M 0.3125m Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A small, 0.3125m decoupler designed especially for deploying a satellite from the launch vehicle. Rather than using explosive bolts to separate the part above it, a spring loaded plate gently pushes the payload away. This one is medium height, for when only a slight standoff is needed. Additional height (needed for solar panels or instruments hanging below the bottom plane of the payload, for example) can be gained by attaching structural payload adapters to the bottom.

name: bluedog_PSM_0p625m_HighProfile
title: P-SSM-6H 0.625m Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A small, 0.625m decoupler designed especially for deploying a satellite from the launch vehicle. Rather than using explosive bolts to separate the part above it, a spring loaded plate gently pushes the payload away. This one is taller than most, for payloads that need a large standoff from the upper stage below. Additional height (needed for solar panels or instruments hanging below the bottom plane of the payload, for example) can be gained by attaching structural payload adapters to the bottom.

name: bluedog_PSM_0p625m_LowProfile
title: P-SSM-6L 0.625m Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A small, 0.625m decoupler designed especially for deploying a satellite from the launch vehicle. Rather than using explosive bolts to separate the part above it, a spring loaded plate gently pushes the payload away. This one is designed to be as low profile as possible, to minimize the length of the fairing. Additional height (needed for solar panels or instruments hanging below the bottom plane of the payload, for example) can be gained by attaching structural payload adapters to the bottom.

name: bluedog_PSM_0p625m_MediumProfile
title: P-SSM-6M 0.625m Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A small, 0.625m decoupler designed especially for deploying a satellite from the launch vehicle. Rather than using explosive bolts to separate the part above it, a spring loaded plate gently pushes the payload away. This one is medium height, for when only a slight standoff is needed. Additional height (needed for solar panels or instruments hanging below the bottom plane of the payload, for example) can be gained by attaching structural payload adapters to the bottom.

name: bluedog_Perfectron
title: PDC-P "Perfectron" Separation Motor
description: Small separation boosters in an aerodynamic housing. This model angles the thrust vertically, to help carry an upper stage away from a lower one, or to assist in ullage. The rockets fire in the direction of the red arrows, so pay close attention and make sure they're thrusting the correct direction before you attempt to use them.

name: bluedog_RadialDecoupler_Medium
title: BD-IBRD Medium Radial Decoupler
description: Medium radial decoupler for decoupling medium (0.9375m - 1.5m) things.

name: bluedog_RadialDecoupler_Mini
title: BD-WBR Mini Radial Decoupler
description: Small radial decoupler for decoupling small things.

name: bluedog_SpinDecoupler_p3125m
title: 0.3125m Spin Motor Decoupler
description: Small 0.3125m spin motor. Once decoupled, two opposing motors will spin up a small payload. <#ef7b06> INSTRUCTIONS: 1) Attach to the bottom of a solid rocket motor. 2) Hold desired attitude using a stage with attitude control and ensure the craft is stable. 3) Disable SAS and then stage the decoupler which will decouple from the bottom and fire the spin motors. 4) Your SRM is now spin stablized. Manually jettison the spin motor using the "Jettison" command in the part action window or an action group which will decouple the spin table from the SRM. 5) Ignite the SRM 6) Profit. (The BDB Yoyo Despin device is reccomended to slow the spin rate after burn is completed. Mandatory RCS and or Persistent Rotation mods are not necessary to use this but are reccomended if you wish the payload to remain spin stablized for entire mission duration).</color>

name: bluedog_Spintable_0p625
title: Spin Motor Decoupler 0.625m
description: 0.625m spin motor. Once decoupled, two opposing motors will spin up a small payload. <#ef7b06> INSTRUCTIONS: 1) Attach to the bottom of a solid rocket motor. 2) Hold desired attitude using a stage with attitude control and ensure the craft is stable. 3) Disable SAS and then stage the decoupler which will decouple from the bottom and fire the spin motors. 4) Your SRM is now spin stablized. Manually jettison the spin motor using the "Jettison" command in the part action window or an action group which will decouple the spin table from the SRM. 5) Ignite the SRM 6) Profit. (The BDB Yoyo Despin device is reccomended to slow the spin rate after burn is completed. Mandatory RCS and or Persistent Rotation mods are not necessary to use this but are reccomended if you wish the payload to remain spin stablized for entire mission duration).</color>

name: bluedog_Spintable_0p9375
title: Spin Motor Decoupler 0.9375m
description: 0.9375m spin motor. Once decoupled, two opposing motors will spin up a small payload. <#ef7b06> INSTRUCTIONS: 1) Attach to the bottom of a solid rocket motor. 2) Hold desired attitude using a stage with attitude control and ensure the craft is stable. 3) Disable SAS and then stage the decoupler which will decouple from the bottom and fire the spin motors. 4) Your SRM is now spin stablized. Manually jettison the spin motor using the "Jettison" command in the part action window or an action group which will decouple the spin table from the SRM. 5) Ignite the SRM 6) Profit. (The BDB Yoyo Despin device is reccomended to slow the spin rate after burn is completed. Mandatory RCS and or Persistent Rotation mods are not necessary to use this but are reccomended if you wish the payload to remain spin stablized for entire mission duration).</color>

name: bluedog_saturn_SII_SLAbase
title: BD-AFB-625 6.25m Super Wide SLA Fairing Base
description: This 6.25m  adapter base contains mounting points for the Kane CSM and 4 jettisonable panels to hold it above the payload. This base has been designed specifically for super wide landers. You can manually decouple the lander once the transposition and docking maneuver is complete or use a separate decoupler.

name: bluedog_saturn_h03_SLA_panel
title: Sarnus-EXSP Super Wide SLA Panel
description: Place in 4x symmetry around the BD-AFB-4625 4.25m-6.25m or BD-AFB-625 6.25m SLA Super Wide Fairing Base.

name: bluedog_saturn_h03_SLAbase
title: BD-AFB-4625 4.25m-6.25m Super Wide SLA base
description: This 4.25m  adapter base contains mounting points for the Kane CSM and 4 jettisonable panels to hold it above the payload. This base has been designed specifically for super wide landers. You can manually decouple the lander once the transposition and docking maneuver is complete or use a separate decoupler.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_AdapterSegment
title: SG9-ASD Adapter Segment
description: Structural section that adapts from the SG-9 "Nonagon" camera system to the modular truss segments. Includes a mounting point and decoupler for the larger SG-9 recovery capsules.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_Camera
title: SG-9 "Nonagon" Reconnaissance System
description: This massive camera assembly forms the core of the SH-9 "Nonagon" Spy Satellite. A pair of rotating 'optical bars' record large format, stereoscopic images covering vast swathes of the ground below. The system is a technological marvel, referred to as some as the most mechanically complex object ever put in space. A set of infrared sensors, originally used for star tracking, can also be repurposed to take IR radiometry measurements.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_FairingBase
title: SG9-FB 1.875m Control Fairing Base
description: Fairing base and probe core for the SG-"Nonagon" satellite. Place above the service module and below the camera.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_LaunchAdapter
title: SG9-LA 1.875m Decoupler
description: Launch adapter and decoupler for the SG-9 "Nonagon" satellite. Place on top of the Prometheus-III avionics unit - the space inside the avionics truss is needed for the service engine.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_LifeboatRCS
title: SG9-LRC Lifeboat RCS
description: Small, backup set of RCS thrusters for the SG-9 "Nonagon" spy satellite. Disabled by default - must be manually activated. Place in 2x symmetry on the small blocks on the bottom of the service module.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_MainRCS
title: SG9-MCB RCS Block
description: Primary attitude control for the SG-9 "Nonagon" spy satellite. Place in 2x symmetry in the open spots on the sides of the service module.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_MappingCamera
title: SG9-9MS "Meadow" Mapping Camera System
description: Supplementary mapping camera system meant to mount to the nose of an SG-9 "Nonagon". Uses the smaller recovery vehicle feature on earlier Spyglass satellites.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_Mk8_Capsule
title: SG9-RV1 Return Capsule Pod
description: This larger return capsule was made to recover the larger film of the SG-9 "Nonagon" satellites. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: This pod has hibernation enabled by default in order to conserve power. Make sure to disable hibernation after separating from the mother craft in order to regain control.</color>

name: bluedog_Hexagon_Mk8_Heatshield
title: SG9-RV3 Return Capsule Heatshield
description: A medium sized heatshield to protect the SG9 Return Capsule on reentry.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_Mk8_Parachute
title: SG9-RV2 Return Capsule Parachute
description: A medium sized parachute for SG-9 Return Capsules. Makes you wonder if its possible to catch the capsule mid air... Includes a manually operated decoupler for separating the retro motor from the rest of the pod once the retro burn is accomplished.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_Mk8_Retro
title: SG9-RV8 Return Capsule Retro Pack
description: A larger retro pack to deorbit the upgraded SG-9 Return Capsules. Make sure to decouple with the capsule facing the correct orientation for the retro burn - the RCS pack (disabled by default) really only has enough monopropellant for spin stabilization.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_ServiceEngine
title: SG9-SPS "Tanya" Service Engine
description: Originally developed as an upgraded secondary propulsion system for Belle-derived Spyglass satellites, later repurposed as the main service propulsion for the SG-9 "Nonagon" satellites.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_ServiceModule
title: SG9-FBC Equipment Module
description: Service module for the SG-9 "Nonagon" satellites. Contains plenty of monopropellant and batteries for a long orbital lifetime.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_SolarPanel
title: SG9-SP66 Deployable Solar Panel
description: Large, fold out non-tracking solar array for the SG-9 "Nonagon" satellites. Place in 2x symmetry on the aft face of the service module, ensuring that they are horizontal (relative to orbital attitude) when deployed.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_TrussSegment
title: SG9-TSD Truss Segment
description: Modular truss segment for the SG-9 "Nonagon" satellite. Includes a mounting point and decoupler for the larger SG-9 recovery capsules.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_VHF_Bent
title: SP9-VHB Helical Antenna
description: Very High Frequency (VHF) antenna for the Nonagon spy satellite. Mounts on the nose of the craft, and should point towards the surface when in orbital orientation.

name: bluedog_Hexagon_VHF_Straight
title: SP9-VHS Helical Antenna
description: Very High Frequency (VHF) antenna for the Nonagon spy satellite. Mounts on the nose of the craft.

name: bluedog_Juno4_EngineMount
title: Chryslus-IVB-EMS 1.25m Engine Mount
manufacturer: Bluedog Design Bureau Special Projects Deparment
description: Mounting plate for attaching a single engine to 1.25m tanks. Includes a node just below the top rim for attaching the interstage fairing.

name: bluedog_Juno4_Engine_45K
title: Chryslus-IV-K45 "Hunter" Liquid Engine
description: This upper stage engine fills the gap between the Belle and Prometheus upper stage engines. Intended for use on the Chryslus IV-B second stage. Using a unique heated hybrid cycle, it eliminates the need for turbopumps while saving mass over traditional pressure fed engines. Surplus hot gas from the generator is fed through a vernier nozzle for roll control.

name: bluedog_Juno4_Engine_6K
title: Chryslus-IV-K6 "Seeker" Liquid Engine
description: Primitive upper stage engine. Don't activate it in the atmosphere - the engine bell is optimized for vacuum performance. Neither the most powerful nor most efficient engine, but it's a start. Designed for use on the Chryslus IV-A second and IV-B third stages, and also used on the Vejur 3rd stage. Includes 0.3125m mounting hardware.

name: bluedog_Juno4_FuelTank_1
title: Chryslus-IVB-440 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Upper stage fuel tank for Chryslus IV-B second stage.

name: bluedog_Juno4_FuelTank_2
title: Chryslus-IVA-160 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Lightweight 1.25m (ish) upper stage tank for the Chryslus-IVA upper stage. Includes guidance and attitude control.

name: bluedog_Juno4_Interstage
title: Chryslus-IVB-SIA 1.25m Structural Interstage
description: 1.25m interstage decoupler for the Chryslus-IVB upper stages.

name: bluedog_Jupiter_EngineMount
title: Chryslus-EF Engine Fairing
description: Fairing to cover up 1.25m engines mounting on 1.5m stages.

name: bluedog_Jupiter_FuelTank
title: Chryslus-2000 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Standard 1.5m fuel tank for the Chryslus rocket.

name: bluedog_Jupiter_Guidance
title: Chryslus-IIAGC Guidance Unit
description: Guidance core for the Chryslus rocket. Includes a bottom decoupler, to separate from the core stage and align the high speed stages for orbital insertion.

name: bluedog_Jupiter_Vernier
title: Chryslus-EE5 "Rhesus" Vernier Exhaust Engine
description: This small vernier nozzle gimbals the exhaust stream of a gas generator engine, adding roll control to your rocket. Though we suppose it could be jury rigged to work with any engine. It's up to you, really.

name: bluedog_CELV_BoosterSkirt
title: Bossart-ADLV-DES Booster Skirt
description: Fairing for covering the booster engines on Bossart ADLV rockets. Attach the HD1-270 "Navi" booster engines to the four outer nodes, and stage them away once you no longer need the thrust.

name: bluedog_CELV_Fin
title: Bossart-ADLV-SSW Aerodynamic Fin
description: A small stabilizing wing for the Bossart-ADLV.

name: bluedog_CELV_SustainerTank
title: Bossart-ADLV-STA1300 Adapter Fuel Tank
description: Fuel tank that incorporates special nodes for stage-and-a-half designs. Attach the booster fairing to the node in the middle of this tank, and the HD1-270 "Navi" sustainer to the bottom.

name: bluedog_LDC_1p875mAdapter
title: Herakles-SAC 1.875m Structural Adapter
description: This structural adapter can be used to transition a stack's diameter from 3.125m to 1.875m, with short and long variants. Includes an optional decoupler that is disabled by default.

name: bluedog_LDC_Adapter
title: Herakles-SA 2.5m/3.75m Structural Adapter
description: This structural adapter can be used to transition a stack's diameter from 3.125m to 2.5m or 3.75m. Includes an optional decoupler that is disabled by default.

name: bluedog_LDC_NoseCone
title: Herakles-ANC 3.125m Nose Cone
description: A tried and proven 3.125m nose cone.

name: bluedog_LDC_S1_EngineMount
title: Herakles-EM1S Engine Mount
description: 3.125m engine mount for the Herakles first stage. Includes numerous options for mounting engines ranging from 1x mounts all the way up to 9x.

name: bluedog_LDC_S1_Tank1
title: Herakles-LF13400 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Large 3.125m fuel tank designed to be the lower half of the Herakles rocket's first stage. Includes mounting points for 8 Muo-V-SF5 "Bronu" Separation Motors.

name: bluedog_LDC_S1_Tank2
title: Herakles-LF10000 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Large 3.125m fuel tank designed to be the upper half of the Herakles rocket's first stage. Includes three different height variants. The short variant (when combined with the lower tank and engine mount) is the proper height for SRB1207 "Helios" Solid Rocket Boosters.

name: bluedog_LDC_S2_Avionics
title: Herakles-ACT 3.125m Avionics Unit
description: A large and advanced avionics compartment for the Herakles rocket.

name: bluedog_LDC_S2_EngineMount
title: Herakles-S2MFYE Engine Mount
description: 3.125m engine mount for the Herakles second stage. Includes numerous options for mounting engines ranging from 1x mounts all the way up to 7x.

name: bluedog_LDC_S2_Interstage
title: Herakles-S2SIA Interstage
description: 3.125m interstage adapter for the Herakles rocket.

name: bluedog_LDC_S2_Tank1
title: Herakles-LF5700 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Large fuel tank for the Herakles rocket's second stage.

name: bluedog_LDC_S2_Tank2
title: Herakles-LF3300 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: A short extension tank for the Herakles rocket second stage.

name: BDB_FASAUmbilicalTower
title: FASA Umbilical Tower
description: This umbilical tower functions as a launch clamp and fuel pump for liquid fuel/hydrogen, oxidizer and mono-propellent. It also Provides electricity. Right click on the tower to start the fuel flow.

name: BDB_FASAlaunchClamp125
title: FASA 1.25m Redstone Launch Clamp
description: Rockets getting stuck? Use the "Redstone Clamp", it attaches to the bottom of small 1.25m rockets.

name: BDB_FASAlaunchClamp25
title: FASA 2.5m Redstone Launch Clamp
description: The 2.5 clamp attaches to the bottom of 2.5m rockets. Just make sure your engine can handle the weight. If your rocket explodes your going to need to add some radial clamps.

name: BDB_FASAlaunchClampApollo
title: FASA Apollo Launch Clamp
description: Similar to the clamps that held the Saturn V down while the engines spooled up. The clamp had a special hood it retracted into. It protect the clamps from rocket exhaust so they could be reused for multiple launches.

name: BDB_FASAlaunchClampAtlas
title: FASA Atlas Launch Clamp
description: The "Atlas Clamp" attaches to the sides of rockets to help stop the launch wiggles.

name: BDB_FASAlaunchTower
title: FASA Launch Tower
description: This launch tower lets you load Kerbals from the tower to your spacecraft.  Load it up with Kerbals from the astronaut complex and right click on the doors at the top or bottom to EVA.

name: bluedog_GeminiFerry_DockingAdapter
title: Leo-F-DSA Docking Adapter
description: Structural docking adapter for the Leo Ferry. Ideally sized for the Kane active docking port.

name: bluedog_GeminiFerry_PressurizedModule
title: Leo-F-PCS Pressurized Cargo Module
description: Cargo module for the Leo Ferry.

name: bluedog_GeminiFerry_RCS
title: Leo-F-OAMS RCS Control Block
description: Large RCS block designed to act as the primary propulsion for the Leo Ferry. Includes variant with the lateral thrusters angled at 45 degrees.

name: bluedog_Gemini_0p9375mEndcap
title: LMSS-STM3 0.9375m Station Endcap
description: A hemispherical cap designed to terminate station modules that don't need a docking port or other inline parts attached past it. An attachment node is still provided to aid in mating the module to the launch vehicle. Optionally, it can also act as a 0.9375m to 0.625m adapter if the central cover is removed.

name: bluedog_Gemini_1p5mEndcap
title: LMSS-STM2 1.5m Station Endcap
description: A hemispherical cap designed to terminate station modules that don't need a docking port or other inline parts attached past it. An attachment node is still provided to aid in mating the module to the launch vehicle. Optionally, it can also act as a 1.5m to 0.625m adapter if the central cover is removed.

name: bluedog_Gemini_1p5mShortSegment
title: LMSS-OCS 1.5m Space Station Module
description: A small 1.5m crew can.

name: bluedog_Gemini_1p875mLongAdapter
title: LMSS-LSA 1.875m Structural Adapter
description: 1.875m to 1.5m structural adapter for the Leo Modular Space Station.

name: bluedog_Gemini_DipoleAntenna
title: Leo-KZ24 Dipole Antenna
description: A simple extending dipole antenna made for the extended Leo program.

name: bluedog_Gemini_DockingAntenna_Fixed
title: Leo-F-DGAF Docking Guidance Antenna
description: Fixed version of the Leo docking antenna.

name: bluedog_Gemini_DockingAntenna_Rotating
title: Leo-F-DGA Docking Guidance Antenna
description: A deployable antenna for advanced Leo variants.

name: bluedog_Gemini_DoubleXAntenna
title: Leo-HD6D Colinear Antenna Array
description: A colinear antenna array made for the Leo program.

name: bluedog_Gemini_InflatableAirlock
title: LMSS-IAM "Expanse" Inflatable Airlock
description: Inflatable airlock for Leo-based stations, useful for allowing crew EVA access to the outside of the station.

name: bluedog_Gemini_LES
title: Leo-LAS Launch Escape System
description: This solid rocket tower is designed to wrench the command pod up and away from a malfunctioning rocket. Use only in case of emergency. WARNING: Staging the LES will also decouple it from the bottom node, in order to dispose of it after launch. Map the engine to the ABORT action group for emergency use. Designed for advanced Leo variants launched on anything bigger than a Prometheus II.

name: bluedog_Gemini_LargeFixedArray
title: LMSS-EX4 Fixed Solar Array
description: A large, non-tracking solar array for Leo Modular Space Stations.

name: bluedog_Gemini_OneRoomStationModule
title: LMSS-ORS 1.875m One-Room Space Station Module
description: Core building block of the Leo Modular Space Station, this module contains a single pressurized volume with associated support equipment. Provides enough space for two crew members.

name: bluedog_Gemini_RadialAttachPoint
title: LMSS-RAP Radial Attachment Point
description: An expansion node for the Leo Modular Space Station. Can be used to add more docking points or other structural connections to a station.

name: bluedog_Gemini_SolarWing
title: Leo-010SM Solar Antenna
description: Small deployable solar wings with communications antennas on the tips.

name: bluedog_Gemini_StructuralEndcap
title: LMSS-STM 1.875m Station Endcap
description: A hemispherical cap designed to terminate station modules that don't need a docking port or other inline parts attached past it. An attachment node is still provided to aid in mating the module to the launch vehicle. Optionally, it can also act as a 1.875m to 0.625m adapter if the central cover is removed.

name: bluedog_Gemini_StructuralNode
title: LMSS-SNMK 1.25m Structural Node
description: 1.25m structural node module for the Leo Modular Space Station. Use radial attachment points to add nodes according to your needs.

name: bluedog_Gemini_TwoRoomStationModule
title: LMSS-TRS 1.875m Two-Room Space Station Module
description: Core building block of the Leo Modular Space Station, this module contains a large pressurized volume split into two "rooms", with associated support equipment. Provides enough space for three crew members.

name: bluedog_Gemini_WhipAntenna
title: Leo-DVO Whip Antenna
description: A simple extending antenna made for the extended Leo program.

name: bluedog_MOL_0p9375mAdapter
title: LMSS-SSA 0.9375m Structural Adapter
description: A small plate for adapting a stack from 0.9375m to 0.625m.

name: bluedog_MOL_1p5mStationSegment
title: LMSS-OLS 1.5m Orbital Laboratory Segment
description: A 1.5m station laboratory module.

name: bluedog_MOL_Adapter_15_125
title: BSA-0120-0100 - MOS-SA Small Structural Adapter
description: A nearly flat 1.5m adapter for MOS and LMSS stations.

name: bluedog_MOL_Adapter_1875_15
title: BSA-0150-0120 - MOS-LA Large Structural Adapter
description: A nearly flat 1.875m adapter for MOS and LMSS stations.

name: bluedog_MOL_Airlock
title: MOS-AS "Adventure" Airlock Segment
description: Dedicated airlock module for MOS stations, useful for allowing crew access to the station as they leave their ships.

name: bluedog_MOL_Camera
title: MOS-NL10 "Dorian" Reconnaissance System
description: This powerful telescope and camera system was originally designed for use by [REDACTED] before being converted to more peaceful, scientific uses. It can be used to gather data from the surface of planets. As well as spy on Kr-[REDACTED]. Don't listen to anyone trying to convince you that unmanned satellites are cheaper and just as effective. The results from the camera cannot be transmitted. It is recommended to recover the data or better yet, process them in a lab such as the MOS-LS "Mossy".

name: bluedog_MOL_ControlSegment
title: MOS-CBS Control Block Segment
description: Thin 1.875m control and avionics system. Use for controlling your MOS stations, and Rhea resupply vehicles.

name: bluedog_MOL_CrewTube
title: LMSS-CTT 0.9375m Crew Tube
description: 0.9375m crew tube for the Leo Modular Space Station.

name: bluedog_MOL_CrewTube_DoubleLength
title: LMSS-CTTD 0.9375m Crew Tube
description: 0.9375m crew tube for the Leo Modular Space Station. This one is longer, in case you need something... longer.

name: bluedog_MOL_DockingPort
title: MOS-DM 1.875m Docking Mechanism
description: This large docking module is used to connect MOS segments to each other. It is capable of soft docking to line up the segments, before retracting and solidifying the connection.

name: bluedog_MOL_EquipmentSection
title: MOS-EFS Equipment Module
description: Equipment section for the MOS space station and Leo Ferry. Contains plenty of monopropellant and electricity.

name: bluedog_MOL_FiveWayAdapter
title: BSA-0120-0120 - MOS-TA 5 Way Structural Adapter
description: A five way 1.5m adapter for MOS based stations.

name: bluedog_MOL_ForkDockingPort
title: LMSS-FDM 1.875m Fork Docking Mechanism
description: This large docking module is used to connect Leo Modular Space Station segments to each other. It is capable of soft docking to line up the segments before retracting and solidifying the connection. Note that it is designed to dock with the corresponding LMSS-RDM 1.875m Ring Docking Mechanism.

name: bluedog_MOL_Lab_New
title: MOS-NLS "Dorian" Orbital Laboratory Segment
description: This mobile laboratory segment was originally designed for use by [REDACTED] before being converted to more peaceful, scientific uses. It can be used to conduct experiments and process data. As well as spy on Kr-[REDACTED].

name: bluedog_MOL_LargeRadiator
title: LMSS-TRP2 Surface Radiator
description: A radially attachable radiator panel to help dissipate heat into space.

name: bluedog_MOL_Propellant
title: MOS-PS-80 Propellant Carrier
description: A large rack of spherical tanks for storing monopropellant.

name: bluedog_MOL_RCS
title: MOS-CB RCS Control Block
description: This large, powerful RCS block is capable of controlling the attitude of entire stations.

name: bluedog_MOL_RingDockingPort
title: LMSS-RDM 1.875m Ring Docking Mechanism
description: This large docking module is used to connect Leo Modular Space Station segments to each other. It is capable of soft docking to line up the segments before retracting and solidifying the connection. Note that it is designed to dock with the corresponding LMSS-FDM 1.875m Fork Docking Mechanism.

name: bluedog_MOL_SmallRadiator
title: LMSS-TRP1 Surface Radiator
description: A radially attachable radiator panel to help dissipate heat into space.

name: bluedog_MOL_Solar1
title: MOS-PVP-100 Solar Array
description: A large solar array, for those stations that are hungry for electricity.

name: bluedog_MOL_Solar2
title: MOS-PVP-2 Solar Array
description: Medium sized tracking solar panels. Primitive, but capable of generating more power than anything else with our current technology. Hopefully we'll come up with something better soon.

name: bluedog_MOL_ThreeWayAdapter
title: BSA-0120-0120 - MOS-TA 3 Way Structural Adapter
description: A three way 1.5m adapter for MOS based stations.

name: bluedog_MOL_TrackingAntenna
title: MOS-GTA Tracking Antenna
description: High speed communications system for transmitting large amounts of classified data back down to Kerbin.

name: bluedog_MOL_UnpressurizedCargo
title: MOS-UCS Unpressurized Cargo Segment
description: This 1.875m unpressurized bay is useful for bringing up things such as small station segments, satellites, supplies, and parts ready to be attached to the outside of something.

name: bluedog_MOL_rackDish
title: MOS-MCL Communications Dish
description: High speed communications system for transmitting large amounts of classified data back down to Kerbin. Adjust the deploy limit to change the final resting angle.

name: bluedog_MiniLab_Adapter
title: Hermes-OMS Equipment Section
description: A 1.25m to 0.9375m adapter that integrates a monopropellant powered fuel cell and batteries.

name: bluedog_MiniLab_Interstage
title: Hermes-OMS 1.25m Structural Interstage
description: Short 1.25m interstage for attaching the Hermes capsule to the top of the Hermes-OMS lab.

name: bluedog_MiniLab_Lab
title: Hermes-OMS 1.25m Lab Module
description: A small 1.25m lab module. It doesn't provide much space for working, but it may prove useful for testing theories about working in space.

name: bluedog_MiniLab_Ladder
title: Hermes-OMS Crew Ladder
description: Ladder for transferring from a Hermes pod to the Hermes-OMS lab.

name: bluedog_Tianja_LargeFixedSolar
title: MOS-DOTD-F2 Fixed Solar Array
description: Large, heavy solar panels imported from the far East. Primitive, but capable of generating more power than anything else with our current technology. Hopefully we'll come up with something better soon.

name: bluedog_Tianja_LargeRotatingSolar
title: MOS-DOTD-R2 Tracking Solar Array
description: Large, heavy solar panels imported from the far East. Primitive, but capable of generating more power than anything else with our current technology. Hopefully we'll come up with something better soon.

name: bluedog_Tianja_SmallFixedSolar
title: MOS-DOTD-F1 Fixed Solar Array
description: Large, heavy solar panels imported from the far East. Primitive, but capable of generating more power than anything else with our current technology. Hopefully we'll come up with something better soon.

name: bluedog_Tianja_SmallRotatingSolar
title: MOS-DOTD-R1 Tracking Solar Array
description: Large, heavy solar panels important from the far East. Primitive, but capable of generating more power than anything else with our current technology. Hopefully we'll come up with something better soon.

name: bluedog_Mercury_Airbrake
title: Hermes M-ASF Destabilizing Flap
description: This small airbrake prevents the Hermes from stabilizing in a "nose-first" orientation during reentry. Attach to the offset node on the Hermes Antenna/Drogue Chute unit. Once in orbit, click the brakes action group to extend it for the rest of the mission.

name: bluedog_Mercury_AntennaNose
title: Hermes M-DCAM Nose Unit
description: This nose cap for the Hermes capsule includes the drogue chute and the main antenna. It has an attach node for a destabilizing flap. The latter might not accomplish much but its theorized to help self orient a reentering craft and its nice to have.

name: bluedog_Mercury_Capsule
title: Hermes M-PRC Personal Reentry Capsule
description: Our Hermes is to Alnair's Almach capsule what the Joker is to Batman. Smaller, spunkier, more colorful, and has a higher number of fatalities under its belt. Erm... Scratch that last part. Can be launched suborbital on a Sandstone rocket or into low Kerbin orbit on a Bossart.

name: bluedog_Mercury_Decoupler
title: Hermes-Etoh 1.25m Decoupler
description: Decoupler for separating the Hermes capsule from an Etoh rocket.

name: bluedog_Mercury_Heatshield
title: Hermes M-HS Heatshield
description: Small 1.25m heatshield for the Hermes capsule. Place underneath, before adding the retropack. Does not include a fairing. Comes with a built in airbag for a nice comfy landing.

name: bluedog_Mercury_Interstage
title: Hermes-Bossart 1.25m Interstage
description: Interstage for separating the Hermes capsule from a Bossart rocket.

name: bluedog_Mercury_LES
title: Hermes M-LES Launch Escape System
description: This solid rocket tower is designed to wrench the command pod up and away from a malfunctioning rocket. Use only in case of emergency. WARNING: Staging the LES will also decouple it from the bottom node, in order to dispose of it after launch. Map the engine to the ABORT action group for emergency use.

name: bluedog_Mercury_Parachute
title: Hermes-MASD Main Parachute
description: Main parachute for the Hermes capsule. Attach to the node in the recovery section.

name: bluedog_Mercury_ParachuteRCS
title: Hermes M-LCM Recovery Module
description: This part contains four way RCS thrusters and a goo experiment. Questionably-important parachute sold separately. <#ef7b06>AUTHOR'S NOTE: DON'T FORGET TO ADD THE SEPARATE MAIN PARACHUTE! AN INTERIOR SPACE AND ATTACH NODE IS PROVIDED. The Goo Experiment door can be closed by action group prior to reentry.</color>

name: bluedog_Mercury_PosigradeRocket
title: Hermes M-PM "Zoot" Kick Motor
description: This tiny solid rocket motor is essentially the ancestor of a modern day Sepratron. They were originally used to push a Hermes away from its Bossart booster. We're sure you'll think of even more uses for it.

name: bluedog_Mercury_RetroRocket
title: Hermes M-RM "Shepherd" Kick Motor
description: A shameless coffee can full of throttleable boom. This rocket motor is meant to give you just enough kick to get you down from orbit... hopefully... It features BDB's proprietary SafeSolid™ system, allowing the engine to be shut down in flight, allowing for more accurate orbital insertions and maneuvers. Surface attach to the back of the Hermes M-RPS Retro Pack in 3x symmetry. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Optionally, you can enable sequential fire in the editor to have them fire one after another even when staged all at once.</color>

name: bluedog_Mercury_Retropack
title: Hermes M-RPS Retro Pack
description: This metal tub attaches to the bottom of the Hermes heatshield, allowing retro solids to be mounted. Decoupling will release the straps to separate from the capsule for reentry. Note that this is purely a structural unit - no propulsion is included. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: The retro pack has a hidden attach node. Attach the decoupler to this node after placing the solid motors.</color>

name: bluedog_AIMP_Antenna
title: MIP-KRA Whip Antenna
description: A small, fixed whip antenna for the MIP probe series.

name: bluedog_AIMP_Core
title: MIP-ACC Probe Core
description: Originally developed for a long-forgotten lunar probe program, the MIP is a capable, if boring, probe core. Includes a small battery and cold gas nitrogen tank.

name: bluedog_AIMP_Magnetometer
title: MIP-FMP Folding Magnetometer Boom
description: This instrument is used for measuring a planet's magnetic field. It breaks magnetometer convention by folding up instead of telescoping. It's harder to fit within a fairing, but is lighter. Sufficiently crafty pilots can use it to right a lander that has tipped over, though this is not recommended.

name: bluedog_AIMP_SolarPaddle
title: MIP-ESP RCS Solar Panel
description: This small solar panel is spring loaded to extend on command. It is capable of rotating to track the sun, and some non-tracking RCS jets are also included.

name: bluedog_AIMP_SolidDecoupler
title: MIP-SSD 0.125m Decoupler
description: A small, very low profile 0.125m stack decoupler for tiny probes.

name: bluedog_AIMP_Star13
title: Staara-13-A "Retras" Solid Rocket Motor
description: Staara-series solid rocket motor, model 13-A. Vacuum optimized nozzle, simpler and more reliable than liquid boosters. Includes 0.3125m mounting hardware. It features BDB's SafeSolid™ system, allowing the engine to be shut down in flight, allowing for more accurate orbital insertions and manuevers.

name: bluedog_ANNA
title: TNSS-GRV1 "NANA" Geodetic Satellite
description: A robust early satellite for mapping the gravitational fields of planetary bodies. Engineers "borrowed" a TNSS-2A "Walnut" satellite, scooped out all the navigation equipment, and replaced it with geodesy equipment. Includes an upper mount designed for attaching secondary payloads or other desired equipment.

name: bluedog_Alouette_Antenna
title: ALTTE-TMA Sounding Antenna
description: A relatively long extending sounding antenna for the Skylark satellite series.

name: bluedog_Alouette_Core
title: ALTTE-D2 "Skylark" Research Satellite
description: Primitive, spin stabilized bus designed to serve as an ionospheric exploration probe.

name: bluedog_Biosat_Adapter
title: Bion-MPB Adapter Section
description: This adapter contains instruments to monitor the effects of space travel on simple life forms. Offers superior quality of scientific data compared to the OTLTH-E but the experiment must be recovered. Mount a Spyglass return capsule to the top to return the science and little critters safely back to Kerbin.

name: bluedog_Biosat_Antenna
title: Bion-QRZ Telemetry Antenna
description: A small extending telemetry antenna for the Bion satellite series.

name: bluedog_Biosat_Magnetometer
title: Bion-MFD Magnetometer Attitude Control Boom
description: The attitude control scheme of the Bion satellites used a magnetometer to help orient it relative to the planet. That doesn't prevent it from also recording and returning the data it collects...

name: bluedog_C1engine
title: TC-1 "Midge" Auxiliary Engine
description: A small bipropellant engine that can serve a multitude of purposes including orbit trimming, auxiliary propulsion, or primary propulsion for small probes.

name: bluedog_Camera_InstrumentTorus
title: Aeolus-EST Camera Equipment Torus
description: Early structural torus for mounting instruments for the Aeolus meteorological satellites. While this has less electrical storage than the later model, it has a battery of cameras for observing cloud coverage.

name: bluedog_Clementine_Bus
title: Tangerine-SDI23 "Citron" Satellite Bus
description: A versatile, robust probe bus built by a shady government corporation in collaboration with Bluedog Design Bureau intended to be the platform to test many cutting-edge space technologies on. Includes a copious internal supply of fuel, two integrated low gain antennas, and an integrated charged particle telescope experiment. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Add the Tangerine-SDI23 "Compass" Star Tracker to your craft to gain additional SAS modes.</color>

name: bluedog_Clementine_Engine
title: Tangerine-SDI23-489-N "Juicer" Bipropellant Space Engine
description: Breakthroughs in engineering have allowed engineers to create a compact, highly efficient bipropellant engine intended for satellite propulsion that runs on liquid fuel. This engine is intended for getting satellites in orbit around other celestial bodies, but it can be used for a wide range of applications.

name: bluedog_Clementine_HGA
title: Tangerine-SDI23-CRA High Gain Antenna
description: A suprisingly simple and robust antenna designed for the Tangerine-SDI23 satellite. Can support near-Kerbin and inner solar system type missions. Designed specifically for Munar and asteroid flyby operations.

name: bluedog_Clementine_ISAS
title: Tangerine-SDI23 "ISA" Adapter
description: Engineers realized that a discarded kick stage could be more than just a simple discarded kick stage; it could also be a secondary satellite! Designed for the Tangerine-SDI23 Satellite kick stage, ISA is intended to be fixed to a Staara-37 solid motor. ISA is its own probe core and includes its own solar panels. ISA is a platform for an integrated radiation monitoring experiment and a micrometeorite/debris impact detector experiment. Includes a decoupler for the top of ISA (designed to separate the primary payload from ISA). However, ISA does not include SAS control (as ISA is spin stabilized) or an internal antenna (the ISA whip antennas are separate parts).

name: bluedog_Clementine_ISAS_Antenna
title: Tangerine-SDI23 "ISA" Whip Antenna
description: A small, fixed whip antenna for the SDI-23 "ISA" satellite.

name: bluedog_Clementine_LowerRCS
title: Tangerine-SDI23 Lower RCS
description: A small, three-way RCS intended for the aft section of the Tangerine-SDI23 satellite.

name: bluedog_Clementine_Sensors
title: Tangerine-SDI23-AIO Imaging Sensor Platform
description: The cream of the crop in imaging technology. This cutting-edge science platform was designed to test the latest imaging systems in long-term space operations with classified shady government techology. The result is one of the most advanced mapping cameras to date. This sensor platform captures images in visible, near infrared, long wave infrared, and ultraviolet light as well as acquiring altitude terrain data with a LIDAR system, all in a small package. However, the compactness of the instrument limits some of the infrared and ultraviolet imaging capabilities slightly. Designed to be used with the Tangerine-SDI23 satellite.

name: bluedog_Clementine_SolarPanel
title: Tangerine-SDI23 "Swiss" Tracking Solar Panel
description: This fold-out, tracking solar panel was originally designed for the Tangerine-SDI23 satellite. The hole in the center of the panel is for the satellite's low gain antennas to poke out of. Includes a variant to have it folded straight so it can be used in more applications.

name: bluedog_Clementine_StarTracker
title: Tangerine-SDI23-SSA "Compass" Star Tracker
description: A cutting edge assembly composed of two star trackers and an advanced computer system designed to help increase the pointing accuracy of the Tangerine-SDI23 spacecraft to aid mapping operations.

name: bluedog_Clementine_UpperRCS
title: Tangerine-SDI23 Upper RCS
description: A small, three-way RCS intended for the forward section of the Tangerine-SDI23 satellite.

name: bluedog_Courier_Core
title: CRR-1B "Messenger" Communications Satellite
description: Primitive, spin stabilized bus designed to be used as an early communications satellite. Includes deployable antennas and a large surface area of solar cells.

name: bluedog_Decoupler_0p125m
title: HLR-JD03 0.125m Decoupler
description: Small 0.125m decoupler for tiny tiny probes.

name: bluedog_ERCS
title: HLR-PCS Attitude Control Thruster
description: A highly efficient electrical xenon RCS thruster. Includes variants with one, two, or three thrusters.

name: bluedog_Explorer_11
title: Pathfinder-11 "Kraushaar" Satellite
description: Early orbital satellite, contains instruments for exploring the gamma ray environment of space.

name: bluedog_Explorer_7
title: Pathfinder-7 "Suomi" Satellite
description: Early orbital satellite, contains instruments for measuring the flux of solar energy absorbed by the planet.

name: bluedog_Explorer_8
title: Pathfinder-8 "Jacchia" Satellite
description: Early orbital satellite, contains instruments for measuring electrical environment of space.

name: bluedog_Explorer_Beacon_SLR
title: BE-SLR227 "Lighthouse" Laser Reflector
description: A small, but cutting edge laser reflector designed to take geodetic measurements. Also includes a forward electrostatic probe to take ionospheric measurements. This experiment is designed to be used with the TNSS-5 "Statum" satellite bus to give it use as a scientific satellite.

name: bluedog_Explorer_S45
title: Pathfinder-S45 "Seddon" Satellite
