description: Early orbital satellite, contains instruments for investigating the shape of the ionosphere.

name: bluedog_Explorer_S46
title: Pathfinder-S46 "Sui" Satellite
description: Early orbital satellite, contains instruments for further radiation experiments following the discoveries by Pathfinder-1.

name: bluedog_Explorer_Star17
title: Staara-17 "Longinus" Solid Rocket Motor
description: Staara-series solid rocket motor, model 17. Vacuum optimized nozzle, simpler and more reliable than liquid boosters. Includes 0.3125m mounting hardware. Can be upgraded to model 17-A, which features minor impovements to thrust and ISP, as well as an increased amount of solid propellant. It features BDB's SafeSolid™ system, allowing the engine to be shut down in flight, allowing for more accurate orbital insertions and maneuvers.

name: bluedog_Helios_Adapter
title: Sonne-MBM-AA Structural Adapter
description: Integral structural adapter for the bottom of the Sonne probe. It decouples on the bottom, to separate from the solid kick motor (typically a Staara-37). Several experiments, as well as the low gain antenna, should be mounted to it.

name: bluedog_Helios_Core
title: Sonne-MBM-HEOS Probe Core
description: 0.9375m probe core for the Sonne spacecraft, created as a joint project between BDB and our teutonic partners. Place a sun shade above and below (flip the lower shade over) to form an hourglass shape, and then attach the experiment arms and RPWS antennas. Includes an integrated cosmic ray detector. Micrometeoroid detector is included, but requires the separate Sonne experiment to be run.

name: bluedog_Helios_Dish
title: Sonne-MBM-LGCA Communications Array
description: A combined medium and high gain antenna for the Sonne spacecraft, created as a joint project between BDB and our Teutonic partners. Place above the top sun shade.

name: bluedog_Helios_LowGainAntenna
title: Sonne-MBM-LGA Low Gain Antenna
description: Low gain horn antenna for the Sonne probe. Mounts on the lower adapter, on the opposite side to the MM detector.

name: bluedog_Helios_MM_Detector
title: Sonne-MBM-MMS Micrometeoroid Detector
description: Advanced micrometeoroid detector with a built in mass spectrometer. Detects impacts and the composition of interplanetary dust. Mounts on the lower adapter of the Sonne probe, on the opposite side to the matching grate on the probe core.

name: bluedog_Helios_Magnetometer
title: Sonne-MBM-MEB Magnetometer Boom
description: Large magnetometer on an extending arm for the Sonne spacecraft, created as a joint project between BDB and our teutonic partners. Place one on each side of the HEOS probe core on the mounting plates provided. Includes two different variants of magnetometer, use one of each.

name: bluedog_Helios_Photometer
title: Sonne-MBM-ZPS Photometer
description: Zodiacal light Photometer, designed to measure light reflected by interplanetary dust. Mounts on the lower adapter of the Sonne probe, in 3x symmetry.

name: bluedog_Helios_RPWSAntenna
title: Sonne-MBM-LRWA RPWS Antenna
description: RPWS whip antenna for the Sonne spacecraft, created as a joint project between BDB and our teutonic partners. Place one on each side of the HEOS probe core on the mounting plates provided. Do note that while it technically works with only one antenna, using at least two would theoretically provide much better data.

name: bluedog_Helios_SunShade
title: Sonne-MBM-SER Sun Shade
description: Large, conical 0.9375m to 1.5m adapter for the Sonne spacecraft, created as a joint project between BDB and our teutonic partners. Place above and below the HEOS probe core (flip the bottom one over to make an hourglass shape). Attach the dish on top and a Staara-37FNV underneath. Contains a mix of solar cells and reflective surfaces to reject heat while providing sufficient electrical power.

name: bluedog_HoopAntenna
title: Pathfinder Crossed Dipole Antenna
description: A pair of dipole antennas, crossed and bent to help fit inside payload fairings.

name: bluedog_IDCSP_Probe
title: MOCA Relay Satellite
description: Primitive, simple probe core with built in antennas. Useful as an early communications satellite, or perhaps a relay sat dropped from a larger probe bus. Their small size allows for an entire constellation to be deployed in a single launch and a dedicated multi decoupler system is available for this purpose.

name: bluedog_IMP_Magnetometer
title: MIP-RMS Extending Rubidium Magnetometer
description: This fascinating instrument uses rubidium vapour to measure the magnetic fields as the spacecraft passes through them. Make sure you leave enough room for it to extend - close proximity to the spacecraft will scramble the instrument's sensors.

name: bluedog_Injun1
title: IW-1 "Trunk" Satellite
description: A tiny satellite that's designed to study radiation and the magnetic field in the ionosphere and beyond. Designed to be launched as a secondary payload sandwiched between TNSS-4A and SR-1 probes, but it can also be launched by itself as a small payload. Has minimal SAS control with magnetic stabilization. Includes built-in solar panels, antennas, and an aft decoupler.

name: bluedog_Kepler_Bus
title: Boruki-K2 "Johannes" Probe Core
description: An advanced satellite bus developed for the Boruki space telescope. Unlike most satellite buses, which are boxes full of avionics, the Boruki-K2 "Johannes" Probe Core is mostly hollow on the inside with its avionics and electronics attached to the outside of the bus. This allows for specialized payloads to be attached to the inner core of the bus. Comes with its own supply of monopropellant for attitude control. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Add the Boruki-K2-KST2 Advanced Star Tracker to your craft to gain additional SAS modes.</color>

name: bluedog_Kepler_ElectronicsBox
title: Boruki-K2-EEB Electronics Box
description: Greeble anything you want with this rad box'o'science! Is capable of storing experiment data and results.

name: bluedog_Kepler_HGA
title: Boruki-K2-FCA High Gain Antenna
description: A compact and advanced high-gain dish antenna developed for the Boruki space telescope. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Attaches to the node on the side of the main probe core.</color>

name: bluedog_Kepler_OmniAntenna
title: Boruki-K2-LGOA Omni Antenna
description: A small low-gain antenna to receive command signals.<#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Attach two to the main Boruki probe core, one to the left of the dish antenna, and one centered on the top half of the opposite side.</color>

name: bluedog_Kepler_RCS
title: Boruki-K2-HDNT-4 Attitude Control Thruster
description: A small and straightforward RCS quad mounted on a boom, for added leverage and thus higher fuel efficiency. Developed for the Boruki space telescope. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: For Boruki, it attaches to the underside of the probe core, on 4 of the 6 sides (exclude the side with, and opposite, the dish antenna).</color>

name: bluedog_Kepler_Radiator
title: Boruki-K2-FPR Radiator Panel
description: A radially attachable curved radiator panel designed to help dissipate heat into space.

name: bluedog_Kepler_ReactionWheelDouble
title: Boruki-K2-RWA-2 Double Reaction Wheel Assembly
description: Dual reaction-wheel assembly for the Boruki space telescope. Just be sure to bring extras as reaction wheels like these don't have the best reliability track record. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Attach two to the main probe core, on the outside edges of the "top" two sides.</color>

name: bluedog_Kepler_ReactionWheelSingle
title: Boruki-K2-RWA-1 Reaction Wheel
description: One half of the Boruki reaction wheel assembly, for when you just need a little push in the right direction.

name: bluedog_Kepler_SolarPanel
title: Boruki-K2-KPLR37 "Charbonneau" Advanced Exoplanet Transitory Observation Telescope
description: Solar panel assembly developed for the Boruki space telescope. Attached to the probe core. Has an optional foil shroud that conforms to the main telescope part.

name: bluedog_Kepler_Spider
title: Boruki-K2-KPLR37 Telescope CCD Photometer Electronics
description: This is the main scientific instrument for Boruki space telescope. It is an array of CCDs with soft focus designed to precisely measure light emission of distant stars, to detect the minute fluctuations caused when an exoplanet passes in front of the star. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Attach to the inside node of the main telescope part.</color>

name: bluedog_Kepler_StarTracker
title: Boruki-K2-KST2 Advanced Star Tracker
description: Designed for the Boruki Space Telescope, this ultra-precision, lightweight composite star tracker provides additional SAS control modes to probe cores as a result of high-quality positional data. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Place a pair of them on the probe core, directly opposite the dish antenna, one at 90° (pointing away from the antenna), and one at 45° (downwards).</color>

name: bluedog_Kepler_Telescope
title: Boruki-K2-KPLR37 "Charbonneau" Advanced Exoplanet Transitory Observation Telescope
description: Boruki space telescope main mirror assembly. With the proper electronics installed, this advanced telescope can be used to detect and study exoplanets by detecting changes in a distant star's brightness caused by a planetary body transiting its parent star. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Attach the Boruki CCD Photometer instrument to the inside node, and the radiator to the outside.</color>

name: bluedog_LOFTI
title: SR-I "Lofty" Probe Core
description: A tiny satellite built out of a SR-1 "Jekyll" probe core. All of the SIGINT surveillance equipment was removed and replaced with ionospheric measurement equipment and a VLF antenna. It is designed to be launched as a secondary (or tertiary) payload, but it can also be launched by itself. Includes a built in decoupler.

name: bluedog_LunarOrbiter_Antenna
title: Codac-A23 Omni Antenna
description: Our engineers said we needed another omni antenna. Our accountants said why. Our engineers said they needed one that folded sideways. Our accountants said ok.

name: bluedog_LunarOrbiter_Camera
title: Codac-LO-2180 "Eastkan" Film Camera
description: Film cameras are limited in that the film must be returned to Kerbin in order to be developed. In order to get a better idea of what lies further out in space, we have developed this advanced film camera in conjunction with our partner Codac. After exposing the film, it is developed automatically and then transmitted in strips using a primitive photoscanner. A significant amount of detail is lost in this process, so the images aren't as valuable as actually returning the film. The film is stored after development, and can be still be examined if it happens to be returned. Interestingly this camera also features a Geiger counter built into the housing to measure radiation.

name: bluedog_LunarOrbiter_Core
title: Codac-PCT "Kreuznach" Probe Core
description: A unique probe core design, the avionics and control systems are built around a truss structure. The inside of the truss is left open for experiments like cameras. The outer ring can be be fitted with folding solar panels and communications equipment. Typically launched upside down inside a Belle upper stage. The control direction can be reversed to assist with this and can also be changed back in flight.

name: bluedog_LunarOrbiter_Dish
title: Codac-A66 Communications Dish
description: Small, retractable communications dish to provide high gain transmission of scientific information.

name: bluedog_LunarOrbiter_Propulsion
title: Codac-PAD4R "Marquardt" Orbital Propulsion System
description: A small, roughly 0.625m monopropellant powered engine. Contains integrated 4-way RCS for two axis control, and four small bottles of monopropellant.

name: bluedog_LunarOrbiter_Solar_SideMount
title: Codac-MOPP20-S Solar Panel
description: Alternate version of the Codac Solar panel which can fold along the spacecraft sides. Doesn't track the sun.

name: bluedog_LunarOrbiter_Solar_Tracking
title: Codac-MOPP20-T Solar Panel
description: Tracking version of the Codac Solar panel.

name: bluedog_LunarOrbiter_Solar_UnderFold
title: Codac-MOPP20-U Solar Panel
description: Blocky, cheap solar panel with a simple unfold mechanism. Designed to fold underneath the Codac probe. Doesn't track the sun.

name: bluedog_Mariner10_chargedParticleTelescope
title: Argo-10-EPE98 Charged Particles Telescope
description: This experiment is designed to measure energetic electrons, protons, and alpha particles in the interplanetary medium and in the vicinity of planets in low orbit.

name: bluedog_Mariner10_probeCore
title: Argo-10-OPB "Amru" Probe Core
description: The culmination of the Burke and Argo programs, this octagonal probe bus was designed for Argo 10 for the purpose of exploring the inner planets. Features built in thermal controls, a small monopropellant store and a large battery. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Add the Argo-10-CNP44 "Sirius" Precision Star Tracker to your craft to gain additional SAS modes.</color>

name: bluedog_Mariner2_CosmicDustDetector
title: Wayfarer-2-DDS Cosmic Dust Detector
description: Our scientists think space might not be as empty as we once thought. This device contains plates for measuring the impacts of 'micrometeoroids', the little pieces of debris and particles that travel through open vacuum at thousands of meters per second. Measuring the number of impacts gives us an idea of how dangerous an area of space may be for our ships.

name: bluedog_Mariner2_IonTrap
title: Argo-2-ICC Ion Chamber
description: This hemispherical ion trap allows us to sense charged particles that pass through it. That will allow us to measure the radiation from higher-energy particles around the system.

name: bluedog_Mariner2_Radiometer
title: Argo-2-ETS Radiometer
description: This instrument is a combination of a microwave and an infrared radiometer, for analyzing the cloud cover and heat return from a planet.

name: bluedog_Mariner2_Solar_Antenna
title: Argo-2-ASP Folding Solar Panel - Antenna
description: Cheap, primitive solar panel with a simple deployment mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings, but doesn't track the sun. Can be switched from the standard angled fold to a straight vertical storage position. This variant includes a low-powered omni antenna, for ensuring contact with home.

name: bluedog_Mariner2_Solar_Basic
title: Argo-2-BSP Folding Solar Panel
description: Cheap, primitive solar panel with a simple deployment mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings, but doesn't track the sun. Can be switched from the standard angled fold to a straight vertical storage position.

name: bluedog_Mariner2_TrackingSolar_Antenna
title: Argo-2-TASP Tracking Solar Panel - Antenna
description: Cheap, primitive solar panel with a simple deployment mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings and equipped with a rotary joint for tracking the sun. Can be switched from the standard angled fold to a straight vertical storage position. This variant includes a low-powered omni antenna, for ensuring contact with home.

name: bluedog_Mariner2_TrackingSolar_Basic
title: Argo-2-TBSP Tracking Solar Panel
description: Cheap, primitive solar panel with a simple deployment mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings and equipped with a rotary joint for tracking the sun. Can be switched from the standard angled fold to a straight vertical storage position.

name: bluedog_Mariner2_Truss
title: Argo-2-ET Experiment Truss
description: Lightweight truss for mounting instruments, includes a built in magnetometer.

name: bluedog_Mariner3_CanopusSensor
title: Argo-MRNR-340 "Argo Navis-1" Star Tracker
description: A newly designed instrument that is the first of its type, this special sensor is designed to use the star Kanopus as a navigational reference object to help a satellite determine its attitude. Enables an intermediate level of SAS control to the Argo-MRNR "Otto" probe core.

name: bluedog_Mariner3_Solar
title: Argo-MRNR-340 Solar Panel
description: Minor advancements in solar panel technology learned from the Burke program has allowed for a more lightweight, efficient solar panel. Includes a solar pressure vane on the end of the panel to aid stabilization as well as built-in RCS thrusters.

name: bluedog_Mariner3_TV_Camera
title: Argo-MRNR-340-PIXL TV Camera Scan Platform
description: Our engineers were able to design a robust and reliable vidicon TV camera system to take photographs on film, electronically scan it, and send it back to Kerbin. The pictures are broken up into many discrete pieces of data that are each assigned a value pertaining to a grayscale color. One of our engineers referred to these pieces of color data that make up the image as 'pixels'. However, some detail and quality in the pictures is lost when using this transmission system. The vidicon TV camera is mounted on a scan platform that is capable of tracking the body it orbits. Also includes a intertial and temperature simulator experiment.

name: bluedog_Mariner3_TV_Camera_UV
title: Argo-MRNR340-PIXL-UV TV Camera and UV Photometer Scan Platform
description: A tracking TV Camera and UV Photometer scan platform. Orginally supposed to fly on an Argo satellite, electrical problems associated with the UV Photometer were discovered causing it to be removed and swapped for a temperature experiment. This unflown version of the scan platform features the UV Photometer that was originally intended to be used on the platform.

name: bluedog_Mariner5_CanopusSensor
title: Argo-MRNR-500 "Argo Navis-2" Star Tracker
description: A slightly more refined version of the Argo-MRNR-340 "Argo Navis-1" Star Tracker that has a slightly reduced mass. Uses the star Kanopus as a navigational reference object to help a satellite determine its attitude. Enables an intermediate level of SAS control to the Argo-MRNR "Otto" probe core.

name: bluedog_Mariner5_Solar
title: Argo-MRNR-500 "Spoon" Solar Panel
description: We asked our engineers to build a spacecraft on short notice, so they took spare parts from the Argo-MRNR-340 Solar Panel to assemble this solar panel. Includes a temperature reference experiment at the end of the solar panel along with built-in RCS thrusters.

name: bluedog_Mariner5_Solar_Antenna
title: Argo-MRNR-500 Solar Panel - Antenna
description: We asked our engineers to build a spacecraft on short notice, so they took spare parts from the Argo-MRNR-340 Solar Panel to assemble this solar panel. Includes a dual-frequency reciever antenna at the end of the solar panel along with built-in RCS thrusters.

name: bluedog_Mariner5_SunShield
title: Argo-MRNR-500 Sun Shield
description: A small, basic deployable sunshield for the Argo 5 probe. Protects the satellite from solar radiation while exploring the inner planets.

name: bluedog_Mariner69_HighGainAntenna
title: Argo-MRNR-700 High Gain Antenna
description: The Argo 700-series high gain antenna.

name: bluedog_Mariner69_LowGainAntenna
title: Argo-MRNR-700 Low Gain Omni Antenna
description: A simple reliable omnidirectional low gain antenna for the Argo 700-series probes. Attaches to the toggleable LGA node on the probe core.

name: bluedog_Mariner69_ScanPlatform
title: Argo-MRNR-700 Scanning Platform
description: Scan platform for the Argo-700 probe.

name: bluedog_Mariner69_SolarPanel
title: Argo-MRNR-700 "Paddle" Solar Panel
description: Upgraded Argo-series solar panel,for Argo 6/7. This one includes the standard 4-way RCS block on the end.

name: bluedog_Mariner71_HighGainAntenna
title: Argo-MRNR-900 High Gain Antenna
description: A derivative of the Argo 700-series high gain antenna, this dish includes unique mounting hardware to attach it directly to the 900-series' oversized propulsion module. Make sure the louver part below it is set to the correct variant, so that it connects to the lower mounting point.

name: bluedog_Mariner71_LowGainAntenna
title: Argo-MRNR-900 Low Gain Omni Antenna
description: A simple reliable omnidirectional low gain antenna for the Argo 900-series probes. Attaches to the back side of the propulsion module.

name: bluedog_Mariner71_PropulsionModule
title: Argo-MRNR-900 "Flour Sack" Propulsion Module
description: After a number of fly-by missions, our engineers had an epiphany: what if we attempted to orbit another planet? That would provide us with far more scientific opportunities than a single high-speed pass. With this thought in the back of their minds, our team developed the biggest innovation in the history of our robotics program - bigger fuel tanks, and an engine to use them. Includes mounting points for the low and high gain antennas. The star tracker gets tucked in under the side.

name: bluedog_Mariner71_SolarAntenna
title: Argo-MRNR-900 "Scoop" Solar  Antenna
description: When our engineers started work on the 900-series Argo probes, they realized that the large propulsion module mounted on top would prevent mounting the panels in the by-then traditional way. This led to the 900-series' second great innovation: mounting the solar panels on stand-offs. This one includes a conical medium gain antenna, along with the standard 4-way RCS block on the end.

name: bluedog_Mariner71_SolarPanel
title: Argo-MRNR-900 "Oar" Solar Panel
description: When our engineers started work on the 900-series Argo probes, they realized that the large propulsion module mounted on top would prevent mounting the panels in the by-then traditional way. This led to the 900-series' second great innovation: mounting the solar panels on stand-offs. This one includes the standard 4-way RCS block on the end.

name: bluedog_Mariner71_StarTracker
title: Argo-MRNR-700 "Argo Navis-32" Star Tracker
description: A slightly more refined version of the Argo-MRNR-500 "Argo Navis-2" Star Tracker that has a slightly reduced mass. Uses the star Kanopus as a navigational reference object to help a satellite determine its attitude. Enables an advanced level of SAS control to the Argo-MRNR "Otto" probe core.

name: bluedog_MarinerBUpgrade
title: MarinerB Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_MarinerB_Solar
title: Argo-B-LSP Folding Solar Panel
description: Cheap, primitive solar panel with a simple deployment mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings, but doesn't track the sun. Can be switched from the standard angled fold to a straight vertical storage position.

name: bluedog_MarinerB_TrackingSolar
title: Argo-B-TLSP Tracking Solar Panel
description: Cheap, primitive solar panel with a simple deployment mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings and equipped with a rotary joint for tracking the sun. Can be switched from the standard angled fold to a straight vertical storage position.

name: bluedog_MarinerB_Truss
title: Argo-B-LMT Experiment Truss
description: Lightweight truss for mounting instruments, includes a built in magnetometer.

name: bluedog_Mariner_Bus
title: Argo-MRNR "Otto" Probe Core
description: Building on the experience gained from designing the Burke satellite line, engineers were able to develop the standardized, relatively lightweight, and reliable octagonal Argo-JPL "Otto" satellite bus. Built to be as modular as possible, this bus can be used for a vastly wide range of scientific missions in a variety of configurations. Includes batteries and an internal supply of monopropellant. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Add a star-tracker to your craft to gain additional SAS modes.</color>

name: bluedog_Mariner_CosmicDustDetector
title: Argo-MRNR-340 Cosmic Dust Detector
description: Our scientists think space might not be as empty as we once thought. Developed based on the experience learned from the Argo 2 cosmic dust experiment. This device contains plates for measuring the impacts of 'micrometeoroids', the little pieces of debris and particles that travel through open vacuum at thousands of meters per second. Measuring the number of impacts gives us an idea of how dangerous an area of space may be for our ships.

name: bluedog_Mariner_CosmicRayDetector
title: Argo-MRNR-340 Cosmic Ray Detector
description: This instrument holds a compact sensor that is capable of measuring the impact direction and energy spectrum of the alpha particles and protons it comes into contact with.

name: bluedog_Mariner_Decoupler
title: Argo-MRNR-345 "Pagasa" Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A 0.9375m payload separation mechanism specifically designed for early Argo satellites. Includes a small amount of clearance for aft-mounted experiments or solar shades.

name: bluedog_Mariner_Early_HGA
title: Argo-MRNR-345 "Nereid-1" Elliptical High-Gain Antenna
description: Recent advancements in communications technology have allowed engineers to design this robust and effective uniquely shaped elliptical high-gain dish antenna intended for early Argo satellite planetary exploration missions. Its aluminum honeycomb structure allows for it to be lightweight, and the fact its fixed instead of tracking or deployable increases its relability and decreases its cost. The antenna was given an elliptical shape to make up for its inability to track and allows it to have a broader pointing range along the direction of Kerbin's orbital motion. Comes with multiple mounting configurations.

name: bluedog_Mariner_Early_LGA_Mast
title: Argo-MRNR-345 "Dodona-1M" Mast Low-Gain Antenna Helium-Vector Magnetometer
description: Simple, lightweight mast antenna for early Argo satellites that carries a small helium-vector magnetometer. Includes multiple mounting configurations and a toggleable node for the Argo 4 Ionization Chamber experiment.

name: bluedog_Mariner_IonizationChamber
title: Argo-MRNR-340 Ionization Chamber and Geiger Counter
description: A small ionization chamber experiment for the Argo 4 spacecraft based off of Burke hardware that also includes a rudimentary geiger counter. Designed to measure the charged particle and radiation environment around a spacecraft. Desgined to be surface mounted or mounted to the Argo-MRNR-345 "Dodona-1M" Mast.

name: bluedog_Mariner_Louver
title: Argo-MRNR Thermal Control Louver
description: A versatile thermal control louver designed to help regulate the temperature of the Argo satellite series. Cheap and easy to produce, but reliable and effective.

name: bluedog_Mariner_Midcourse_Engine
title: Argo-MRNR-357 "Argus" Midcourse Correction Engine
description: A small monopropellant powered engine with an internal fuel supply, not enough for large orbital maneuvers but sufficient for adjusting an encounter trajectory. Originally based on the Burke satellite engine, this engine has an expanded fuel reserve and a slightly larger range of attitude control. Interestingly, this engine was designed to be mounted on the side of various Argo satellites. Attitude control is accomplished through jet vanes mounted inside the nozzle. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Includes a control point to help use the engine in a side-mounted configuration.</color>

name: bluedog_Mariner_PlasmaProbe
title: Argo-MRNR-345 Solar Plasma Probe
description: This instrument is designed to detect solar wind particles and determine their flow and intensity. Includes a toggleable cover.

name: bluedog_Mariner_TrappedRadiationDetector
title: Argo-MRNR-345 Trapped Radiation Detector
description: This small but advanced instrument is designed to analyze and measure trapped electrons and ions and map planetary radiation belts.

name: bluedog_Mariner_UV_Photometer
title: Argo-MRNR-500-UPM Ultraviolet Photometer
description: Originally intended to fly on the Argo 4 spacecraft, this instrument was removed due to electrical problems and repurposed to fly on the Argo 5 spacecraft. This instrument measures ultraviolet light emissions and reflections to determine the chemical compositions and other properties of observed bodies.

name: bluedog_Mono_SmallSingle
title: HLR-0x5-MPS Monopropellant Tank
description: A small radially attached bottle of Monopropellant. Useful for small probes that need RCS, probably not enough for serious course adjustments.

name: bluedog_Mono_SmallTriple
title: HLR-1r5-MPS Monopropellant Tank Assembly
description: Three small radially attached bottles of Monopropellant. Useful for small probes.

name: bluedog_Mono_SphericalTank
title: HLR-3x-MPS Monopropellant Sphere
description: A small radially attached spherical monopropellant tank.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_BeaconAntenna
title: Aeolus-BATA Beacon and Telemetry Antenna
description: Very low gain but rugged antenna for the later Aeolus satellites. Not useful for transmitting scientific data, but a low electricity way to receive commands and transmit telemetry.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_Decoupler
title: Aeolus-PSM Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A roughly 0.9375m payload separation mechanism specifically designed for the Aeolus probe series, providing room for the experiments mounted to the bottom of the instrument torus.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_EarlyCommandAntenna
title: Aeolus-ECCA RCS/Command Antenna
description: Command and control antenna for the early Aeolus meteorological satellites. Includes built-in six axis RCS thrusters.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_EarlyControlCore
title: Aeolus-LCC "Stratus" Control Core
description: Control core for the early model Aeolus meteorological satellites.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_InstrumentTorus
title: Aeolus-IST Instrument Support Torus
description: Structural torus for mounting instruments for the Aeolus meteorological satellites. Includes supplementary batteries and monopropellant.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_Instrument_ERB
title: Aeolus-PBR Planetary Radiation Budget Instrument
description: This instrument is used for long term measurements of the solar radiation budget of an atmospheric planet. Part one of the Aeolus Multi Instrument Suite - it can be used without either subsequent experiment for reduced science return.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_Instrument_ESMR
title: Aeolus-ESMR Electrically Scanning Microwave Radiometer
description: This instrument is used  for mapping the microwave radiation from a planet's surface. This information is used to measure the water content of clouds, and to observe sea ice. Returns a medium to high amount of science compared to other microwave radiometers.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_Instrument_SAMS
title: Aeolus-SAMS Stratospheric and Mesospheric Sounder
description: This instrument can be used to map the air layers of the atmosphere. Part three of the Aeolus Multi Instrument Suite - it requires the Planetary Radiation Budget and Total Ozone Mapping System experiments, but together their combined returned data will fully map the the primary weather systems of the planet.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_Instrument_SIS
title: Aeolus-SIS Satellite Infrared Spectrometer
description: This instrument is used for measuring the infrared spectrum of a planet, useful for determining the vertical profiles of temperature and water vapor in the atmosphere.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_Instrument_SMMR
title: Aeolus-SMMR Scanning Multichannel Microwave Radiometer
description: This instrument is used for long term measurements of the cloud cover of an atmospheric body. Returns a high amount of science compared to other microwave radiometers.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_Instrument_THIR
title: Aeolus-ITHIR Scanning Infrared Radiometer
description: This instrument can be used to measure the infra-red reflections coming off a planet's surface. Certain IR bands are released from specific chemical processes, which lets scientists infer what sort of activity is occurring on a body.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_Instrument_TOMS
title: Aeolus-TOMS Total Ozone Mapping System
description: This instrument can be used to measure and map the ozone layers of a planet. Part two of the Aeolus Multi Instrument Suite - it requires the Planetary Radiation Budget experiment, but combined the instruments can return more weather data.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_LateCommandAntenna
title: Aeolus-LCCA Command Antenna
description: Command and control antenna for the late model Aeolus meteorological satellites.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_LateControlCore
title: Aeolus-LCC "Cirrus" Control Core
description: Control core for the later model Aeolus meteorological satellites. Includes built-in six axis RCS thrusters.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_PayloadDeck
title: Aeolus-SPD Payload Deck
description: Lightweight structural deck, to get more space for mounting experiments or other radially attached parts. Based on the Aeolus satellite's instrument torus.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_SBandAntenna
title: Aeolus-SBCA S-Band Antenna
description: S-band communications antenna for the Aeolus meteorological satellites. Nominally several are mounted to the bottom of the instrument torus for increased data bandwidth.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_SolarPanel
title: Aeolus-BSP Solar Panel
description: This fold-out, tracking solar panel was originally designed for the Aeolus meteorological satellite series. When placed in 2x symmetry, it will mirror so that both panels fold to one side. This frees up room on the other side of the satellite for mounting taller instruments.

name: bluedog_Nimbus_Truss
title: Aeolus-STS Structural Truss
description: Lightweight truss for the Aeolus meteorological satellite series.

name: bluedog_OAO3_PEP_instrument
title: AOO-WPE "Bentham" Advanced Ultraviolet Telescope
description: This instrument for the improved AOO-3 Roman space telescope contains a single large ultraviolet telescope and three complementary x-ray instruments. Both experiments return more science compared to earlier models  and the telescope can also function as a SENTINEL to detect asteroids.

name: bluedog_OAO3_serviceModule
title: AOO-MPC "Roman 3" Service Module
description: This service module component with opening door panels for the Roman 3 spacecraft provides a lot of mission flexibility. Useful to store extra propellant, batteries, experiments etc.

name: bluedog_OAO_ProbeCore
title: AOO-MPC "Roman" Probe Core
description: Large, versatile, octagonal probe core forming the main bus for the Astronomical Orbital Observatory series of space telescopes. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Add the AOO-STP Precision Star Tracker to your craft to gain additional SAS modes.</color>

name: bluedog_OAO_SAO_instrument
title: AOO-OSA "Smithson" Secondary Telescope
description: Double up your science! This secondary instrument containing four X-Ray telescopes attaches to the "bottom" of the AOO Space Telescope probe core so you can perform observations at both ends of the observatory.

name: bluedog_OAO_WEP_instrument
title: AOO-WPE "Marquette" Ultraviolet Telescope
description: The primary instrument for the early AOO space telescopes, this block contains no fewer than five ultraviolet telescopes and a pair of UV spectrometers for good measure. Can function as a SENTINEL to detect asteroids.

name: bluedog_OAO_antenna
title: AOO-CTR Command Antenna
description: A small antenna to receive command signals.

name: bluedog_OAO_balanceBoom
title: AOO-RBM Balance Boom
description: A small RCS quad mounted on a boom, for added leverage and thus higher fuel efficiency.

name: bluedog_OAO_solarLower
title: AOO-BSP-L Lower Solar Panel
description: Folding fixed solar panel for the AOO series of space obvervatories. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE:  Attach in mirror symmetry to the sides of the AOO-OSA "Smithson" instrument unit. A cut out on the corner of the panel allows for some overlap with the upper solar panel set. </color>

name: bluedog_OAO_solarUpper
title: AOO-BSP-U Upper Solar Panel
description: Folding fixed solar panel for the AOO series of space obvervatories. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE:  Attach in mirror symmetry to the sides of the AOO-WPE "Marquette" unit. A cut out on the corner of the panel allows for some overlap with the lower solar panel set. </color>

name: bluedog_OAO_spacecraftAdapter
title: AOO-XSA 0.9375m to 1.25m Spacecraft Adapter
description: A 0.9375m to 1.255m payload adapter with built in decoupler. For when you need to attach a spacecraft larger than the stage below it.

name: bluedog_OAO_starTracker
title: AOO-STP Precision Star Tracker
description: The product of extensive development in order to provide the required pointing accuracy for the Astromical Orbital Observatory program, this high precision star tracker provides additional SAS control modes to probe cores as a result of high quality positional data.

name: bluedog_OFO_Antenna
title: OTLTH-A Communications Antenna
description: A small triple-boom mounted antenna.

name: bluedog_OFO_Experiment
title: OTLTH-E Space Adaptation Experiment
description: This small self contained laboratory can measure the adaptation of small, primitive organisms to a microgravity environment over an extended time. Originally used with a MIP probe core. Data gathered can be transmitted but the science returns will be lower than a dedicated recoverable experiment such as the Bion probe adapter.

name: bluedog_OGO_Adapter
title: HLR-OOG 0.9375m to 0.625m Payload Adapter
description: A 0.9375m to 0.625m payload adapter with built in decoupler.

name: bluedog_OGO_Bus
title: HLR-OOG "Sansisco" Probe Core
description: Medium sized, rectangular probe bus for scientific and commercial satellites, originally design for our geophysical research satellite series. Includes the standard loadout of control processors, batteries, and other essential equipment.

name: bluedog_OGO_ExperimentBoom_1
title: HLR-OOG-EP4 Ionization and Electrostatic Analysis Boom
description: Sophisticated instrument used for gathering Electrostatic data from Auroral particles and other sources.

name: bluedog_OGO_ExperimentBoom_2
title: HLR-OOG-EP2 Gravimetric Scanner
description: This advanced instrument can map the gravitational fields of planetary bodies.

name: bluedog_OGO_ExperimentBoom_3
title: HLR-OOG-EP1 Ion Trap Boom
description: This instrument can trap charged particles that pass through it. That will allow us to measure the solar wind around the system.

name: bluedog_OGO_HighGainAntenna
title: HLR-OOG High Gain Antenna
description: Compact but powerful high gain antenna.

name: bluedog_OGO_LongBoom_Ball
title: HLR-OOG-EP6 Gamma Ray Spectrometer
description: We are not sure why our scientists wanted a Gamma Ray Spectrometer before an Alpha or a Beta one but here it is! The instrument is particularly sensitive to the Hydrogen spectrum in order to locate water.

name: bluedog_OGO_LongBoom_Hoop
title: HLR-OOG-EP5 Folding Magnetometer Boom
description: This interestingly shaped hoop magnetometer is designed to study magnetohydrodynamic waves and other magnetic field structures in orbit.

name: bluedog_OGO_OPEP
title: HLR-OOG-OPEP Science Instrument
description: This science container contains a mass spectrometer that can be used used to analyze the composition of atmospheres and surfaces from orbit, as well as a cosmic ray telescope that can detect solar and galactic cosmic radiation.

name: bluedog_OGO_RCS
title: HLR-OOG Attitude Control Thruster
description: Tiny 3-way RCS thrusters on a fixed boom originally designed for the HLR-OOG Sansico probe. A pair placed on one end of the bus is enough to give sufficient control authority. But we're sure you can find other uses for this.

name: bluedog_OGO_SolarPanel_Antenna
title: HLR-OOG-RPWS Solar Panel
description: Medium sized folding solar panel with sun tracking and a Radio Plasma Wave Science experiment built in.

name: bluedog_OGO_SolarPanel_Basic
title: HLR-OOG Solar Panel
description: Medium sized folding solar panel with sun tracking.

name: bluedog_OSO_Arm
title: SOO-ARM Actuating Reaction Member
description: A small RCS quad mounted on a boom, for added leverage and thus higher fuel efficiency. Also has a small antenna built into the bottom.

name: bluedog_OSO_Core
title: SOO-NON Probe Core
description: Standard 0.625m probe core. Has 9 sides, yes, really.

name: bluedog_OSO_Experiment
title: SOO-SEP Solar Experiment Package
description: Centerpiece of the Solar Orbiting Observatory series of probes. This standalone version has the solar panel removed. The experiment package is designed to track the sun, making sure that it keeps the various experiments pointed at Kerbol. (Author's note - the solar panel module is a workaround to let the standalone version of the experiment track the sun)

name: bluedog_OSO_Photometer
title: SOO-PPE Photopolarimeter Experiment
description: A simple photometric experiment used to measure the intensity of light levels.

name: bluedog_OSO_Sail
title: SOO-SES Solar Experiment Sail
description: Centerpiece of the Solar Orbiting Observatory series of probes. This large sail shaped photovoltaic panel contains a large, sophisticated package of solar experiments. The panel and the experiment package are designed to track the sun, making sure that it both provides power and gives the experiments a clear view of Kerbol.

name: bluedog_OV1_10_LymanAlphaPhotometer
title: LVO1-LA3 Lyman-Alpha UV Photometer
description: Telescope used to measure the UV spectrum of a body.

name: bluedog_OV1_10_Xray_spectrometer
title: LVO-1XSG X-ray Spectrometer
description: This experiment is designed to detect X-ray fluorescence and alpha particles both in deep space and in orbit around planetary bodies.

name: bluedog_OV1_10_magnetometer
title: LVO1-GXM Gravity Gradient Stabilized Magnetometer
description: This rollout magnetometer features 4 supplementary gravity gradient stabilisation booms. Requires the supplementary LV01-GXM-2 boom to be present on the craft to function (preferably on the opposite side).

name: bluedog_OV1_10_magnetometer2
title: LVO1-GXM-2 Gravity Gradient Stabilized Magnetometer
description: This rollout magnetometer cannot function on its own. However it works together as a package with the LVO1-GXM. Place on the same craft on the opposite side.

name: bluedog_OV1_10_probeCore
title: LVO1-10 "Limpet-10" Probe Core
description: Simple pill shaped probe core designed to be piggybacked on Bossart rockets. Features cutouts for science instruments.

name: bluedog_OV1_1_probeCore
title: LVO1-1 "Limpet-1" Probe Core
description: Simple pill shaped probe core designed to be piggybacked on Bossart rockets. This probe is not stabilized.

name: bluedog_OV1_propulsionKit
title: LVO1 Propulsion Kit
description: This capable readymade kit can be used to add 3-axis control, comms and a set of small monopropellant thrusters to the Staara "Aquilae" kick motor. It also includes a decoupler to deploy LVO1 series "Limpet" probes.

name: bluedog_POPPY1
title: P-20 "Tulip-1" Probe Core
description: An extended version of the SR-1 "Jekyll" probe core. The P-20 "Tulip-1" pushes this design to its maximum intelligence collection capabilities. Unlike its previous incarnations, the fact this satellite is a SIGINT/ELINT reconnaissance satellite is no longer secret. It is designed to be launched as a secondary (or tertiary) payload, but it can also be launched by itself. Includes a built in decoupler as well as antennas.

name: bluedog_POPPY2
title: P-24 "Tulip-2" Probe Core
description: A small satellite that is an evolution of the P-20 "Tulip-1" design. Features a larger profile, more solar panels, and more advanced SIGINT/ELINT reconnaissance technology. Despite intended to be launched 4 at a time on a Belle-D, the P-24 "Tulip-2" can also be launched by itself. Features an upper node where an optional thruster control block can be added for control and orbital adjustment. Includes a built in decoupler and internal antenna.

name: bluedog_POPPY2_RCS
title: P-24 Control Block
description: A small ammonia micro-thruster control block.

name: bluedog_POPPY2_RCS_Antenna
title: P-24 Control Block and Antenna
description: A small ammonia micro-thruster control block with an antenna.

name: bluedog_POPPY_Antenna
title: P-24 Omni Antenna
description: A small extending antenna for the P-24 "Tulip-2" satellite.

name: bluedog_Pioneer5_Core
title: Pilgrim-P5 "Hajj" Probe Core
description: This probe is a scaled down version of Pilgrim-P3E6. While being much smaller and lighter, it is far less complex and does not have an engine. Includes a rudimentary micrometeorite detector, ionization chamber, and geiger mullen-tube.

name: bluedog_Pioneer5_SolarPaddle
title: Pilgrim-P5-TSP Solar Paddle
description: This small solar panel is spring loaded to extend on command. It is capable of rotating to track the sun.

name: bluedog_Pioneer6_Bus
title: Pilgrim-PIO6E-CCB "Kohoutek" Probe Core
description: Versatile, drum shaped probe core with room on top for instruments and antennas, and a ring of solar panels around its sides. Includes an integrated cosmic ray telescope.

name: bluedog_Pioneer6_IonSensor
title: Pilgrim-PIO6E-ITE Folding Ion Trap Boom
description: A pair of hemispherical ion traps on a boom, to keep them away from the spacecraft.

name: bluedog_Pioneer6_Magnetometer
title: Pilgrim-PIO6E-MAG Folding Magnetometer Boom
description: A smaller magnetometer boom, with a slightly lower scientific return.

name: bluedog_Pioneer6_MainAntenna
title: Pilgrim-PIO6E-PWD Communications Antenna
description: Simple, lightweight mast antenna.

name: bluedog_Pioneer6_MidcourseEngine
title: Pilgrim-PIO6E-MCE "Mickel" Midcourse Correction Engine
description: Weak monoprop engine meant to help refine a probe's flyby, comes with a small propellant bottle attached. Never used on the Pilgrim 6 probes as flown, but proposed - one wonders how precise their heliocentric trajectory needed to be.

name: bluedog_Pioneer6_RCS
title: Pilgrim-PIO6E-PAT Folding RCS Boom
description: A small RCS quad mounted on a boom, for added leverage and thus higher fuel efficiency.

name: bluedog_Pioneer6_ServiceModule
title: Pilgrim-PIO6E-PSM Service Module
description: A 0.625m drum covered in solar panels, containing some batteries, a small monopropellant bottle, and space for an engine or some experiments. Has an alternate node to connect to the 0.625m ring on the bottom.

name: bluedog_Pioneer6_StanfordAntenna
title: Pilgrim-PIO6E-SEA Communications Antenna
description: Simple, lightweight deployable antenna. Mounts to the bottom rim of the PIO6E service module, and folds up along the side of the probe until deployed.

name: bluedog_PioneerAble_Adapter
title: Bossart-SAA 0.9375m Interstage
description: A small, 0.9375m to 0.9375m extension interstage originally designed to attach an Alpha upper stage to the Bossart rocket. There's no getting around it, its going to look weird.

name: bluedog_PioneerAble_Antenna
title: Pilgrim-P3-VLFA Antenna
description: A small, fixed whip antenna for the Pilgrim P3 probe.

name: bluedog_PioneerAble_Core
title: Pilgrim-P3E6 "Pog" Probe Core
description: This probe core includes a first generation SAS system, some big batteries and is instrumented with radiation and micrometeorite impact experiments. Despite massively overengineered and expensive, it's fairly advanced and capable for when it was developed. It also includes a retrograde facing monopropellant thruster, though curiously it doesn't include any fuel...

name: bluedog_PioneerAble_Engine
title: Pilgrim-P3-MCE "Taber" Course Correction System
description: One of the first pure vacuum engines ever invented, the "Taber" includes a supply of monopropellant suitable for low-energy orbital insertions and course corrections. Normally mounted inside the Pilgrim P3 probe bus, there is an optional top attachment point that enables it to be used externally with other spacecraft.

name: bluedog_PioneerAble_SolarPaddle
title: Pilgrim-P3-TSP Solar Paddle
description: This small solar panel is spring loaded to extend on command. It is capable of rotating to track the sun.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_1
title: Pilgrim-P1 "Ramo" Probe Core
description: This 0.3125m probe core integrates an omni antenna and geiger counter for measuring radation. Designed to be flung hopefully at the Mun, it has an integrated retro motor to help capture it into orbit. Without any onboard power generation it is strongly suggested to hibernate the probe between maneuvers to reduce power consumption. It features BDB's SafeSolid™ system, allowing the engine to be shut down in flight, allowing for more accurate orbital insertions and maneuvers.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_4
title: Pilgrim-P4 "Amba" Probe Core
description: This 0.3125m probe core integrates an omni antenna and a low fidelity film camera. Although designed for a Munar flyby, it does not have onboard power generation. It is strongly recommended to hibernate the probe between maneuvers to reduce power consumption.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_AMD
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-AMD "Orpheus" Asteroid Detector
description: This experiment contains four non-imaging telescopes with photomultipliers designed to spot dust particles or larger asteroids.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_AftAdapter
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F Aft Adapter
description: This structural adapter is designed to provide an interface for the Pilgrim-PNR10F "Allen" Probe Core to be mated to a launch vehicle. Includes louvers for thermal control.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_AftAdapterAlternate
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F Aft Adapter (Alternate)
description: This structural adapter is designed to provide an interface for the Pilgrim-PNR10F "Allen" Probe Core to be mated to a launch vehicle. This version does not include louvers.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_CPD
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-CPI Charged Particle Detector
description: A small charged particle experiment designed to detect energetic electrons, protons, and alpha particles in both planetary and interplanetary regions.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_CRT
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-CCC Cosmic Ray Telescope
description: A small instrument that analyzes the composition and energy of cosmic ray particles.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_Decoupler
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A 0.3125m payload separation mechanism specifically designed to mate the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft to a Staara-37FNV Solid Rocket Motor.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_ExperimentBus
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-EXP Experiment Payload Bay
description: This squashed hexagonal lightweight container was designed with the purpose of being used as an extension to the Pilgrim-PNR10F "Allen" Probe Core. Small cutouts are marked in the bay for placement of experiments or other equipment.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_ExtensionBus
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X Extension Bay
description: This compartment was designed with the purpose of being used as an extension to the Pilgrim-PNR10F "Allen" Probe Core. Designed as part of the PNR10X program, a series of proposals involving extending the lifespan of Pilgrim-PNR10 satellites and repurposing this hardware for new missions. It houses a small supply of monopropellant and an integrated battery. Can also be used as a platform for mounting equipment.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_GeigerTube
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-GTT Geiger Tube
description: This experiment is designed to measure the intensity of ionizing radiation in the surrounding environment.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_HGA
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-RFLCTR27 High Gain Antenna
description: A large high gain dish antenna (and medium gain antenna) designed for the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft that is very light for its size. Great at transmitting at vast distances at the cost of transmission speed. Includes integrated RCS thrusters and two sun sensors that gives a small amount of SAS control. Equipped with several aft-mounted micrometeorite detection panels.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_HGA_Alternate
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-RFLCTR27 High Gain Antenna (Alternate)
description: A large high gain dish antenna (and medium gain antenna) designed for the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft that is very light for its size. Great at transmitting at vast distances at the cost of transmission speed. Does NOT include integrated RCS thrusters and sun sensors. Equipped with several aft-mounted micrometeorite detection panels.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_IPP
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-IPP Imaging Photopolarimeter
description: A small photopolarimeter imaging system intended for use with spin-stabilized spacecraft and designed for the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft. Unlike traditional TV camera imaging, this instrument does not have a vidicon tube, and instead uses spin-scan imaging techniques. It can also preform photopolarimetric observations in addition to imaging. While it doesn't take the best images, it is a pretty effective photometer. Includes both a basic imaging experiment and a photopolarimeter experiment.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_InfraredRadiometer
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-IRE Infrared Radiometer
description: This instrument analyzes the infrared radiation being reflected off a body. This data can be used to analyze a planet or moon's heat output and weather systems.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_LGA
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-SBLGA Low Gain Omni Antenna
description: A small, fixed omnidirectional s-band low gain antenna. Designed for the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft, this antenna is designed to communicate with ground stations during launch and the beginning of the its cruise period. While designed as a secondary antenna, this antenna could be used for any number of applications, including as a primary antenna.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_LargeLouver
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X Large Thermal Control Louver
description: A larger thermal control louver designed for the Pilgrim-PNR10X mission proposals.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_MLS
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X-MLS Multispectral Line Scan Camera
description: This advanced instrument developed for the proposed Pilgrim-PNR10X follow-up missions to the Pilgrim-PNR10F missions is designed to take multispectral line-scan images.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_Magnetometer
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-HVM Helium Vector Magnetometer
description: This instrument designed for the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft is used to analyze and map planetary and interplanetary magnetic fields. Includes a toggleable counterweight at the end of the boom to aid in balancing the center of mass for proposed follow-up missions.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_MediumLouver
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F Medium Thermal Control Louver
description: A medium-sized thermal control for the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft. Intended to be placed in pairs on the aft side of the Pilgrim-PNR10F-EXP Experiment Payload Bay.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_OrbiterPropulsionUnit
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X-OPO Propulsion System
description: Using lessons learned from the Codac-PAD4R "Marquardt" Orbital Propulsion System, engineers at Bluedog Design Bureau have developed an advanced monopropellant-fueled propulsion system for Pilgrim-PNR10X mission proposals. Could be useful for constructing outer solar system orbiter missions. Includes aft-mounted thermal control louvers as well as a toggleable micrometeorite shield.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_OrbiterScanner
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X-LSS Line-Scan Imaging Science Platform
description: This advanced science system designed for one of the Pilgrim-PNR10X mission proposals incorporates the Pilgrim-PNR10F-IRE Infrared Radiometer and the Pilgrim-PNR10F-UVP Ultraviolet Photometer along with a new advanced vidicon camera imaging system to create a multi-mode line-scan imaging system intended for planetary missions.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_PlasmaAnalyzer
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-QPA Quadrispherical Solar Plasma Analyzer
description: This instrument is designed to detect solar wind particles originating from Kerbol for the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft. Intended to be mounted on top of the Pilgrim-PNR10F-EXP Experiment Payload Bay and peer through a hole in the Pilgrim-PNR10F-RFLCTR27 High Gain Antenna's dish.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_Probe
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X-APP "Caelus" Atmospheric Entry Probe
description: A somewhat primitive yet highly robust atmospheric entry probe intended to probe the atmospheres of gas giants. Designed for one of the Pilgrim-PNR10X mission proposals. Includes batteries, reaction wheels, probe core control, and rudimentary temperature and pressure sensors. Also has an integrated atmospheric experiment package in the probe's nose section equipped with a small photometer and a quadrupole mass spectrometer. However, this probe can not transmit data; it has an upper mount under the upper heatshield designed to accommodate an antenna. The upper and lower heatshields are designed to be jettisoned after atmospheric entry so data collection and transmission can begin. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: We do not recommend turning on automatic jettison, as this will cause the heatshields to be ejected during launch.</color>

name: bluedog_Pioneer_ProbeAdapter
title: DS-P10P 0.625m Tall Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A relatively tall 0.625m payload separation mechanism that was originally designed for mating Staara-37 Solid Rocket Motors to payloads on Daleth rockets. The extra height can house the top half of the Staara-37, and the extra height can also fit some aft-mounted equipment on your payload. Also used with one of the Pilgrim-PNR10X mission proposals where it is used to mate the Pilgrim-PNR10X spacecraft to a Staara-37FNV Solid Rocket Motor.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_ProbeAntenna
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X-APTA Atmospheric Entry Probe Telemetry Antenna
description: This robust and reliable telemetry antenna is designed to send telemetry and experiment data from the Pilgrim-PNR10X-APP "Caelus" Atmospheric Entry Probe back to the Pilgrim-PNR10X spacecraft. This antenna is optimized to send data with minimum electricity usage at the cost of longer transmission times.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_ProbeCore
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F "Allen" Probe Core
description: Breakthroughs in materials and manufacturing have allowed engineers to design a super lightweight hexagonal satellite bus for cheap that can take exploration to new heights. Modular in design, this core is designed with slots to accommodate various expansions like control systems, electrical systems, thermal control systems, experiment bays, and more. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Add the Pilgrim-PNR10F-SRA Kanopus Tracker to your craft to gain additional SAS modes.</color>

name: bluedog_Pioneer_ProbeDecoupler
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X-PSA Atmospheric Entry Probe Adapter
description: A 0.625m adapter designed for a Pilgrim-PNR10X mission proposal. Purely designed to house the Pilgrim-PNR10X-APP "Caelus" Atmospheric Entry Probe while enroute to its destination. Includes an internal separation mechanism designed to eject the probe to prepare it for entry. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: The decoupler is not on the upper or lower nodes of the adapter, the decoupler is attached to the middle node inside the adapter and can only separate payloads attached to this node.</color>

name: bluedog_Pioneer_ProbeExperiment
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X-AEPE Atmospheric Experiment Package
description: A standalone version of the atmospheric experiment package integrated into the Pilgrim-PNR10X-APP "Caelus" Atmospheric Entry Probe. This small (but heavier than it looks) experiment package contains a small photometer and a quadrupole mass spectrometer.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_Radiator
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F Shunt Radiator
description: A small shunt radiator designed for the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft to aid in maintaining thermal control.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_RelayAntenna
title: Pilgrim-PNR10X-PRA Relay Antenna
description: Engineers at Bluedog Design Bureau took the Pilgrim-PNR10F-SBLGA Low Gain Omni Antenna, added a ground plate and other equipment to upgrade its capabilities so it can serve as a short-range relay antenna. Designed for missions involving the Pilgrim-PNR10X-APP "Caelus" Atmospheric Entry Probe, this antenna can achieve a link with the atmospheric entry probe so the Pilgrim-PNR10X spacecraft can relay it back to Kerbin.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_SNAP19
title: PB-PANS-19P Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
description: A pair of radioisotope electric generators intended for deep space missions, specifically designed for the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft. The RTG is mounted on three extending rods so that the radiation being emitted from these generators does not damage or interfere with spacecraft electronics. This RTG can be upgraded by adding a third PB-PANS-19 unit to extend the operating life of the Pilgrim-PNR10 spacecraft as used in the Pilgrim-PNR10X mission proposals.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_SmallLouver
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F Small Thermal Control Louver
description: A standalone version of the small thermal control louver from the Pilgrim-PNR10F Aft Adapter.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_StellarReferenceAssembly
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-SRA Kanopus Tracker
description: A lightweight star tracker designed to use the star Kanopus as a reference point. Even though to designed help track the position, attitude, and spin of the Pilgrim-PNR10F spacecraft, this star tracker can be used to provide additional SAS control modes to other probe cores as well.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_TRD
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-JTR Trapped Radiation Detector
description: This small but advanced instrument is designed to analyze and measure trapped electrons and ions and map planetary radiation belts.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_UltravioletPhotometer
title: Pilgrim-PNR10F-UVP Ultraviolet Photometer
description: This tiny, basic instrument analyzes ultraviolet light emissions and reflections to determine the chemical compositions of observed bodies.

name: bluedog_Pioneer_VernierSolids
title: Pilgrim-P1-008 "Wally" Solid Rocket Booster
description: Set of 8 extremely small rocket boosters on a 0.125m mount. Only really useful for putting distance between a probe and it's mother craft. The motors may or may not have been stolen from a model rocket kit belonging to a BDB engineer's offspring. It features BDB's SafeSolid™ system, allowing the engine to be shut down in flight, and since it's a cluster of engines, restarted again, allowing for more accurate orbital insertions and maneuvers. Not that you'll have much time to activate it.

name: bluedog_ProbeRCS
title: HLR-RT Attitude Control Thruster
description: Probe sized RCS cluster, includes many layout variants.

name: bluedog_RAE_DipoleAntenna
title: REI-ESDA Electric Field Dipole Antenna
description: A dipole antenna designed for the REI spacecraft specifically configured to take measurements of the local electric field.

name: bluedog_RAE_MotorDecoupler
title: REI-S17 Solid Rocket Motor Decoupler
description: A small 0.3125m decoupler designed specifically for separating the Staara-17 solid rocket motor from the REI "Helix" Probe Core.

name: bluedog_RAE_ProbeCore
title: REI "Helix" Probe Core
description: This is the core of REI (Radio Exploratory Investigator), a satellite designed to conduct radio astronomy observations. This core might be small, but it's actually quite capable (and somewhat heavy) for its size. Includes a small magnetic stabilization system, SAS capabilities, and electric charge. While orginally intended to be a Kerbin-orbiting satellite, this satellite can be upgraded to hold a small amount of monopropellant to make it capable of Munar operations.

name: bluedog_RAE_RCS
title: REI-ACS2 RCS Boom
description: An RCS block mounted on a small boom, for added leverage and thus higher fuel efficiency. Intended to give additional attitude control to the REI-B satellite so it would be able to conduct missions in Munar orbit.

name: bluedog_RAE_RadioAntenna
title: REI-RBR1500 Radio Astronomy V-Antenna
description: An ultra-long antenna designed for radio astronomy signal collection for the REI spacecraft. The antenna is tightly wound into a coil which is deployed by a motor driven system. This antenna includes a variant for surface attachment as well as a variant for mount attachment.

name: bluedog_RAE_SolarPaddle
title: REI "Ginkgo" Double-Sided Solar Paddle
description: An tiny and strange double-sided oddly shaped solar paddle. Originally intended for the REI line of satellites, this fan-shaped solar is curved so that it can wrap around the cylindrical REI "Helix" Probe Core while keeping a small radial profile. While the solar panel is intended to be used in sets of four, angled at 28.5° for maximum solar coverage regardless of the direction the spacecraft is facing, this solar panel comes with a straight variant as well. Used on the Explorer 38 and 49.

name: bluedog_RAE_TelemetryAntenna
title: REI-CDTSA Telemetry Antenna
description: A small, fixed telemetry antenna for the REI probe series. Includes two length variants.

name: bluedog_RAE_TrackingSolarPaddle
title: REI "Ginkgo" Tracking Solar Paddle
description: An extremely peculiar and small double sided solar panel. Folds up for storage in fairings, but doesn't track the sun. This solar panel comes in a variety of sizes depending on electrical needs. Folds out at a 45 degree angle and includes a dipole telemetry antenna for maintaining ground communication.

name: bluedog_RAE_VCPS
title: REI-MCS Velocity Correction Propulsion System
description: Upon discovering that radio noise from Kerbin can interfere with radio astronomy observations, engineers set out to find a way to enable the REI-B satellite to preform its radio astronomy observations from Munar orbit. This small 0.3125m package contains two tiny monopropellant-fueled engines and four monopropellant tanks. This system can be used to help correct and refine the orbit of the REI spacecraft after Munar insertion. While it was originally designed for REI, it can be used for any number of applications.

name: bluedog_RAE_VCPS_Decoupler
title: REI-MCS-DU Decoupler
description: A small 0.3125m decoupler designed specifically for separating the REI-MCS Velocity Correction Propulsion System from the REI-B spacecraft after a desirable Munar orbit is achieved. Decouples from the upper node.

name: bluedog_RTG_GPHS
title: PB-GPHS Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
description: A small, modular radioisotope thermoelectric generator. Suitable for use in probes where solar panels are unusable. The cutting edge in RTG technology, this RTG is highly versatile and perfect for a wide variety of applications.

name: bluedog_RTG_MHWRTG
title: PB-MHW Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
description: A small, modular radioisotope thermoelectric generator. Suitable for use in probes where solar panels are unusable. This RTG was developed to be perfect for long-duration, deep-space missions.

name: bluedog_RTG_RHU
title: PB-TNY-CT Radioisotope Heater Unit
description: A tiny pellet of plutonium used to keep electronics warm. Produces a very small amount of power.

name: bluedog_RTG_SNAP19
title: PB-PANS-19 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
description: A small, modular electric generator.

name: bluedog_RTG_SNAP19_Nimbus
title: PB-PANS-19N Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
description: A double stack of PANS-19 RTGs in a peculiar angled mount.

name: bluedog_RTG_SNAP19_Quad
title: PB-PANS-19Q Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
description: Four PANS-19 RTGs mounted on a truss. The arm swings out, to get the RTGs further away from the spacecraft's systems and instruments.

name: bluedog_RTG_SNAP3
title: PB-PANS-3 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
description: A tiny RTG for providing a trickle of keep-alive power for spacecraft.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Battery
title: Burke-ZAP Rechargeable Battery Pack
description: Small capacity radial battery for probes. The white dust cover is meant to face out to protect the part - not the black battery. It will last you long enough to reach, say, the Mun. (Note: Warranty void if used inside Mun's SOI)

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block1_ElectroAnalyzer_Device1
title: Burke-1-EDA1 Electrostatic Analyzer Device 1
description: One of the two devices required for the electrostatic analyzer experiment to function.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block1_ElectroAnalyzer_Device2
title: Burke-1-EDA2 Electrostatic Analyzer Device 2
description: One of the two devices required for the electrostatic analyzer experiment to function.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block1_ElectroAnalyzer_Experiment
title: Burke-1-EIA Electrostatic Analyzer Experiment
description: Sophisticated instrument used for gathering Electrostatic data. Requires both the separate "Electrostatic Analyzer Devices 1 & 2" to be on board the vessel to function.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block1_LymanAlphaTelescope
title: Burke-1-LMT Lyman-Alpha UV Telescope
description: Telescope used to measure the UV spectrum of a body.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block1_Truss
title: Burke-1-RMT Experiment Truss
description: Truss for mounting instruments, includes a built in magnetometer and ion trap.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block2_GammaRaySpectrometer
title: Burke-2-GRSP Gamma Ray Spectrometer
description: We are not sure why our scientists wanted a Gamma Ray Spectrometer before an Alpha or a Beta one but here it is! The instrument is particularly sensitive to the Hydrogen spectrum in order to locate water.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block2_OmniAntenna
title: Burke-2-61-P Omni Antenna
description: This uniquely shaped low-gain omni antenna is designed to go over the rough lander in the Burke Block 2 probes. Make sure you deploy it before you release the probe!

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block2_RadarAltimeter
title: Burke-2-RAD Radar Altimeter
description: This experimental radar altimeter dish can be used to map the surface height of the planet below. Needs to be deployed before use.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block2_RetroDecoupler
title: Burke-2-RMD 0.3125m Decoupler
description: A 0.3125m decoupler specifically designed to decouple the Burke Block 2 rough lander just prior to impact. It's also useful in general as a payload decoupler.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block2_RoughLander
title: Burke-2-RLP Rough Landing Probe
description: This "rough lander" is designed to be attached to a Staara-10-LYC "Aethra" solid motor. Fired retro just before impact aboard a lunar impactor, if all goes well it should be brought to a nearly complete stop before landing, more or less intact, on the surface. Once there it has a simple seismometer experiment that can be transmitted back home.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block2_TVCamera
title: Burke-2-VTS Television Camera
description: A simple television camera system for relaying images back home. The quality of data gathered is worse than a regular camera but all of the data collected can be transmitted.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Block3_TVSystem
title: Burke-3-RCA Television Camera System
description: This conical structure contains six television cameras and the associated hardware for rapidly processing them for transmission home.  The quality of data gathered is worse than a regular camera but all of the data collected can be transmitted.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Bus
title: Burke-HKS "Rorat" Probe Bus
description: Sturdy hexagonal probe core with integrated trusses, for attaching things such as solar panels and instruments. It includes storage for monopropellant fuel, for use with the included attitude control thrusters or small engines. Unfortunately this didn't leave space for any batteries - don't forget to attach them! Includes a bare probe core variant, and a double stacked version for Argo-B-DSPB is also unloackable.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Decoupler
title: Burke-WTD Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A 0.625m payload separation mechanism specifically designed for the Burke probe series, providing room for the high gain dish to be folded underneath.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Dish
title: Burke-OVBR-1 Communications Dish
description: This communications dish might be a little bit heavy, and hard to fit into a fairing, but it's the best we'll be able to provide for the time being. By default it folds underneath what it is attached to, but it can be switched to fold upwards.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Engine
title: Burke-MP829 "Groudle" Midcourse Correction Engine
description: A small monopropellant powered engine with an internal fuel supply, not enough for large orbital maneuvers but sufficient for adjusting an encounter trajectory. Designed to be mounted up inside the spacecraft bus. Attitude control is accomplished through jet vanes mounted inside the nozzle.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Lander_Antenna
title: Burke-L-6TP1 Antenna
description: A combination of a high gain dish and a low gain omni antenna.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Lander_Leg
title: Burke-L-LSL Landing Leg
description: We crashed a bunch of Burke probes into the Mun when someone had the bright idea to maybe put some landing legs and a more powerful propulsion system on one. These tiny legs will enable you to convert a Burke probe core into a soft lander.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Lander_Propulsion
title: Burke-L-TDPS Terminal Propulsion System
description: Descent propulsion for the Burke-L Lander Prototype. Use a solid motor to reduce most of the speed, and these for your final touchdown.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Lander_Solar_Fixed
title: Burke-FSSP Folding Solar Panel
description: Cheap solar panel with a simple unfold mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings. Doesn't track the sun.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Lander_Solar_Tracking
title: Burke-FSSPT Folding Tracking Solar Panel
description: Cheap solar panel with a simple unfold mechanism, mounted on a servo to track the sun. Folds up for storage in fairings.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Lander_Truss
title: Burke-L-STT Structural Truss
description: Lightweight truss for mounting instruments and other necessities. Contains some batteries.

name: bluedog_Ranger_OmniAntenna
title: Burke-A27-C Antenna
description: Tired of long antennas? This one comes coiled up in a cylinder! The overall length is kept down, but weighs slightly more as a result.

name: bluedog_Ranger_PayloadDeck
title: Burke-SPD Payload Deck
description: Lightweight structural deck, to get more space for mounting experiments or other radially attached parts.

name: bluedog_Ranger_Solar
title: Burke-17-ZOID Folding Solar Panel
description: Large, cheap solar panel with a simple unfold mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings. Doesn't track the sun.

name: bluedog_Ranger_TrackingSolar
title: Burke-17-ZOIDT Tracking Solar Panel
description: Large, cheap solar panel with a simple unfold mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings, and is equipped with a rotary joint for tracking the sun.

name: bluedog_Relay_Antenna
title: JPR1-62BU1 Biconical Horn Antenna
description: This lightweight communications antenna provides omnidirectional coverage for relaying signals.

name: bluedog_Relay_Core
title: JPR1-2677 "Repeater" Communications Satellite
description: Primitive, spin stabilized bus designed to be used as an early communications satellite. The whip antennas on the bottom are for telemetry - attach an antenna to the top for use as a relay.

name: bluedog_SOLRAD
title: SR-1 "Jekyll" Probe Core
description: A tiny satellite that evolved from the Easton-V3 probe core. Small and unassuming, the SR-1 is presented to the public as a scientific satellite to study solar x-rays. However this is a cover for its classified primary mission, to intercept signals from the Krussians. It is designed to be launched as a secondary (or tertiary) payload, but it can also be launched by itself. Includes a built in decoupler as well as antennas.

name: bluedog_SOLRAD8
title: SR-8 "Kreplin" Probe Core
description: An extended version of the SR-1 "Jekyll" probe core. This is a purely scientific satellite, possessing none of the reconnaissance equipment that SR-1 used. Includes experiments to study solar UV and X-Ray emissions, along with other solar activity. This satellite pushes this probe design's scientific capabilities to its limits. That being said, the large amount of experiments on this satellite comes at the cost of science value. It is designed to be launched as a secondary (or tertiary) payload, but it can also be launched by itself. Includes a built in decoupler as well as antennas.

name: bluedog_SmallKlaw
title: KMAC-23-5 "Klaw" 0.625m Grapple Unit
description: Engineers at Bluedog Design Bureau found some old blueprints for some kind of over-engineered grabbing device in the dumpster behind a competitor. These documents were studied and revised, and then subsequently thrown in the dumpster again. Later an intern found the discarded designs and they were finally adapted to make a sleek 0.625m grapple unit that can be used for all sorts of applications. While originally solely created for asteroid rendezvous missions, this grapple unit can be modified for missions that have non-asteroid targets.

name: bluedog_SmallSquarePanel_Rotating
title: HLR-SSQ-R Mini Solar Panel
description: A small, non-tracking photovoltaic panel mounted to a 90 degree hinge.

name: bluedog_SmallSquarePanel_Static
title: HLR-SSQ Mini Solar Panel
description: A small, static photovoltaic panel for things that need a small amount of electricity.

name: bluedog_SurveyorOrbiterUpgrade
title: SurveyorOrbiter Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_SurveyorOrbiter_Antenna
title: RVMR-HG25R High Gain Relay Antenna
description: The Raumvermesser mast holds a Planar-array High-Gain Antenna, which shouldn't be use for grilling, but can be used as a relay.

name: bluedog_SurveyorOrbiter_Solar
title: RVMR-PVAR Solar Panel
description: Tracking solar panel with attitude control jets on the tip for the Raumvermesser orbiters.<#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Attach a pair to the core (without symmetry), one on a leg attachment point, and one directly opposite using the 'extended' attachment point option.</color>

name: bluedog_Surveyor_Adapter
title: LVMR-ISD Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A payload separation mechanism specifically designed for the Lanvermesser program, able to provide room for the retro motor's nozzle.

name: bluedog_Surveyor_AlphaSpectrometer
title: LVMR-AS32-R Alpha Spectrometer Experiment
description: Deployable experiment for the Landvermesser probe. Goes on the rear of the spacecraft, replacing the auxiliary battery used in the earlier missions.

name: bluedog_Surveyor_AuxBattery
title: LVMR-55i Landvermesser Auxiliary Battery
description: The blueprints show that this was a case for some science experiment, but there was a page missing. To prevent design delays, the engineers just crammed a dense battery in it.

name: bluedog_Surveyor_Camera
title: LVMR-CAM-S1 Landing Site Survey Camera
description: The rotating head with a mirror window allows the camera to take a mosaic of pictures of the landing site for analysis without having to move the actual camera. This is useful for evaluating the safety of a landing site ahead of sending a Kerbal crew, but there is only enough film for one site survey. If you need to run more surveys, bring additional cameras or have a Kerbonaut ironically replace the film.

name: bluedog_Surveyor_Core
title: LVMR-MB 'Landvermesser' Lander Core
description: This very light and rugged probe is designed to perform landing site surveys ahead of crewed flights. Includes propellant for its 3 vernier engines (Sold separately) and the control thrusters mounted on the legs (Also sold separately). The Solid Fuel Retromotor will be required for retro braking maneuvers.

name: bluedog_Surveyor_Leg
title: LVMR-SLG Landing Leg
description: Landing leg for the Landvermesser system. Includes reaction control thrusters - some would say too many, but can you ever really have too much reaction control? <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: RCS disabled by default, and toggles with the Gear action group.</color>

name: bluedog_Surveyor_Omni
title: LVMR-A071-99 Landvermesser Omni Antenna
description: This Omni antenna is a masterful re-use of old plumbing equipment and electronic parts from the bargain bin. It complements Landvermesser's HGA for short-range or emergency communication. Inclides the two variants for Landvermesser, as well as a veriant for the Raumvermesser orbiter.

name: bluedog_Surveyor_Scoop
title: LVMR-SC28-L Topsoil Scoop
description: This actuated arm can be used to interact with the topsoil to expose material for photography.
