It can help analyze physical properties of the surface material but collects none and can run no chemical analysis. Be sure to check that the arm can reach the ground because, well, that would be embarrassing...

name: bluedog_Surveyor_SolarAntenna
title: LVMR-AE20 HGA Antenna and Solar Panel
description: The Landvermesser mast holds a Planar-array High-Gain Antenna and a single Solar Panel for charging the batteries; neither of which should be used for grilling, but those radio waves will likely cook something... eventually.

name: bluedog_Surveyor_Vernier
title: LVMR-LV03 Landvermesser Vernier
description: This small engine is designed to be mounted to the Landvermesser as a set of three. It is a fairly efficient early design, but far too fragile to be mounted on a stack.

name: bluedog_Syncom
title: HGHS-301 "Satkom" Communications Satellite
description: A small (but capable) cylindrical, spin-stabilized communications satellite. Comes with space for an apogee motor and is equipped with thrusters and a small supply of monopropellant.

name: bluedog_TACSAT_Antenna
title: Sonne-MBM-LGCA Communications Array
description: An extremely large array of a variety of antennas optimized for Keostationary orbit communications. This array features five high-gain helical UHF antennas, two low-gain X-band horn antennas, and a single biconical antenna for telemetry and control. This antenna can fold up to fit in a 1.875m fairing. Designed for the HGHS-318 "Botte" satellite bus. Features Kerbin-tracking capabilities.

name: bluedog_TACSAT_Bus
title: HGHS-318 "Botte" Satellite Bus
description: A very large, barrel-shaped satellite bus. Sized at 1.75m, this satellite bus is the perfect size for 1.875m fairings/launch vehicles. Equipped with thrusters, batteries, and a modest supply of monopropellant. Includes a 0.3125m upper node for payload attachment, and while not designed for apogee motors, this satellite includes space for apogee motors up to 0.9375m in diameter on the bottom of the spacecraft.

name: bluedog_TIROS
title: OTWS Weather Satellite
description: Primitive, spin stabilized bus designed to serve as an experimental weather satellite. It mounts two television cameras, one with a wide field of view and another with a narrow lens. Placing it in a low orbit will allow it to relay images of things like hurricanes back to KSC, providing early warning to communities in the areas it can see.

name: bluedog_TRYP_Core
title: HLR-TRYP Probe Core
description: An unusually shaped standard probe core for unusually shaped satellites.

name: bluedog_TTS1
title: HLR-TTS1 Tracking Training Satellite
description: Small piggyback payload, used for verifying and training operators for the Deep Space Network. Includes transmitters and a temperature probe.

name: bluedog_Telstar_Antenna
title: TAT-PHON-F21 Helical Antenna
description: This lightweight communications antenna provides omnidirectional coverage for relaying signals.

name: bluedog_Telstar_Core
title: TAT-PHON1 "Kompfner" Communications Satellite
description: Primitive, spin stabilized bus designed to be used as an early communications satellite. The central ring is filled with two arrays of horn antennas, and a helical antenna can be placed on top to enhance reception.

name: bluedog_Tempel2_Ion
title: HLR-ZECR6 "Tempel" Ion Engine
description: Prototype xenon-powered engine for highly efficient interplanetary travel. Keep in mind that this prototype is more expensive and likely not as efficient as our upcoming models.

name: bluedog_Transit2A
title: TNSS-2A "Walnut" Navigation Satellite
description: A robust early navigational satellite. Includes an integrated solar panel, a very basic internal relay antenna, equipment for mapping the gravitational fields of planetary bodies, and an upper mount designed for attaching secondary payloads or other desired equipment.

name: bluedog_Transit4A
title: TNSS-4A "Barrel" Navigation Satellite
description: A robust early navigational satellite. TNSS-4A is also designed to be a test platform for the PB-PANS-3 RTG which can be attached to the lower mount of the satellite. Includes an integrated solar panel, a very basic internal relay antenna, equipment for mapping the gravitational fields of planetary bodies, and an upper mount designed for attaching secondary payloads or other desired equipment.

name: bluedog_Transit4A_Decoupler
title: TNSS-4A 0.3125m Decoupler
description: A small 0.3125m decoupler intended for the TNSS-4A satellite. Also provides clearance for the PB-PANS-3 RTG.

name: bluedog_Transit5_Antenna
title: TNSS-5 "Lampshade" Navigation Antenna
description: A small extending navigational antenna for the TNSS-5 satellite series.

name: bluedog_Transit5_Bus
title: TNSS-5 "Statum" Satellite Core
description: A tiny, versatile satellite bus designed to be as compact and light as possible. While one of the smallest of the program, this satellite bus is the most advanced of the TNSS program. While designed for navigation constellations, this satellite bus can be used for a number of things. Includes all the basic necessities that a probe core would have, although to keep it as light as possible it has only minimal SAS control.

name: bluedog_Transit5_Fins
title: TNSS-5BN Aft Fin Adapter
description: A 0.3125m adapter intended for the TNSS-5BN satellite. The fins are intended to keep the front of the spacecraft pointing forward in case of reentry, so that its RTG is vaporized on reentry to minimize radioactive material that reaches the surface. This adapter is hollow to allow for equipment to be placed inside. The bottom node includes a built-in decoupler.

name: bluedog_Transit5_GravityGradientBoom
title: TNSS-5 Gravity Gradient Boom
description: A 0.125m extending gravity gradient boom. Once extended, the spacecraft will become stabilized due to tidal gravitational effects. This method of stabilization requires no electrical power. Adds additional SAS control.

name: bluedog_Transit5_GravityGradientBoom_Light
title: TNSS-5BN Gravity Gradient Boom
description: A 0.125m extending gravity gradient boom. Once extended, the spacecraft will become stabilized due to tidal gravitational effects. This method of stabilization requires no electrical power. Adds additional SAS control. This version also has a small amount of solar cells to power a light on the end of the gravity gradient boom to aid in ground tracking.

name: bluedog_Transit5_Magnetometer
title: TNSS-5E Extending Magnetometer Experiment
description: This instrument is used for measuring a planet's magnetic field. Requires the separate "TNSS-5E Magnetometer Equipment Device" to be on board the vessel to function.

name: bluedog_Transit5_Magnetometer_Equipment
title: TNSS-5E Magnetometer Equipment Device
description: A device required for the TNSS-5E Magnetometer experiment to function.

name: bluedog_Transit5_RTG
title: TNSS-5BN Power and Communications Section
description: This is a section of the TNSS-5BN satellite that combines the power unit, a PB-PANS-9 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator with a navigation antenna ground plate. Perfect for nuclear powered navigation satellites.

name: bluedog_Transit5_SNAP9A
title: PB-PANS-9 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
description: A small, modular electric generator. Learning from the design of the previous PB-PANS-3 RTG, engineers have made a much more sophisticated electrical generator. This RTG occupies the middle ground between the PB-PANS-3 and the PB-PANS-19 radioisotope thermoelectric generators.

name: bluedog_Transit5_SOOS_Antenna
title: TNSS-5 Advanced Navigation Antenna
description: A more advanced version of TNSS-5's navigational antenna.

name: bluedog_Transit5_SOOS_Cage
title: TNSS-5 STOT Cradle
description: The STOT ("Stacked TNSS on TNSS") cradle is an epoxy structure capable of supporting the weight of a second TNSS-5 satellite on top of it, allowing for two TNSS-5 satellites to be launched together. This cradle is fixed to one satellite and includes a built-in decoupler on the top node to separate a second TNSS-5 satellite.

name: bluedog_Transit5_Solar
title: TNSS-5 Double-Sided Solar Panel
description: An extremely peculiar and small double sided solar panel. Folds up for storage in fairings, but doesn't track the sun. This solar panel comes in a variety of sizes depending on electrical needs. Folds out at a 45 degree angle and includes a dipole telemetry antenna for maintaining ground communication.

name: bluedog_Transit5_SolarScience
title: TNSS-5E Solar Experiment Package
description: A small 0.3125m platform for solar science.

name: bluedog_Transit5_UVSpectrometer
title: TNSS-5E Ultraviolet Telescope
description: A small, cheap, and compact telescope designed to take measurements in the UV spectrum.

name: bluedog_Viking_Bioshield_Decoupler
title: Spartan/B-LDD Bioshield Decoupler
description: Structural adapter for the Spartan Lander's Bioshield. Connects to the top of the core. The bottom node includes a decoupler, for jettisoning the truss and the lower bioshield after the lander has departed. The staging is disabled on the decoupler by default, to minimize accidents.

name: bluedog_Viking_Orbiter_Core
title: Spartan/O-PCC Probe Core
description: The culmination of the Burke and Argo programs, this octagonal probe bus was designed for the orbiter component of the Spartan program. Includes a small monopropellant store and a large battery. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Add the Spartan/O-CST "Calliope" Precision Star Tracker to your craft to gain additional SAS modes.</color>

name: bluedog_Viking_Orbiter_LaunchAdapter
title: Spartan/O-LTA Launch Adapter
description: Aft adapter for the Spartan Orbiter, connecting it to the upper stage. Mounts to the bottom of the core.

name: bluedog_Viking_Orbiter_PropulsionSection
title: Spartan/O-PSD Propulsion Module
description: Large propulsion module for probes, sufficient to bring the Spartan probe complex to orbit around Duna. Include liquid fuel, oxidizer, and a gimballing engine. Attaches to the bottom of the probe core.

name: bluedog_Viking_Orbiter_SolarPanel
title: Spartan/O-NTSP Folding Solar Panel
description: Non-tracking solar panel with attitude control jets on the tip. The control jets are configured by default for roll and yaw only. Can be switched from the standard angled fold to a straight vertical storage position.

name: bluedog_Viking_Orbiter_SolarPanel_Relay
title: Spartan/O-NTSP.R Relay Solar Panel
description: Non-tracking solar panel with attitude control jets on the tip. Includes a relay antenna, for communicating with the lander on its way to the surface.

name: bluedog_Viking_Orbiter_highGainAntenna
title: Spartan/O-HGA High Gain Antenna
description: Powerful relay antenna for the Wayfarer 10 probe with built in attitude control jets and homeworld tracking. The attitude control jets are set to the pitch axis only by default. Features both an angled version for Wayfarer 10 and a straighter version for easier radial attachment for other uses.

name: bluedog_Viking_Orbiter_lowGainAntenna
title: Spartan/O-LGG Low Gain Omni Antenna
description: A simple reliable omnidirectional low gain antenna for the Spartan/O probe.

name: bluedog_Viking_Orbiter_scanPlatform
title: Spartan/O-RSP "Voyeur" Scanning Platform
description: The main science instrumentation for the Spartan/O probe, this science platform includes telephoto cameras, an infrared radiometer, and an infrared spectrometer.

name: bluedog_Viking_Orbiter_starTracker
title: Spartan/O-CST "Calliope" Precision Star Tracker
description: This compact star tracker device can provide advanced SAS modes to any spacecraft.

name: bluedog_Xenon_MediumStack
title: HLR-mNGS Xenon Tank
description: A medium sized xenon tank for a 0.625m stack.

name: bluedog_Xenon_SmallSingle
title: HLR-1rNGS Xenon Tank
description: A small radially attached bottle of xenon gas. Useful for probes that need ion RCS, probably not enough for serious course adjustments.

name: bluedog_Xenon_SmallStack
title: HLR-sNGS Xenon Tank Assembly
description: A small sized xenon tank for a 0.625m stack.

name: bluedog_Xenon_SmallTriple
title: HLR-3rNGS Xenon Tank Assembly
description: Three small radially attached bottle of xenon gas. Useful for probes that need ion RCS, probably not enough for serious course adjustments.

name: bluedog_YoYoDespin
title: Y0-Y0 De-Spin Device
description: A small weight that when staged will move outwards on a rigid pole and then detach. Given angular momentum = mass * velocity * radius, increasing radius will decrease angular velocity since momentum is conserved. Technically this is not a yoyo despin device because there is no "snap" when the weight is fully extended stopping or reversing the spin. Always attach in symmetry. In typical use, a 0.3125 Spin Motor Decoupler is attached to the bottom of the kick motor (Staara 20), and the Despin Device is attached to the side of the kick motor or payload. First the spin motor "spins up" the vessel, then the kick motor is fired. When the kick motor completes its burn, the Despin Device is deployed to slow the spin rate back down.

name: bluedog_mariner10_SciencePallet
title: Argo-10-SPL Structural Science Palette
description: Lightweight sidemount truss for mounting instruments and other necessities.

name: bluedog_mariner10_UVspectrometer
title: Argo-10-EUS77 Ultraviolet Spectrometer
description: This advanced Extreme Ultraviolet Spectrometer consists of dual instruments. The combination of an occultation spectrometer and an airglow spectrometer yields high quality data.

name: bluedog_mariner10_camera
title: WLE-5000 "Duovid" Television Camera System
description: This advanced camera system for designed for Argo 10 includes a set of stereoscopic high quality television cameras and a basic airglow ultraviolet spectrometer.

name: bluedog_mariner10_cameraStandalone
title: WLE-5000 "Duovid" Standalone Television Camera System
description: This advanced camera system for designed for Argo-10 spacecraft includes a set of stereoscopic high quality television cameras and a basic airglow ultraviolet spectrometer. Available with both compact quadpod and mast mounting options.

name: bluedog_mariner10_decoupler
title: Argo-WSA-2 Payload Separation Mechanism
description: A 0.9375m payload separation mechanism specifically designed for the Argo program, able to provide room for aft scientific payloads, folding sunshield mechanisms, and more.

name: bluedog_mariner10_engine
title: Argo-10-MPS990 "Horton" Midcourse Correction Engine
description: A small monopropellant powered engine with an internal fuel supply. Although designated a midcourse correction engine, it has a generous store of monopropellant to allow for several burns on a multiplanetary flyby mission. Designed to be mounted up halfway inside the spacecraft bus. Attitude control is accomplished through jet vanes mounted inside the nozzle. An extra hidden bottom attach node is located within the engine to allow the decoupler to attach to it.

name: bluedog_mariner10_highGainAntenna
title: Wayfarer-10-HGRD-22 High Gain Relay Dish
description: Powerful relay antenna for the Wayfarer 10 probe with built in attitude control jets and homeworld tracking. The attitude control jets are set to the pitch axis only by default. Features both an angled version for Wayfarer 10 and a straighter version for easier radial attachment for other uses.

name: bluedog_mariner10_lowGainAntenna
title: Argo-10-ALA22 Omni Antenna
description: A simple reliable omnidirectional low gain antenna for the Argo 10 probe.

name: bluedog_mariner10_magnetometer
title: Argo-10-DTFM Folding Magnetometer Boom
description: Folding triaxial magnetometer boom with dual detectors.

name: bluedog_mariner10_plasmaScience
title: Argo-10-SEAEC/TCIR Electrostatic Science & IR Radiometer
description: This high end experiment package contains three instruments. An Ionization and Electrostatic Analysis experiment designed to study the plasma regime around planets, a broadband infrared radiometer, and an experiment to study solar wind.

name: bluedog_mariner10_solar
title: Argo-10-ACSP Folding Solar Panel
description: Tracking solar panel with attitude control jets on the tip. The control jets are configured by default for roll and yaw only. Can be switched from the standard angled fold to a straight vertical storage position.

name: bluedog_mariner10_starTracker
title: Argo-10-CNP44 "Sirius" Precision Star Tracker
description: This compact star tracker device can provide advanced SAS modes to any spacecraft.

name: bluedog_mariner10_sunShield
title: Argo-10-UBL34 Sun Shield
description: A deployable sunshield for the Argo 10 probe. Protects the probe from solar radiation while exploring the inner planets. Attaches to the Argo 10 engine and has a small opening for the thruster.

name: bluedog_probeRCSblock
title: HLR-PCS Attitude Control Thruster
description: 3 way probe RCS. Place 45 degrees off axis for proper transforms.

name: bluedog_probeRCSblockE
title: HLR-PCST Attitude Control Thruster
description: 3 way probe RCS. Place 45 degrees off axis for proper transforms. The bottom thruster has been enlarged. You can engage its overdrive via the throttle.

name: bluedog_solarBattery
title: HLR-15 Solar Battery
description: This arrangement of three small solar panels includes a battery. They can either charge the battery or provide power directly to your spacecraft systems.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_HGA
title: Nomad-HG14 High Gain Antenna
description: High data rate dish for transmitting science.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_RTG
title: Nomad-NMK2 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
description: An oddly angled RTG designed to attach to the Nomad lander at a corner. Also has a variant to attach it to a flat surface.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_boomSampler
title: Nomad-DG1 Boom Sampler
description: A boom with a scoop to scoop soil. And hopefully discover something interesting about the surface of other planets.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_camera
title: Nomad ALX-256 Panoramic Camera System
description: A high quality panoramic camera to send those beautiful images back home from your robotic landers.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_commandAntenna
title: Nomad C7C-2 Command Antenna
description: Command and control antenna for the Nomad lander. Fixed design so it can receive signals from the orbiter's relays throughout the descent.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_core
title: NMD-14 "Nomad" Lander Core
description: Evolved from the Landvermesser, the Nomad Lander can carry a substantial science payload down to the surface of bodies with thin atmospheres. Outfitted with large batteries and a capacious fuel tank. A floating lower attach node has decouple functionality and is used to attach to the heatshield.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_descentEngine
title: TR33 "Halberd" Descent Engine
description: This engine is designed for propulsive landing on bodies with thin atmospheres. The engine bell is canted outwards and shaped to reduce dust being kicked up at the landing site. The engine does not gimbal so make sure to bring an attitude control system and to use in a symmetry group of at least 3 engines. The engine runs on monopropellant which is found to be less likely to contaminate landing sites than bipropellant exhaust.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_drill
title: Nomad-A11 Auger Drill
description: This auger type drill does not penetrate very deep but can obtain surface samples deeper than a soil scoop.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_leg
title: Nomad-LTG3 Landing Leg
description: A sturdy retracting landing leg, perfect for landing on other bodies. Includes attitude control jets and adjustable friction pads. RCS disabled by default, and toggles with the Gear action group. Use the Gear action group (default keybind: G) after seperating from the heat shield.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_longRangeSampler
title: Nomad-LRS Hydrometer
description: This instrument measures a planet's atmosphere for moisture, one of the most important substances known to Kerbalkind, and a building block of life as we know it. Also useful for washing the ship before takeoff. Includes a bonus thermometer.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_parachute
title: Nomad-SSP4 Parachute
description: Supersonic parachute. Configured by default for thin atmospheres with very low pressure and high altitude for deployment. Its suggested to bring an engine or three for propulsive landing for final touchdown or things might get bumpy.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_passiveAirSampler
title: Nomad-PSMS Passive Air Sampler
description: This instruments combines an atmospheric mass spectrometer, barometer, and atmosphere analysis instrument.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_radarAltimeter
title: Nomad Lander RDLT-45 Radar Altimeter Science Package
description: This disk shaped radar altimeter dish can be used to map the surface height of the body below. Also features a basic gravity sensor and accelerometer.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsLander_srbMount
title: Nomad SMD-24 Mount
description: Just a simple frame covered in fabric, this mount with built in decoupler is sized specifically to attach the Staara 24 motor to the Nomad Lander core.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_HGA
title: Nomad-CDR18 High Gain Dish Antenna
description: Powerful relay antenna for the Nomad Orbiter with homeworld tracking. Features an optional receptacle that allows the dish to be placed flat against a surface.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_HGA_large
title: Nomad-CDR130 High Gain Dish Antenna
description: This upgraded high gain antenna for the Nomad orbiter is as wide as the probe itself! Attaches to the same point as the standard high gain dish but folds underneath instead. Features cutouts for the spacecraft adapter attachement points and the engines. Hopefully the holes dont affect the perfomance too much! Features homeworld tracking.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_LGA
title: Nomad-LGA22 Low Gain Antenna
description: A simple deployable low gain, omni directional antenna.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_MGA
title: Nomad-CDR9 Medium Gain Antenna
description: A backup relay antenna for the Nomad orbiter, this medium gain dish features homeworld tracking.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_PSP
title: Nomad-PSP-VMP Planetary Scan Platform
description: All of the orbital science package for the baseline Nomad orbiter is contained in this mega instrument. Features a set of vidicon cameras, infrared spectrometers, an ultraviolet spectrometer, and an infrared radiometer.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_PSP_upgrade
title: Nomad-PSP-FCMP Improved Planetary Scan Platform
description: Upgraded orbital science package for the Nomad orbiter . Features mostly the same instruments as the baseline version including infrared spectrometers, an ultraviolet spectrometer, and an infrared radiometer. However the primary imaging system has been upgraded from Vidicons to a high resolution film camera and accompanying built in scanner.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_SM
title: Nomad-SEM8 Service Module
description: A convenient service module for the Nomad probe system, this unit has built in RCS booms for attitude control, space to attach a propulsion system and plenty of surface area for science instruments and other support equipment.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_annularSolarPanel
title: NMD-AS8 Annular Solar Panel
description: Annular solar panel designed to attach in an array of eight to the corners of the "Nomad-SEM8 Service Module".

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_atmosphericMassSpec
title: Nomad-MSO3 Atmospheric Mass Spectrometer
description: This atmospheric mass spectrometer can analyze the compositon of the atmosphere of the body below from orbit.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_backshell
title: Nomad-ASB36 Capsule Backshell
description: Featuring a built in decoupler, this backshell together with the accompanying heatshield can encapsulate a planetary lander in a cosy contamination free environmnet until its time to deorbit. The Backshell is intended to be retained by the orbiter.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_core
title: NMD-73 "Nomad" Probe Core
description: The Nomad 73 probe core is a top of the line bus designed for prestigous planetary science missions. This unit is equipped with large batteries, advanced SAS modes and a recess for an atmospheric lander capsule. A flat top option is also available for more versatility.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_cosmicRay
title: Nomad-CR64 Cosmic Ray Detector
description: A small experiment for detecting cosmic ray impacts.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_heatshield
title: Nomad Heat Shield
description: Roughly 3.6m heat shield for the Nomad lander. Has built in RCS jets and a store of monopropellant for atttitude control during deorbit and entry until the lander can take over after separation. RCS disabled by default, and toggles with the action group Custom 10. Use the Custom 10 action group (default keybind: 0) after seperating from the backshell.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_magnetometerBoom
title: Nomad HLR-NMD-EP5 Folding Magnetometer Boom
description: This interestingly shaped hoop magnetometer is designed to study magnetohydrodynamic waves and other magnetic field structures in orbit. Derived from an instrument used on the HLR-OOG Sansisco probe.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_mmImpact
title: Nomad-P1NG-3MD Micrometeoroid Detector
description: Our scientists think space might not be as empty as we once thought. This device contains a plate for measuring the impacts of 'micrometeoroids', the little pieces of debris and particles that travel through open vacuum at thousands of meters per second. Measuring the number of impacts gives us an idea of how dangerous an area of space may be for our ships.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_neutronAlbedoBoom
title: Nomad HLR-NMD-SM6 Folding Soil Moisture Sensor Boom
description: This instrument measures neutron albedo to try to detect moisture in the soil below.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_propulsionModule
title: NMD-PM200 Propulsion Module
description: A capacious propulsion module for the Nomad probe orbiter with large fuel tanks, attachment points for primary and secondary engines, and even solar panels. Designed to fit inside of the NMD-SM "Nomad" Service Module. The pressurisation spheres might poke out the top into the probe core above.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_relayAntenna
title: Nomad Lander Relay Antenna
description: This small relay antenna allows Nomad to stay in contact with it's lander probe.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_solarFlat
title: Nomad 4QS Fixed Solar Panel
description: A flat solar panel designed to attach to the bottom of the Nomad orbiter's propulsion module.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_solarPlasma
title: Nomad SPS Solar Plasma Sampler
description: This instrument is used to measure the composition of the solar wind plasma.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_solarXray
title: Nomad XRI Solar X-ray Imager
description: A small X-ray imager for Nomad.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_spacecraftAdapter
title: Nomad-BD-SPM-4.25 Spacecraft Adapter
description: A roughly 4.25m truss spacecraft adapter and built in decoupler designed specifically for the Nomad spacecraft.

name: bluedog_voyagerMarsOrbiter_starTracker
title: Nomad Precision Star Tracker
description: A high precision star tracker designed for the Nomad probe core. Place over the constellation marking on the Nomad-SEM8 Service Module.

name: bluedog_Beacon1
title: Pathfinder-BCN "Bloon" Satellite
description: This 0.125m probe core is derived from the Pathfinder-1 "Sienno" probe core. Instead of Pathfinder-1's geiger counter, Pathfinder-BCN houses an inflatable "balloon" experiment for use in space. This experiment is intended to make atmospheric density measurements in Kerbin orbit. Also has a small apogee kick motor built into the nose as well as an omni antenna.

name: bluedog_Juno1_Explorer1
title: Pathfinder-1 "Sienno" Satellite
description: This 0.125m probe core integrates an omni antenna and a geiger counter for measuring radation. Attaches to the top of the "Vicenza" solid motor.

name: bluedog_Juno1_Guidance
title: Etoh-C Guidance Unit
description: Guidance core for the Etoh-C Rocket with built in RCS jets. Includes a bottom decoupler, to separate from the core stage and align the high speed stages for orbital insertion.

name: bluedog_Juno1_Nose
title: Etoh-C Nose Cone
description: This nose cone comes with an optional built in decoupler for attaching the "Vicenza" high speed stages to the booster. Optionally it can be cut down for use as a more traditional 1.25m to 0.625m adapter.

name: bluedog_Redstone_A7_TailUnit
title: Etoh-140-TU "Sandstone" Liquid Fuel Engine
description: This primitive booster engine was originally designed to run on alcolox. Initially used on the Sandstone ballistic missile, the engine would later be upgraded to use a more volatine Hydyne fuel. The engine was also used on the Hermes Sandstone launch vehicle but the designers went back to the safer although less performant Alcolox mix. The shroud includes vanes below the nozzle that deflect the engine exhaust, allowing for primitive thrust vectoring. Includes a slightly lighter shroudless version, without any thrust vectoring.

name: bluedog_Redstone_AirVane
title: Etoh-AVRT Air Vane
description: A small control fin with two RCS jets built into the base.

name: bluedog_Redstone_Fin_Basic
title: Etoh-AF Aerodynamic Fin
description: This aerodynamic fin.

name: bluedog_Redstone_Fin_CtrlSurf
title: Etoh-CS Control Surface
description: This aerodynamic fin includes a control surface, to help keep your rocket going the right way. It also includes a thrust vane, but you don't want to know about that.

name: bluedog_Redstone_FuelTank
title: Etoh-1400 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: This 1.25m tank was originally over twice as long as the FLT-800. You aren't ready for this kind of power. Maybe we'll have to take it away from you.

name: bluedog_Redstone_Guidance
title: Etoh-H Guidance Unit
description: Guidance core for the Etoh-Hermes rocket, with a little room inside for the Hermes retro pack. Doesn't accomplish much, but it will make a rocket taller.

name: bluedog_Redstone_MediumFuelTank
title: Etoh-300/600 Liquid Fuel Tank
description: 1.25m extension tank made using Etoh tooling. Includes two switchable length options.

name: bluedog_Redstone_QuadEngine
title: Etoh-340-QTU "Feldspar" Liquid Fuel Engine
description: In an effort to extend the service life of the basic "Sandstone" engine design, engineers have modified the engine significantly. Four downrated thrust chambers are now powered by set of common pumps and machinery. The net effect is this 1.5m powerplant has significant lifting power compared to contemporary engines, but still lacks efficiency.

name: bluedog_Sergeant_11x
title: HLR-2911 "Vicenza-11" Solid Rocket Cluster
description: A cluster of 11 Vicenza solid rocket motors. It features BDB's SafeSolid™ system, allowing the engine to be shut down in flight, allowing for more accurate orbital insertions and maneuvers.

name: bluedog_Sergeant_11x_Decoupler
title: HLR-VD11 0.625m Decoupler
description: Small 0.625m decoupler with a hole in the middle. Used on the Sienno/Vicenza stack between the 3x and 11x stages. Attach to the hidden node at the top of the 3x motors, then attach the 11x motor to this.

name: bluedog_Sergeant_1x
title: HLR-291 "Vicenza" Solid Rocket
description: Small 0.125m solid rocket motor. It features BDB's SafeSolid™ system, allowing the engine to be shut down in flight, allowing for more accurate orbital insertions and maneuvers.

name: bluedog_Sergeant_3x
title: HLR-293 "Vicenza-3" Solid Rocket Cluster
description: A cluster of 3 Vicenza solid rocket motors. It features BDB's SafeSolid™ system, allowing the engine to be shut down in flight, allowing for more accurate orbital insertions and maneuvers.

name: bluedog_Sergeant_3x_Decoupler
title: DGR-VD03 0.3125m Decoupler
description: Small 0.3125m decoupler. Used on the Sienno/Vicenza stack between the 1x and 3x stages.

name: bluedog_Sparta_0p625mAdapter
title: Etoh-L 0.625m Interstage
description: 0.9375m to 0.625m structural adapter with an optional decoupler to turn it into an interstage. Originally used for the Etoh-L rocket to separate the second stage from the booster stage.

name: bluedog_Sparta_0p625mInterstage
title: Etoh-L 0.625m Interstage
description: A short, rather generic 0.625m interstage originally used for the Etoh-L to separate the payload from the second stage.

name: bluedog_Sparta_ControlJets
title: Etoh-L-AUCT Control Jets
description: 2-way stage RCS, originally intended to provide attitude control for the Etoh-Leonidas launch vehicle.

name: bluedog_Sparta_Guidance
title: Etoh-L Guidance Unit
description: Guidance core for the Etoh-Leonidas rocket. Includes a bottom decoupler, to separate from the core stage and align the high speed stages for orbital insertion. Do note that in this configuration, control thrusters are sold separately.

name: bluedog_WRESAT
title: Etoh-L "Aussat" Probe Core
description: A leftover reentry test vehicle turned into an scientfic satellite. Equipped with experiments to measure the ionosphere, Kerbin's ultraviolet halo, and solar x-ray emissions.

name: bluedog_Ablestar_Fairing_SAF
title: BD-AFB-AS Alphastar Fairing Base SAF
description: A low profile 0.9375m-ish fairing base designed especially for the Fenris Alphastar-160 upper stage. Includes an adjustable hard fairing.

name: bluedog_Agena_POPPY_fairingBase_SAF
title: Belle-RPP 1.25m "Rhoeas" Fairing Base SAF
description: This flared 1.25m fairing base was originally made for a secretive surveillance satellite. One of the larger options available for the Belle upper stage, it has plenty of other uses though.

name: bluedog_Agena_SLV3B_Fairing_SAF
title: Bossart-PCR3B-SF 1.875m Fairing Base SAF
description: A special 1.875m fairing base designed to fully shroud a Belle upper stage on top of the Bossart PCR3B rocket. Place on top of the Bossart-PCR3B-FB adapter fairings base. An optional attach node can be enabled in the editor to use it as a standalone fairing base.

name: bluedog_Agena_Titan33B_adapterFairingBase
title: Prometheus-33B-FB 1.875m Adapter Fairing Base SAF
description: 1.875m fairing base that integrates a 1.875m to 0.9375m structural adapter. Designed to completely enclose the Belle upper stage and sensitive payloads for the Prometheus 33B and 34B rockets. Was also adapted for the Bossart PC23F. Can be enabled as a decoupler but it is recommended to place the Bossart-PCR3B-SI 0.9375m Interstage on top when using with a Belle upper stage.

name: bluedog_Delta2_1875_adapter_fairingBase_SAF
title: Daleth-P/K 1.875m Prometheus Fairing Adapter SAF
description: This 1.875m fairing base was designed to allow the 1.5m Daleth P/K Fairing Adapter to use the standard Prometheus fairing. Simply place on top of the 1.5m Daleth fairing skirt. Also features an optional top attach node to enable its use as a standalone fairing base.

name: bluedog_Juno2FairingBase
title: Chryslus-II-VCA Fairing Cone
description: A special fairing base for the Chryslus II rocket. The fairing might not be very spacious but will safely enclose a Vicenza cluster and a small payload.

name: bluedog_LDC_3p5mFairingBase
title: Herakles 3.5m Adapter Fairing Base Adapter SAF
description: 3.125m to 3.5m fairing base adapter for very large payloads.

name: bluedog_Titan3_CommercialDPAF_SAF
title: Prometheus-III/COMM 2.5m Dual Payload Adapter
description: 2.5m dual payload adapter for the Commercial Prometheus III. This innovative device has an integrated fairing on top and has room to carry another payload underneath. First attach your lower payload to the stock version of the 2.5m Prometheus fairing base and then place this on top. The adapter needs to be manually decoupled in the part action window after the upper payload has deployed.

name: bluedog_VanguardFairing_SAF
title: Easton-AFB 0.625m Fairing Base SAF
description: A special fairing base for the Easton Rocket. Has plenty of room in the cylindrical base for a solid kick motor and features an adjustable fairing cone on top.

name: bluedog_J2A2
title: Saturn Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_J2S
title: Saturn Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_J2X
title: Saturn Upgrade
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_Pegasus_ElectronSpectrometer
title: Condor-RME3 Electron Spectormeter
description: This instrument is designed for the Condor satellite with the intent of measuring trapped radiation to construct maps of planetary radiation belts.

name: bluedog_Pegasus_ElectronicsCanister
title: Condor-SUS "Boxy" Probe Core
description: A unique and robust probe core, the Condor-SUS "Boxy" probe core is a rectangular electronics cansiter that houses various satellite equipment and systems. This probe core was designed specifically for satellites that are integrated with their upper stages, this one being specifically designed for the Sarnus S-IV mounted Condor satellite. As a result, this probe core does not have very large batteries as it is meant to rely on the batteries of its upper stage. Despite this, it can be repurposed for other uses and comes with equipment such as a built-in direct antenna, reaction wheels, and small aft mounted thermal control radiators.

name: bluedog_Pegasus_ForwardSolar
title: Condor-FSP1 Solar Panel
description: A simple, sturdy, and compact solar panel designed as the forward solar panel for the Condor satellite. Doesn't track the sun.

name: bluedog_Pegasus_MM_Experiment
title: Condor-MMEP Micrometeorite Impact Experiment Wing
description: A very large panel designed to monitor and record micrometeorite impacts. This advanced experiment can map the density and distribution of micrometeorites in planetary orbits.

name: bluedog_Pegasus_Solar
title: Condor-SSP2 Solar Panel
description: A simple and sturdy solar panel designed for the Condor satellite. Doesn't track the sun.

name: bluedog_Pegasus_Truss
title: Condor-UB Truss Structure
description: A large truss structure design to mount the Condor satellite's experiments and solar panels. Designed to be housed inside an Kane Boilerplate and fixed to a Sarnus S-IV upper stage.

name: bluedog_S2_M1_mount
title: Sarnus-MBCM 3.75m Engine Mount
description: 3.75m engine mount designed specifically for the massive MBC-1 Megalodon Engine. Attach to the Sarnus-SII-4600 3.75m Engine Mount.

name: bluedog_Saturn_4p25m_adapters
title: Sarnus-SIVB-425 Adapters
description: A series of adapters to connect 3.75, 3.125 or 1.875m stages to 4.25m sized stages.

name: bluedog_Saturn_5m_adapter
title: Sarnus-05T425 5m to 4.25m Interstage
description: A 5m to 4.25m generic interstage or structural adapter.

name: bluedog_Saturn_6p25m_adapter
title: Sarnus-SII-62505 6.25m to 5m Interstage
description: A 6.25m to 5m generic interstage or structural adapter.

name: bluedog_Saturn_AJ260
title: Sarnus-BR-425 Solid Rocket Booster
description: 4.25m jumbo sized solid booster. Includes inline stack mount and radial mounted variants, as well as half and full length options.

name: bluedog_Saturn_AJ260_Nose
title: Sarnus-ANC 4.25m Nose Cone
description: Aerodynamic nose cone for 4.25m boosters, like the BR-425 and S1E.

name: bluedog_Saturn_AJ260_RadialDecoupler
title: Sarnus-RBD 4.25m Radial Decoupler
description: Massive radial decoupler for attaching (and separating) 4.25m boosters. Currently includes custom lengths for the S1E tank and BR-425 SRB variants.

name: bluedog_Saturn_AJ260_Sepratron
title: Sarnus-BR-S Radial Separatron
description: An even larger scale separation motor for even larger scale boosters. The nozzles are 8 degrees canted outwards, make sure they don't impinge on the core!

name: bluedog_Saturn_Engine_F1
title: Sarnus-LE1F-2214 "Regor" Liquid Engine
description: The most powerful single-chamber engine ever constructed, the LE1F 'Regor' is a powerful engine for the most powerful of rockets. As if it weren't powerful enough upgrades are also available.

name: bluedog_Saturn_Engine_H1
title: Sarnus-HD1-270 "Navi" Liquid Engine
description: An upgrade over the aging LVT-45, this 1.25m lifter engine has high aspirations.

name: bluedog_Saturn_Engine_J2
title: Sarnus-HE2J-515 "Dnoces" Cryogenic Engine
description: After Inon-derived upper stages proved too weak for large launchers, a new high-powered, high efficiency vacuum engine was created. While it sacrifices a bit of efficiency, the thrust to weight ratio is better for lifting upper stages.

name: bluedog_Saturn_Engine_J2T
title: Sarnus-HE2JT "Tohces" Cryogenic Aerospike
description: A development of the Dnoces engine, the Tohces reuses a number of components such as turbopumps, while exchanging the bell-shaped thrust chamber for an annular aerospike. The result is a slightly lighter engine, with higher ISP. Unlike some aerospikes, it is able to perform limited gimbaling using differential thrust.

name: bluedog_Saturn_LRB_EngineMount
title: Sarnus-LRB-PDEB Engine Mount
description: Structural base with mounting points for the dual "Regor" engines of the Sarnus LRB.

name: bluedog_Saturn_LRB_Tank
title: Sarnus-LRB-40K Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Long 4.25m fuel tank developed using S1C technology and techniques. Intended for use as liquid strap-on boosters on uprated Sarnus-V variants.

name: bluedog_Saturn_Radiator_Large
title: Sarnus-SII-TCS-3 Cryogenic Stage Radiator Large
description: Shrouded deployable radiator for keeping your cryogenic stages nice and chilly. Triple-panel version for the largest of hydrogen tanks. Radiates 48kW at 300K.

name: bluedog_Saturn_Radiator_Medium
title: Sarnus-SII-TCS-2 Cryogenic Stage Radiator Medium
description: Shrouded deployable radiator for keeping your cryogenic stages nice and chilly. Double-panel version for big hydrogen tanks. Radiates 32kW at 300K.

name: bluedog_Saturn_Radiator_Small
title: Sarnus-SII-TCS-1 Cryogenic Stage Radiator Small
description: Shrouded deployable radiator for keeping your cryogenic stages nice and chilly. Single-panel version. Radiates 16kW at 300K.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1B_Fin
title: Sarnus-SI-AAS Advanced Aerodynamic Surface
description: A more refined fin for a less refined launcher.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1B_Interstage
title: Sarnus-SIVB-42IA Interstage
description: 4.25m Interstage for the Sarnus S-IVB upper stage. Attach to the bottom rim of the mounting plate, once the engine has been attached. It includes 4 solid retro motors that fire when staged, to pull the previous stage away from the upper stage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1C_Airbrake
title: Sarnus-SID-ABF Airbrake Fin
description: This large aerodynamic fin includes a pair of air brake flaps, for aiding in recovery of stages.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1C_Decoupler
title: Sarnus-SIC-625SD 6.25m Stack Decoupler
description: Thin stack decoupler for 6.25m core stages. In the Sarnus V configuration, attach underneath the S-II interstage. Once the S-IC is pulled away, fire the S-II ullage motors, ignite the 5 second stage engines, and then separate the interstage after ullage burnout.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1C_EngineMount
title: Sarnus-SIC-FE5M Engine Mount
description: Massive engine mount for the Sarnus S5 first stage, designated S-IC. Includes mounting points for the 5 "Regor" engines and 4 aerodynamic stabilizing fins. And includes retro solids to pull the first stage back during staging.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1C_Fin
title: Sarnus-SIC-ASF Aerodynamic Fin
description: This large aerodynamic fin is small compared to the massive Sarnus S5 that it attaches to.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1C_Tank
title: Sarnus-SIC-86K Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Massive 6.25m fuel tank for the S-IC first stage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1D_BoosterSkirt
title: Sarnus-SID-BE4 Booster Skirt
description: Large engine mount for the Sarnus S-1D first stage. This booster skirt is staged with the outer four engines during the burn, turning the booster into a stage-and-a-half configuration.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1D_Parachute
title: Sarnus PR-1R Radial Parachute
description: A large radial parachute for recovery of Sarnus stages.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1D_SustainerTank
title: Sarnus-SID-ST1 Sustainer Mount
description: Large sustainer mount for the center engine in the Sarnus S1D stage. Attach the booster skirt to the top of the sustainer mount, and stage them when sufficient thrust is reached.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1D_Vernier
title: Sarnus-VF1 "Tutu" Liquid Vernier
description: These small vernier engines are designed to provide roll control authority for Sarnus rocket stages powered by a single Regor engine such as the S1-D half stage. Mount to the bottom of the Sarnus rocket's main fuel tank.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1E_Tank
title: Sarnus-SIE-16K Liquid Fuel Tank
description: Developed to replace the clustered tank of the Sarnus S1 first tank, this tank is much lighter and has a bit more fuel.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1_EngineMount
title: Sarnus-SI-2800 Engine Mount
description: Structural base with mounting points for the 8 first stage engines of the Sarnus S1. Place 4 "Grivan" engines in the center, followed by 4 "Navi" engines in the outboard mounts.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1_LargeFin
title: Sarnus-SI-LAS Large Aerodynamic Surface
description: Large fins for the Sarnus SI stage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1_Retro
title: Sarnus-SI-SRM Retro Motor
description: A growler full of boom, for pulling your first stage back from your upper stage at separation.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1_SmallFin
title: Sarnus-SI-SAS Small Aerodynamic Surface
description: Small is a relative term.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S1_Tanks
title: Sarnus-SI-16K Liquid Fuel Tank
description: LFO tank for the Sarnus-S1 first stage, made up of eight modified Etoh fuel tanks wrapped around a modified Chryslus fuel tank. The design saves on cost, but doesn't have the highest mass efficiency.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S2_3p75_mount
title: Sarnus-SII-4600 Engine Mount
description: Alternative mount for the Sarnus S2 stage allowing for large engines with 3.75m interfaces to be mounted such as the MBC-1 Megalodon. The upper attach node is doubled. Attach it to the tank, then attach the interstage to the top of the engine mount once you've added the engines.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S2_EngineMount
title: Sarnus-SII-2300 Engine Mount
description: Mounting plate for the 5 HE2J-550 'Dnoces' engines that make up the S-II stage. The upper attach node is doubled. Attach it to the tank, then attach the interstage to the top of the engine mount once you've added the engines.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S2_Fin
title: Sarnus-SII-HDF Aerodynamic Fin
description: Large fins with hold down connectors for Sarnus SII-INT variants.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S2_Interstage
title: Sarnus-SII-625IAD 6.25m Interstage
description: 6.25m straight-walled interstage decoupler for the Sarnus S-II stage. Attach this to the S-II engine mount, then attach the S-II ullage motors.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S2_Tank
title: Sarnus-SII-60K Cryogenic Fuel Tank
description: Massive 6.25m fuel tank for the S-II stage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S2_Ullage
title: Sarnus-SII-SUM Ullage Motor
description: Large scale ullage motor for the S-II interstage. Attach to the outside of the interstage, fire them to settle the propellant before separating the interstage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S2_wetWorkshop
title: Sarnus-SII-WWS Wet WorkShop
description: Using lessons learned from the Hokulani program, this space wet workshop space station module is based on the massive Sarnus SII Cryogenic Fuel Tank. After launch, switch from fuel to lab before boarding scientists.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_AARDVTruss
title: Kanaloa-AARDV Truss Adapter
description: Adapter truss for mounting the Kanaloa-AARDV in a 4.25m fairing. Includes retro rockets, for separating the previous stage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_APS_200
title: Sarnus-SIVB-APS-200 Auxilary Propulsion System
description: A large thruster arrangement for controlling the attitude of the Sarnus-IVB stage. This version is intended for the Sarnus 1B rocket, and lacks ullage thrusters due to the single burn flight profile.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_APS_500
title: Sarnus-SIVB-APS-500 Auxilary Propulsion System
description: A large thruster arrangement for controlling the attitude of the Sarnus-IVB stage. Because the Sarnus V flight profile includes multiple burns for the SIVB upper stage, ullage thrusters are also included.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_CentaurTruss
title: Inon 3.125m Truss Adapter
description: Bottom part of an Inon stage. Attach to the node at the bottom of the top rim on the Inon mounting plate. This one includes a 3.125m truss adapter, for mounting on large fairing bases.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_DPAFbase
title: Sarnus-SIVB-DB4 Dual Payload Adapter Base
description: Base for a dual payload adapter system for the Sarnus Rocket, designed originally for the "Nomad" probe system. Attach the first payload to the base and then attach the Dual Payload Fairing to the floating top node.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_EngineMount
title: Sarnus-S4B Engine Mount
description: Engine mount for a single 'Dnoces' cryogenic upper stage engine. Mount Sarnus APS units and small ullage motors for the complete package.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_InstrumentUnit
title: Sarnus-SIVB-IU Instrument Unit
description: 4.25m instrument unit for the Sarnus S-IVB upper stage. Contains enough torque to control large rockets, and the batteries to keep them running. Includes 3.75m and 6.25m variants.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_Interstage
title: Sarnus-SIVB-W625IA Interstage Adapter
description: 6.25m to 4.25m interstage fairing, attach to the bottom of the S-IVB engine mount. Functions as a decoupler and integrates solid retro motors to push away the previous stage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_SLA
title: Sarnus-SIVB-LAM Lander Adapter Module
description: This 4.25m to 2.5m adapter opens in four 'petals' to separate the Kane-11 Service Engine's hidden attach node from a Sarnus stack. Staging the decoupler opens the petals and releases the CSM. Manually decouple the MEM once the transposition and docking maneuver is complete. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: The SINA MEM is attached to the payload structure via a hidden node within the descent stage, not the bottom of the engine.</color>

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_SLA_JettisonBase
title: Sarnus-SIVB-BLAM Lunar Adapter Base
description: This 4.25m  adapter base contains mounting points for the Kane CSM and 4 jettisonable panels to hold it above the payload. Includes standard conical, and slightly wider cylindercal variants. The Sina MEM is attached to the payload structure on the inside. Manually decouple the MEM once the transposition and docking maneuver is complete. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: The SINA MEM is attached to the payload structure via a hidden node within the descent stage, not the bottom of the engine.</color>

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_SLA_Panel
title: Sarnus-SIVB-SLAM Lander Adapter Segment
description: Place in 4x symmetry around the Sarnus-SIVB-BLAM Lunar Adapter Base. Includes standard conical, and slightly wider cylindercal variants.\n<#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: Stage TOGETHER with the Sarnus-SIVB-BLAM Lunar Adapter Base</color>

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_Tank
title: Sarnus-SIVB-14300 Cryogenic Fuel Tank
description: Medium sized 4.25m liquid hydrogen tank for upper stages.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4B_Ullage
title: Sarnus-SIV-SRM Ullage Motor
description: Large scale ullage motor for large scale boosters. Automatically decouples after expending itself, to save weight.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4C_ShellPort
title: Sarnus-SIVB-42SP Interstage Docking Adapter
description: 4.25m Interstage in-line docking adapter. Docks with the SIVB-42TP port.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4C_TrussPort
title: Sarnus-SIVB-42TP Interstage Docking Adapter
description: 4.25m Interstage in-line docking adapter. Docks with the SIVB-42SP port.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4F_Tank
title: Sarnus-SIVF-14300 Cryogenic Fuel Tank
description: Small sized 6.25m liquid hydrogen tank for upper stages.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4_2p5m_centaurAdapter
title: Sarnus-SIV ASC-875 Upper Stage Adapter
description: Interstage decoupler to allow 1.875m spacecraft or stages to be mounted to the top of the SIV stage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4_2p5m_spacecraftAdapter
title: Sarnus-SIV ASC-25 Spacecraft Adapter
description: 2.5m Interstage decoupler to allow 2.5m spacecraft or stages to be mounted to the top of the SIV stage. Also has a version to allow such stages to be attached to 1.875m lower stages.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4_Adapter
title: Sarnus-SIV A6BP Payload Adapter
description: A payload adapter designed to mate 2.5m payloads to the Sarnus-SIV stage. While designed specifically for mating SIV with the Kane Boilerplate Service Module, this adapter can be used for a wide range of applications. Also the primary mount for the Condor satellite, and as such includes a toggleable mount to hold the Condor satellite as well as toggleable guide rails to guide the Kane Boilerplate safely off of Condor. Includes an integrated decoupler and a toggleable extension.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4_AdapterTank
title: Sarnus-SIV-2200 Cryogenic Fuel Tank
description: 3.75m to 2.5m LHO adapter tank for the Sarnus-SIV second stage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4_Boilerplate
title: Kane-SA-MSM Service Module Boilerplate
description: A boilerplate test model of the Kane Service Module intended to simulate its properties during launch. Comes with basic avionics instrumentation and batteries to support unmanned testing. The boilerplate was designed to be hollow to house a secondary payload if desired, however it can be filled with ballast for missions that do not involve a secondary payload. Includes toggleable mockup (nonfunctional) RCS thrusters and an optional integrated decoupler.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4_EngineMount
title: Sarnus-SIV-600X Engine Mount
description: Mounting plate for the 6 second stage engines of the Sarnus SIV upper stage. Place an "Inon" on all 6 mounting points.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4_InstrumentUnit
title: Sarnus-SIV-CGI Instrumentation Unit
description: 2.5m pressurized instrument unit for the Sarnus SIV upper stage. Contains enough torque to control large rockets, and the batteries to keep them running. Can be upgraded to the Block II version which reduces mass by mounting instrumentation on the walls instead of using pressurized cylinders, similar to later Sarnus instrument units.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4_Interstage
title: Sarnus-SIV Interstage
description: 3.75m Interstage for the Sarnus-S4 stage. Attach to the hidden node inside the S-4 engine mounting plate.

name: bluedog_Saturn_S4_Tank
title: Sarnus-SIV-3500 Cryogenic Fuel Tank
description: LHO tank for the Sarnus-SIV second stage.

name: bluedog_Saturn_SNAP29
title: PB-PANS-29 Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator and Radiator
description: RTG with integrated radiator, for mounting on 4.25m stages. The radiator can cool one SIVB's worth of LHO, maybe about 1.5m more at a stretch.

name: bluedog_Saturn_SideDockingPort
title: Sarnus OCDP Orbital Construction Docking Port
description: Docking port for mounting to the structural Radial Docking Adapter

name: bluedog_Saturn_SideDockingRail
title: Radial Docking Adapter
description: Large radial structural rail for mounting OCDPs to the side of large upper stages, to facilitate in-orbit construction. Auto-struts recommended.

name: bluedog_saturn_S4B_lowProfileDecoupler
title: Sarnus-S4B-425LPD 4.25m Low Profile Stack Decoupler
description: Thin stack decoupler 4.25m stages.

name: bluedog_saturn_S4b_payloadAdapter
title: Sarnus-SIVB-SA12 Structural Payload Adapter
description: This lightweight structural adapter goes on top of your upper stage to help mount payloads. Include three different endcap diameters.

name: bluedog_saturn_s2_dockingPortActive
title: Sarnus IMSDP-A 6.25m Active Orbital Construction Docking Port
description: A XL sized docking port designed to dock gigantic stages for orbital construction. This active version has a key that helps line up with the passive version. Deploy the probe for a soft docking and retract when lined up to complete the docking action.

name: bluedog_saturn_s2_dockingPortPassive
title: Sarnus IMSDP-P 6.25m Passive Orbital Construction Docking Port
description: A XL sized docking port designed to dock gigantic stages for orbital construction. This passive version has a notch that the active version should line up to assist with precise alignment.

name: bluedog_Geiger
title: Radek-716 Geiger Counter
description: Radiation occurs in trace amounts all over Kerbin, but our scientists think that it is far more pervasive outside our atmosphere. This device measures the incoming ionizing radiation and gives us an idea of how irradiated space might be. Oh, sorry, we didn't mean to scare you. Don't worry. We're sure it's harmless.

name: bluedog_IRspec
title: AIL-CH Infra-red Spectrometer
description: This instrument can be used to measure the infra-red reflections coming off a planet's surface. Certain IR bands are released from specific chemical processes, which lets scientists infer what sort of activity is occurring on a body.

name: bluedog_IonSensor
title: SWD-CCCP Hemispherical Ion Trap
description: This hemispherical ion trap allows us to sense charged particles that pass through it. That will allow us to measure the solar wind around the system.

name: bluedog_MassSpec
title: COS-B3N3T Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer
description: Kerbals have always wondered the eternal question: If I take off my helmet outside the ship, will I be able to breathe? The answer lies here.

name: bluedog_Micrometeorite
title: P1NG-0WW Micrometeoroid Detector
description: Our scientists think space might not be as empty as we once thought. This device contains three plates for measuring the impacts of 'micrometeoroids', the little pieces of debris and particles that travel through open vacuum at thousands of meters per second. Measuring the number of impacts gives us an idea of how dangerous an area of space may be for our ships.

name: bluedog_MiniGoo
title: Micro Goo™ Radiometer
description: Houses a Micro Goo™ sample and exposes it to different types of radiation. Also extremely fragile! Own a brand name goo sample today!

name: bluedog_cameraLowTech
title: MV-4 "Zufar" Film Camera
description: While taking measurements with instruments is all well and good, it is also important to get an idea of what space actually looks like. To that end, we've provided this film camera in a space-friendly casing. The film has to be returned to us in order for it to be developed, so make sure the unit is recovered if you want results.

name: bluedog_cameraMidTech
title: Codac LO-2180 "Eastkan" Film Camera
description: Film cameras are limited in that the film must be returned to Kerbin in order to be developed. In order to get a better idea of what lies further out in space, we have developed this advanced film camera in conjunction with our partner Codac. After exposing the film, it is developed automatically and then transmitted in strips using a primitive photoscanner. A significant amount of detail is lost in this process, so the images aren't as valuable as actually returning the film. The film is stored after development, and can be still be examined if it happens to be returned.

name: bluedog_hydrometer
title: WDU-W3T Surface Hydrometer
description: This instrument measures a planet's atmosphere for moisture, one of the most important substances known to Kerbalkind, and a building block of life as we know it. Also useful for washing the ship before takeoff.

name: bluedog_upgrade_logo
title: BDB Upgrade Logo
description: Nothing to see here citizen. Move along.

name: bluedog_GooLab_Antenna
title: MONK-E-WHBF Whip Antenna
description: A simple extending whip antenna, designed to be mounted on the MONK-E Goo Laboratory.

name: bluedog_GooLab_Module
title: MONK-E-MGL Orbital Goo Laboratory
description: What is the mystery goo? How did it get here? What does it want? Those questions, and many more, will be answered here: The MONK-E Orbital Goo Laboratory. Capable of supporting, and studying, two goo "samples" for long durations in orbit - both crew tended, or as a station module - and then safely packaging them for return home. They'll love it, we're sure.

name: bluedog_GooLab_Solar
title: MONK-E-PPS Photovoltaic Power Supply
description: Cheap, primitive solar panel with a simple deployment mechanism. Folds up for storage in fairings, but doesn't track the sun.

name: bluedog_MORL_PBG
title: M-PBG15 Plutonium Brayton-cycle Generator
description: Similar to an RTG, the Plutonium Brayton-cycle generator does not use a reactor, just a lump of very radioactive and hot Plutonium-238. However, heat is converted to electricity using the far more efficient (albeit more complex) Brayton cycle.

name: bluedog_MORL_PBGrack
title: Hokulani PR-11 Equipment Rack
description: A handy equipment rack for 4.25m space stations.

name: bluedog_MORL_aeroCone
title: Hokulani OLM-NC25 Aerodynamic Nose Fairing
description: A 2.5m hollow nose cone with built in decoupler.

name: bluedog_MORL_antenna
title: Hokulani OLM-HGD15 High Gain Antenna
description: High speed communications system for space stations.

name: bluedog_MORL_resistojet_RCS
title: MORL-RJE12 Resistojet Electric RCS Unit
description: Resistojets heat up the propellant using an electric current passed through a resistive heating element. Engineers deny it was inspired by the tea kettle in the lab. This Resistojet based RCS block therefore requires EC to function but in return achieves very high Isp. Available with MonoPropellant and Liquid Hydrogen variants.

name: bluedog_MORL_solar
title: Hokulani-OLM-SP12 Solar Panel Wing
description: Large tracking solar panel designed for a 4.25m profile.

name: bluedog_MORL_workshop
title: Hokulani-OLM Laboratory
description: A compact all in one space station module. Includes multiple docking options. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: DO NOT MAKE THIS PART THE ROOT OF YOUR CRAFT. If this part is root, the docking port covers will not function properly. The top docking port is recommended as the root part.</color>

name: bluedog_Skylab_ACS
title: Hokulani-ACT RCS Unit
description: Reaction control thruster block for the Hokulani orbital workshop, place them on the front and back of the OWS radiator mount, on the white corrugated section at the bottom.

name: bluedog_Skylab_ATM_antenna
title: Kane-OCO-CA Command Antenna
description: Small command antenna designed to be attached to the bottom of the Kane OCO core.

name: bluedog_Skylab_ATM_core
title: Kane-OCO Telescope Mount
description: The Kane telescope mount forms the core of the Hokulani space station's solar science observatory. Place the experiment unit on top. Although designed to be deployed via a robotic truss, it includes hardware for autonomous control, so it can be properly docked to a station remotely or used as a probe core.

name: bluedog_Skylab_ATM_experiments
title: Kane-OCO Telescope Mount Experiment BLock
description: This suite of advanced instruments is used to observe the activity of Kerbol at a level of detail unattainable by ground based telescopes.

name: bluedog_Skylab_ATM_solar
title: Kane-OCO-ASP Solar Panel
description: Extending solar panels for the Kane-OCO Telescope Mount. Attach to the railing on the bottom of the telescope experiment unit 45 degrees off primary axes.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_MWspec
title: Hokulani-EOSS Microwave Spectrometer
description: An extending with a microwave spectrometer on the end.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_aftMDA
title: Hokulani-RMPS Aft Docking Adapter
description: This useful module adds multiple docking nodes, extra consumables and an airlock to the rear of the Hokulani station. The airlock can be swapped out for a larger docking node.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_dishSmall
title: Hokulani-EOSS-DS1 Communication Dish
description: A small backup comm dish for space stations.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_interstageModule
title: Hokulani-EOSS-IM Interstage Station Module
description: Built by combining the interstage and oxidizer tank from the Sarnus SIVB stage, this unusual station features room for various experiments, an airlock, a docking port (with aero cover), and an unpressurized cargo bay that opens outward. <#ef7b06>AUTHOR'S NOTE: Toggle the docking port cover in the VAB in order to place a Kane-11-DDM6 0.625m Passive Docking Port. The cover can be manually jettisoned in flight.</color>

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_massSpec
title: Hokulani-EOSS-MS5 Mass Spectrometer
description: An aerodynamically shielded doployable mass spectrometer isntrument.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_mulitSpec
title: Hokulani-EOSS-MSSB Multispectral Sensor
description: An extending boom with a multispectral sensor.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_paraAntenna
title: Hokulani-EOSS-HG15 High Gain Antenna
description: High speed communications system for large spacecraft.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_radar
title: Hokulani-EOSS-MMR Radar Antenna
description: A deployable high resolution mapping radar system for large space stations and spacecraft.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_rolloutSolar
title: Hokulani-eROSA Experimental Rollout Solar Array
description: An experimental rollout solar array. Lighter, smaller and more powerful than regular panels!

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_rolloutSolar_tracking
title: Hokulani-eROSA Experimental Rollout Solar Array (Tracking)
description: An experimental rollout solar array. Lighter, smaller and more powerful than regular panels! This version is capable of sun tracking

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_scatterometer
title: Hokulani-EOSS-SCT14 Radar Scatterometer
description: This radar scatterometer instrument can measure weather patterns on planets below.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_solarPanel
title: Hokulani-EOSS Solar Wing
description: Folding solar arrays designed to fit inside of the Hokulani EOSS interstage station module. Deploy one after the other to avoid clipping.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_solarPanel_90
title: Hokulani-EOSS Solar Wing 90 Deg
description: Variant of the Hokulani EOSS interstage Solar Wings designed to fold out at a 90 degree angle for more versatility.

name: bluedog_Skylab_EOSS_telescope
title: Hokluani-EOSS "Planetwave" Multi Telescope System
description: Powerful multi telescope system with direct crew access to instruments at the back. Features geperal purpose, x-ray and solar instruments.

name: bluedog_Skylab_IRspec
title: Hokulani HS-191 Infra-red Spectrometer
description: This instrument can be used to measure the infra-red reflections coming off a planet's surface. Certain IR bands are released from specific chemical processes, which lets scientists infer what sort of activity is occurring on a body.

name: bluedog_Skylab_LB_radiometer
title: Hokulani HS-194 L-Band Radiometer
description: The L-band microwave radiometer is a remote sensing instrument that can be used to monitor soil moisture.

name: bluedog_Skylab_PMA
title: Hokulani-AMP Pressurized Mating Adapter
description: A pressurized structural extension that gives more clearance for docking spacecraft.

name: bluedog_Skylab_RAP
title: Hokulani-RAP Radial Attachment Point
description: An expansion node for the Hokulani Multiple Docking Adapter. Can be used to add more docking points or other structural connections to a station.

name: bluedog_Skylab_RadiatorMount
title: Hokulani-RMPS Radiator Unit
description: Radiator that replaces the engine mount on the Hokulani dry workshop. Includes monopropellant storage for the station's RCS thrusters.

name: bluedog_Skylab_TRS_camera
title: Hokulani PCS Monitoring TV Camera
description: A compact camera with a convenient built in light.

name: bluedog_Skylab_TRS_lamp
title: Hokulani QLS Illumination Unit
description: Compact light to assist with docking.

name: bluedog_Skylab_TRS_microDocking_cone
title: Hokulani MDS-C 0.3125m Passive Docking Mechanism
description: Miniature probe-and-drogue docking system. This is the passive port, designed to catch the active port's probe.

name: bluedog_Skylab_TRS_microDocking_probe
title: Hokulani MDS-P 0.3125m Passive Docking Mechanism
description: Miniature probe-and-drogue docking system. This is the active port, Approach the target with the probe extended. Once soft docking is achieved and the vessels properly aligned, retract the probe to hard dock and establish a solid connection.

name: bluedog_Skylab_TRS_omniAntenna
title: Hokulani CRRS-A12 Omni Antenna
description: Compact and robust antenna for short range communication.

name: bluedog_Skylab_TRS_probeCore
title: Hokulani H-RSS "Sisyphus" Robotic Retreival System Core
description: The Sisyphus probe core is the basis of a modular space tug system. Designed originally to boost the orbit of space stations, it can function as a standalone probe core with six axis attitude control and can operate with up to four H-RRP2 Propulsion Kits (or without them at all).

name: bluedog_Skylab_TRS_propulsionKit
title: Hokulani H-RRP4 Propulsion Kit
description: Self contained strap on propulsion kit with large propellant tanks and 8 thrusters.

name: bluedog_Skylab_TRS_solarPanel
title: Hokulani RRS-S10 Solar Panel
description: A small fixed solar panel for the Hokulani Robotic Retrieval System. Comes with variants that can be mounted snugly on sharp corners or on a flat surface.

name: bluedog_Skylab_VFB_ESM
title: Hokulani-EFB-ESM Planetary Flyby Mission Module
description: A modified Sarnus LAM yielded this mission module, packed with useful equipment for a basic, simple interplanetary flyby. Attachment works the same as the other LAMs - attach the hidden node on the Kane Engine Plate to the top, and then attach four SLAMs to the nodes on the sides. A docking port and a Hokulani EFB-HA12 High Gain Antenna should go on top. An unpressurized cargo bay is built into the bottom of the module to carry the AAT 25 "Stellartron" telescope EFB-R4XH Multi Probe Dispenser (or indeed anything else you wish to store there instead).

name: bluedog_Skylab_VFB_antenna
title: Hokulani EFB-HA12 High Gain Antenna
description: High speed communications system for transmitting data across interplanetary distances.

name: bluedog_Skylab_VFB_boom
title: Hokulani EFB-MXB Multi-experiment Science Boom
description: An extending boom with both a magnetometer and mass spectrometer for your crewed interplanetary science needs.

name: bluedog_Skylab_VFB_entryProbe
title: Hokulani EFB-R4 Atmoshperic Entry Probe
description: A simple self contained probe with all the requirements for planetary atmospheric science. Includes a heatshield, antennas, rcs, and a small course correction solid motor. If you're lucky it might even survive impact with the surface! Features hydrometer and atmosphere analysis experiments.

name: bluedog_Skylab_VFB_lightweightWetWorkshop
title: Hokulani-EFB-WS Interplanetary Wet Workshop
description: A more advanced version of the wet workshop Hokulani-OWS. Better equipped for interplanetary flyby missions. After launch, switch from fuel to lab before boarding scientists. A less capable version of the full Hokulani lab with room for 2 scientists, the wet workshop can be sent to higher orbits or even to other bodies. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: DO NOT MAKE THIS PART THE ROOT OF YOUR CRAFT. If this part is root, the sunshield will not function properly.</color>

name: bluedog_Skylab_VFB_probeDispenser
title: Hokulani EFB-R4XH Multi Probe Dispenser
description: A cosy little box to hold up to four atmospheric entry probes. Use a set of any 0.3125m decouplers inside to attach the probes.

name: bluedog_Skylab_VFB_solarPanel
title: Hokulani-EFB-R12 Solar Panel
description: These hardy solar panels were designed for interplanetary flybys and provide both power and micrometeorite protection! The panels are deployable and though they do not track, they can be individually oriented to the sun via a deploy limit in the part action window. Place 12 radially around the Hokulani-LWWS Light Wet Workshop underneath the aero shield.

name: bluedog_Skylab_VFB_telescope
title: Hokulani AAT 27 "Stellartron" telescope
description: Large fixed mount telescope system designed for a crewed planetary flyby mission though it surely has other applications. Features multiple experiment instruments.

name: bluedog_Skylab_WetWorkshop
title: Hokulani-WWS Wet Workshop
description: A stripped down lighter version of the Hokulani Wet Workshop designed for planetary flybys and other demanding mass sensitive missions. Seats a crew of 4. After launch, switch from fuel to lab before boarding scientists. A wide jettisonable aero shield is provided to protect 12 EFB-R12 Solar Panels during ascent; make sure to jettison the aero shield during or after ascent. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: DO NOT MAKE THIS PART THE ROOT OF YOUR CRAFT. If this part is root, the sunshield will not function properly.</color>

name: bluedog_Skylab_Workshop
title: Hokulani-OWS Orbital Workshop
description: Built from a modified Sarnus-SIVB-11300 fuel tank, this massive volume is capable of housing up to 6 Kerbals in comfort, while also providing them all the tools they need to work effectively and conduct science in space.  With such luxurious amenities as a shower and a treadmill, crews will love to step into their new home-away-from-home. <#ef7b06> AUTHOR'S NOTE: DO NOT MAKE THIS PART THE ROOT OF YOUR CRAFT. If this part is root, the sunshield will not function properly.</color>

name: bluedog_Skylab_airlockModule
title: Hokulani-ALM Airlock Module
description: This multipurpose part serves as a 4.25m-1.875m adapter module, fairing base, life support and service compartment, crew tube, and an airlock all in one! Just be sure your Kerbals watch their heads on their way out. The hatch might have a familiar look to it...

name: bluedog_Skylab_discone_antenna
title: Hokulani-DCA Discone Antenna
description: A small omni antenna on a very long rod, in case you need to take your space station pole vaulting.

name: bluedog_Skylab_dockingNodeAdapter
title: Hokulani-MDX Multiple Docking Node Extension
description: A crew passable adapter that can expand the number and type of docking ports your space station can use. Can also be detached in an emergency as a free flying lifeboat. If you're very desperate!

name: bluedog_Skylab_evaLight
title: Hokulani EVA Lightbulb
description: Cheap compact light designed to be placed externally on space stations to assist in spacewalking activities.

name: bluedog_Skylab_multiSpectralScanner
title: Hokulani HS-192 Multispectral Scanner
description: This advanced instrument is capable of remote sensing resources in 13 different bands! Real bang for your buck.

name: bluedog_Skylab_multipleDockingAdapter
title: Hokulani-MDA Multiple Docking Adapter
description: A crew passable structural adapter with points for 2 docking ports. More can be added via radial docking adapters if desired.

name: bluedog_Skylab_parasol
title: Hokulani-UB22 "Brolly" Sun Shield
description: A deployable sunshield for emergency cooling! Attach to the Hokulani zenith scientific airlock (on EVA if necessary) and shield your precious station from the baleful glare of Kerbol.

name: bluedog_Skylab_powerModuleSolar
title: Hokulani-PXXL Power Tower Solar Panel
description: Enormous high tech solar panels to support your space station exppansion needs.

name: bluedog_Skylab_powerModuleSolar_double
title: Hokulani-PXXL2 Power Tower Solar Panel Double
description: Enormous high tech solar panels to support your space station exppansion needs. Now with twice the power output!

name: bluedog_Skylab_powerModule_berthing_active
title: Hokulani PMBP-A Power Module Berthing Port (Active)
description: Common Androgynous Docking System, passive version intended to mate with active counterparts. Useful for permanent fixtures that won't have to form the active docking partner, such as berthing ports on station modules.

name: bluedog_Skylab_powerModule_berthing_passive
title: Hokulani PMBP-P Power Module Berthing Port (Passive)
description: A simplistic berthing port intended only to allow power and data transfer.

name: bluedog_Skylab_powerModule_core
title: Kane-PMTC Power Module Core
description: If you wanted to build some kind of "tower of power", this component can act as the foundation. Features a probe core, reaction wheels and large batteries for power regulation. An interface for a solar support structure is provided above to attach large deployable solar panels. Radial attach points are also available if you prefer to berth this to a station using a robotic arm. This core was built using left overs from a famous space telescope.

name: bluedog_Skylab_radarAltimeter
title: Hokulani HS-193 Radar Altimeter
description: This radar altimeter dish can be used to map the surface height of the body below. It can also collect radar spectrometry data to determine surface-level wind speeds.

name: bluedog_Skylab_solar_radio_burst_antenna
title: Hokulani Solar Radio Noise Burst Antenna
description: This might look like a small comms dish but its actually designed to listen to stellar radio burst noise.

name: bluedog_Skylab_wetWorkshop_airlockMDA
title: Hokulani-SMDA Combo Airlock & Docking Adapter
description: A lighter combination airlock and docking adapter designed to fit inside the Sarnus-SIVB-LAM adapter. Well suited for wet workshop stations.

name: bluedog_Spacelab_airlockModule
title: Hokulani-EALM Expansion Airlock Module
description: A small expansion module for the Hokulani OWS that includes an external airlock, meaning EVAs can be carried out without disrupting operations in the rest of the station.

name: bluedog_Spacelab_handrail
title: Hokulani HTHR-1 Handrail
description: A high quality handrail imported from Habtech industries. Attach radially for a convenient gripping point for EVAs.

name: bluedog_skylab_dockingTarget
title: Hokulani HDT-1 Visual Docking Target
description: A small device used as a visual alignment guide for docking. This is a standalone model made from spares for use with docking ports of your choice.

name: bluedog_skylab_powerModule_radiator
title: Hokulani PMBP-RDT Radiator (Tracking)
description: A radially attachable deployable radiator. This version tracks to point edgewise to the sun for better cooling. Available in single and double sizes.

name: bluedog_skylab_powerModule_radiator_fixed
title: Hokulani PMBP-RDT Radiator (Fixed)
description: A radially attachable deployable radiator. This version does not feature solar tracking to allow for more restrictive placement but is less efficient as a result. Available in single and double sizes.

name: bluedog_skylab_powerModule_support
title: Hokulani MSPT Solar Support Structure
description: A structural adapter with useful attach nodes for solar panels and radiators.

name: bluedog_skylab_solarWing
title: Hokulani-PPA Solar Panel Wing
description: Large, poorly shielded solar panels for providing power to your orbital workshops. Place radially, 30 degrees off center. The panels will automatically mirror to face the correct direction. Be careful not to lose them on the way up!

name: bluedog_skylab_structuralAdapter
title: Hokulani MSA 1.875m Structural Adapter
description: A simple structural adapter built from left over Hokulani parts to transition from 1.875m to smaller diameters.

name: bluedog_spacelab_SciencePallet
title: Hokulani HSP-11 Science Pallet
